./.title: Introduction
./.body:
Backlog.md User Manual
A Markdown-native task and kanban visualization tool

Backlog.md turns any Git repository directory into a self-contained project board. Every task is a standalone Markdown file, 100% offline and private, with no internet connection required.
Core Features

Markdown-native: all data is stored as .md files, Git-friendly
AI-Ready: supports Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Kiro, Cursor, and other AI assistants
Dual-mode interface: terminal TUI board + modern Web browser interface
Rich-text paste: paste from Word or Google Docs as Markdown, with .docx file upload support
Dates & planning: tasks and milestones support dueDate, plannedStart, and plannedEnd; board cards show planning windows and overdue highlights in real time
Project health: four dimensions—due, overdue, stale, and blocked—unified in the Web statistics page and the CLI overview command
Wiki knowledge base: LLM-maintained incremental knowledge base, human-readable and editable; browser supports file-tree navigation, in-place editing, labels, and live sync; built-in skill installable to Claude/Codex
Task graph: knowledge graph of task relationships with Cypher queries (CLI backlog graph and MCP graph tools) and Web visualization; default RyuGraph WASM backend with zero native dependencies
Office document preview: preview .docx / .pdf / .pptx / .xlsx documents in-app; Word and Excel support editing and write-back to source files; unsupported formats show a conversion hint
Live SQL query blocks: embed sqlite-query / duckdb-query / mdb-query fenced blocks in documents; Web reading view renders read-only live query results (SQLite / DuckDB / Access, 500-row limit) with in-place editing
Chart blocks: draw flowcharts and data charts with mermaid / echarts fenced blocks; ECharts covers all built-in series and follows light/dark themes; query results can feed charts directly, or reference named query blocks via fromQuery
Quick notes (Memos): lightweight capture inbox under backlog/memos/; terminal / Web / MCP / search share the same storage; entity IDs and wikilink automatically connect to the knowledge web
Cross-platform: macOS, Linux, Windows

Two Usage Paths

MCP spec-driven (recommended): AI agents manage tasks directly through the MCP protocol, no manual commands needed
Manual CLI mode: users operate tasks, boards, and documents through terminal commands

Installation
npm i -g @kuwork/backlog.md

Other installation options:

bun add -g @kuwork/backlog.md
brew install backlog-md (upstream formula)
nix run github:MrLesk/Backlog.md (upstream flake)

Quick Start
# Initialize a project
backlog init my-project

# Create a task
backlog task create "Implement user login"

# View the TUI board
backlog board

# Start the Web interface
backlog browser


This manual covers the complete guide from basic installation to advanced AI integration.
Related Concepts

Product Overview — Backlog.md core positioning and feature overview
Installation & Initialization — install methods and project initialization steps
AI Integration Setup — AI integration configuration and workflow

00-快速开始/00-产品概述.html.title: Product Overview
00-快速开始/00-产品概述.html.body:
Product Overview
Backlog.md is a Markdown-native task and kanban visualization CLI tool that also runs as an MCP server for AI coding assistants.
Core Positioning



Feature
Description




Markdown-native
Every task is a standalone .md file; frontmatter stores metadata; body holds the description and acceptance criteria


AI-Ready
Supports Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Kiro, Cursor, and other MCP/CLI-compatible AI assistants


100% offline & private
All data lives locally in the repository; no account or internet required


Cross-platform
macOS, Linux, and Windows



Main Features
Task Management

Task CRUD: create, edit, view, archive, and delete
Subtask support: decimal numbering (e.g., back-4.1)
Dependency management: inter-task dependencies and automatic sequence calculation
Draft system: independent draft ID space; promote to formal tasks at any time

Board & Visualization

Terminal TUI board: launch the interactive terminal board with backlog board
Web browser interface: launch the modern React interface with backlog browser, supporting rich-text paste and Word document upload
Board export: export as Markdown tables or embed in README

Search

Fuse.js-based fuzzy search across tasks, documents, and decisions
Unified search experience in CLI, TUI, and Web
Multi-dimensional filtering by status, priority, labels, and more

AI Integration

MCP protocol: AI agents invoke Backlog.md tools directly
CLI instructions: generate agent instruction files that guide AI usage of commands
Wiki Skill installation: backlog wiki install deploys the built-in knowledge-base skill to Claude/Codex
Spec-driven workflow: describe an idea → AI breaks it into tasks → implement one by one

Wiki Knowledge Base

LLM-maintained incremental knowledge base: AI agents read tasks/docs/decisions source files and compile them into a structured wiki; human-readable and editable
Browse the backlog/wiki/ file tree directly in the browser with a collapsible sidebar
In-place editing: title, body, and labels can be changed; saving automatically updates frontmatter
File management: create files/folders, rename, and empty folders remain visible
Live sync: multi-tab/WebSocket instant synchronization of file changes
AI skill support: backlog wiki install one-click deployment to Claude/Codex

Task Comments

Append discussion and review records to tasks; supports Markdown body and optional author
CLI: backlog task edit  --comment "content" --comment-author @name
MCP: task_edit commentsAppend and commentAuthor fields
Web UI: task detail modal shows comments read-only in preview mode; edit mode can append new comments
Comment text participates in search; backlog search can find tasks containing relevant comments

Dates & Planning

Task date fields: optional dueDate, plannedStart, and plannedEnd
Milestone dates: set time ranges and deadlines for milestones
Board date indicators: TaskCard shows planning windows and overdue highlights
Web UI auto-fill: setting dueDate automatically suggests plannedStart / plannedEnd

Documents & Decisions

Document management: supports sub-folder grouping
Decision records (ADR): standard architecture-decision format with status transitions
Milestones: task assignment, completion detection, and archiving

Technology Stack

Runtime: Bun + TypeScript 5
CLI: Commander.js + Clack interactive wizard
TUI: bblessed terminal interface
Web UI: React + Tailwind CSS v4
Search: Fuse.js fuzzy matching
Build output: single-file executable binary with embedded Web assets

Distribution Channels

npm: @kuwork/backlog.md
Homebrew: backlog-md (upstream formula)
Nix: nix run github:MrLesk/Backlog.md (upstream flake)
GitHub Releases: platform binaries at kuwork/Backlog.md

Related Concepts

User Manual Cover — cover and quick entry points
Installation & Initialization — install methods and project initialization
AI Integration Setup — AI integration configuration and workflow

00-快速开始/01-安装与初始化.html.title: Installation & Initialization
00-快速开始/01-安装与初始化.html.body:
Installation & Initialization
Installation
Via npm (recommended)
npm i -g @kuwork/backlog.md

Via Bun
bun add -g @kuwork/backlog.md

Via Homebrew (macOS / Linux)
The Homebrew formula currently points to the upstream repository:
brew install backlog-md

Via Nix
The Nix flake currently points to the upstream repository:
nix run github:MrLesk/Backlog.md

GitHub Releases
Visit the Releases page to download the binary for your platform.

Apple Silicon (M1/M2) note: if you run the x64 version of Node or Bun through Rosetta, the CLI launcher detects the host architecture and Rosetta state and resolves the matching arm64 platform package; if the installed package does not match the CPU architecture, it prints clear architecture info and a reinstall command to avoid illegal hardware instruction errors. If you encounter binary resolution issues, reinstall using a native arm64 runtime first.

Initialize a Project
Enter the root of your Git repository and run:
backlog init [project-name]

The interactive wizard guides you through:

Project name
Default task status list
Label definitions
AI integration mode choice (MCP / CLI instructions / skip)


When using a custom task ID prefix (--task-prefix), only letters are allowed, and doc and decision are reserved names (used by documents and decisions); all entry points reject them.

File-system-only Project Without Git
backlog init --no-git

Use this for task management in non-code projects.
Initialize in Another Directory (BACKLOG_CWD)
backlog init does not accept a --cwd command-line flag (only mcp start accepts --cwd). It supports two ways to specify the target directory: switch the shell working directory before running, or pin the directory with the BACKLOG_CWD environment variable (which takes precedence over process.cwd(), falling back to the current working directory).
# Option 1: switch to the target repo first (most straightforward)
cd /path/to/repo && backlog init my-project

# Option 2: use an environment variable in CI/scripts (directory must already exist)
BACKLOG_CWD=/path/to/repo backlog init my-project

BACKLOG_CWD requires the directory to already exist; otherwise it fails fast with Invalid directory from BACKLOG_CWD and exits. init uses the unified runtime cwd resolution (requireRuntimeCwd), so BACKLOG_CWD and all subsequent commands see the same target directory—init no longer only recognizes the process current directory. The TUI and Web server follow the same resolution rule.
Non-interactive Initialization (CI / Scripts)
--defaults skips all interactive prompts and uses default values, which is ideal for CI and scripts; other parameters are supplied on the command line as needed:
# All defaults, one-shot initialization
backlog init "My Project" --defaults

# Specify AI integration mode (cli / mcp / none, default cli)
backlog init "My Project" --defaults --integration-mode cli

# Specify agent instruction files to generate (comma-separated; cursor writes AGENTS.md; none skips)
backlog init "My Project" --defaults --agent-instructions agents,claude

Common non-interactive parameters:



Parameter
Description




--defaults
Use defaults for all prompts


`--integration-mode 
mcp\
none>`
AI integration mode (default cli; CLI instructions recommended)


--agent-instructions 
Agent instruction files to generate: claude / agents / gemini / copilot / cursor (writes AGENTS.md) / none


--backlog-dir 
Backlog directory: backlog / .backlog / custom relative path


--task-prefix 
Task ID prefix (letters only, default task; draft, doc, decision are reserved)


`--config-location 
root>`
Where to store the configuration file


--no-git
Do not integrate Git


--web-port 
Web UI default port (default 6420)


--default-editor 
Default editor command



Directory Structure After Initialization
backlog/
├── tasks/          # Task files
├── docs/           # Documents
├── decisions/      # Decision records
├── drafts/         # Drafts
├── milestones/     # Milestones
├── archive/        # Archived items
├── completed/      # Completed tasks
├── assets/         # Attachments
├── config.yml      # Project configuration
└── wiki/           # Knowledge base (optional)
Verify Installation
backlog --version

Running without subcommands shows the welcome screen and detects whether the current directory is initialized:
backlog

Upgrading Backlog.md
Upgrade paths mirror installation paths:
npm / Bun: update the global package to the latest version (package name @kuwork/backlog.md)
npm update -g @kuwork/backlog.md
# or force a fresh install of the latest version
npm i -g @kuwork/backlog.md@latest

Homebrew (upstream formula):
brew upgrade backlog-md

GitHub Releases binary: download the new release from Releases and replace the old binary.
After upgrading, it is recommended to:

Run backlog --version to confirm the new version is active.
Re-run backlog init in the project root (no arguments needed)—it will create any missing directories introduced by the new version (e.g., memos/, docs/, etc., via ensureBacklogStructure()) without overwriting existing configuration or data.

Configuration Management
After initialization, adjust settings through the advanced configuration wizard:
backlog config

Configurable items include:

Task ID prefix
Default status list
Definition of Done default checklist
Default editor
Web UI port and auto-open browser
Git integration options (auto-commit, bypass hooks, etc.)

Related Concepts

Product Overview — Backlog.md core positioning and feature overview
AI Integration Setup — AI integration configuration after initialization
Configuration Management — adjusting configuration after initialization

00-快速开始/02-AI集成设置.html.title: AI Integration Setup
00-快速开始/02-AI集成设置.html.body:
AI Integration Setup
Backlog.md supports two AI integration modes: MCP protocol (recommended) and CLI instruction files.
MCP Protocol (recommended)
MCP (Model Context Protocol) allows AI agents to invoke Backlog.md tools directly, without users typing CLI commands manually.
Claude Code
claude mcp add backlog --scope user -- backlog mcp start

OpenAI Codex
codex mcp add backlog -- backlog mcp start


Codex uses -- as the stdio command separator.

Google Gemini CLI
gemini mcp add backlog -s user backlog mcp start

Kiro
kiro-cli mcp add --scope global --name backlog --command backlog --args mcp,start

Cursor
Manually configure mcpServers and add:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "backlog": {
      "command": "backlog",
      "args": ["mcp", "start"]
    }
  }
}


CLI instruction mode: Cursor also reads the project root AGENTS.md as a general agent instruction file. When running backlog init or backlog agents --update-instructions, Cursor instructions are written to AGENTS.md; no separate .cursorrules file is generated.

CLI Instruction Files
For AI tools that do not support MCP, Backlog.md can generate agent instruction files that guide the AI on how to use backlog commands.
Generate Instruction Files
Choose CLI instruction mode during backlog init, or run later:
backlog agents --update-instructions

This generates:

CLAUDE.md — Claude Code / Claude Desktop
AGENTS.md — generic agent instructions (Cursor also reads this file)
GEMINI.md — Gemini CLI
.github/copilot-instructions.md — GitHub Copilot


Re-running backlog init or backlog agents --update-instructions preserves existing AGENTS.md content; Backlog.md only updates its marked blocks.

Instruction File Contents
The files include workflow guides, task creation conventions, acceptance-criteria formats, and other rules so the AI knows how to:

Create tasks with acceptance criteria
Use backlog commands to manage the task lifecycle
Follow project conventions (branch naming, commit format, etc.)

Integration Mode Comparison



Mode
Suitable Tools
Pros
Cons




MCP
Claude, Codex, Gemini, Kiro, Cursor
AI invokes tools directly; more reliable and safer
Requires the tool to support the MCP protocol


CLI instructions
GitHub Copilot, Cursor, others
Good compatibility; no special protocol required
AI must parse shell output; slightly lower reliability



Recommended AI Workflow
Step 1: Describe the Idea
Tell the AI agent what you want to build, and let it break the work into small tasks, each with a clear description and acceptance criteria.
Step 2: One Task at a Time
Handle one task per agent session, one task per PR. Make sure each task is small enough to complete within a single conversation.
Step 3: Write a Plan Before Coding
Before implementation, ask the agent to study the codebase and write an implementation plan in the task.
Step 4: Implement and Verify
Have the agent implement the task. After completion, review the code, run tests, and check lint to verify the result.
Restart Loop When Unsatisfied
Clear the plan/notes/final summary, refine the task description and acceptance criteria, and rerun in a new session.

10-任务管理/00-任务生命周期.html.title: Task Lifecycle
10-任务管理/00-任务生命周期.html.body:
Task Lifecycle
In Backlog.md, every task is a standalone Markdown file that goes through a complete status flow from idea to final archive.
Status Flow
The full flow from creation to completion is:
Draft → To Do → In Progress → Done → Archived / Completed



Status
Description




Draft
Draft state uses an independent ID space (e.g., draft-1) and does not consume formal task numbers


To Do
Default status for newly created tasks, waiting to start


In Progress
Marked manually when work starts, or updated automatically by an AI agent


Done
Work is complete; the task still remains in backlog/tasks/


Archived
After running backlog task archive, moved to backlog/archive/tasks/; soft delete


Completed
After running backlog cleanup, Done tasks are moved to backlog/completed/



State Machine
The table above shows the default status list. The actual status list for a project is declared in backlog/config.yml under statuses, and supports a semantic object form:



Field
Description




name
Status name (column label)


category
One of six categories: initial / active / wip / blocked / done / dropped, replacing the old "last position is terminal" convention


exit
Terminal-state exit action (e.g., archive)


display
When false, the board hides this column (tasks in it are hidden too)


next
Array of transition edges; each edge can declare when / requires / evidence / ai permissions



Key points:

Newly initialized projects use the built-in seven-column default state machine (To Do → Planning → Plan Review → In Progress → In Review → Done, plus the archival terminal state Dropped). The CLI config command only has get/set/list subcommands; to restore the default state machine, click the Default button in the Web settings state-machine editor—the button only loads the default machine into the editor, and you still need to save for it to take effect
The default machine includes finalization gates: In Progress → In Review requires the task file to be finalized per task-finalization, and In Review → Done requires acceptance per task-finalization. New projects have this out of the box, no manual configuration needed
The state machine is declarative, not enforced: out-of-bounds transitions do not error, but the CLI/MCP guide (backlog instructions overview) renders the full state table, categories, transition edges, and a "stop for human review" checklist, so AI agents work according to the declared machine
Legacy string-array configurations remain compatible; the settings page provides a visual state-machine editor for maintaining the object form
For full semantics, see the wiki concept page State Machine Semantics

Task File Structure
Each task file begins with YAML frontmatter for structured metadata; the body records the task description, acceptance criteria, implementation plan, and other information.
---
id: back-10
title: "Task Title"
status: "In Progress"
assignee: ["@user"]
reporter: "@user"
created_date: "2026-05-06"
updated_date: "2026-05-06"
completed_date: "2026-05-06"
labels: ["feature", "backend"]
priority: high
milestone: "M1 - CLI"
dependencies: ["back-1", "back-2"]
references: ["https://docs.example.com", "src/api.ts"]
docs: ["doc-1"]
ordinal: 1000
type: feature
dueDate: "2026-05-20"
plannedStart: "2026-05-10"
plannedEnd: "2026-05-18"
actual_start: "2026-05-10 09:00"
actual_end: "2026-05-15 18:30"
parentTaskId: "back-4"
---

Core Field Reference



Field
Description
Example




id
Unique task identifier; custom prefix supported
back-10, proj-42


title
Task title, single-line text
"Implement user login"


status
Current status; must be in the project's config.statuses list
"To Do", "In Progress"


assignee
List of assignees in @username format
["@alice", "@bob"]


reporter
Creator
"@alice"


priority
Priority; optional high, medium, low
high


milestone
ID or title of the assigned milestone
"M1 - CLI"


dependencies
List of IDs of tasks this task depends on
["back-1", "back-2"]


ordinal
Custom sort weight; smaller values appear first
1000


type
Task type, e.g. bug, feature, enhancement, docs
feature


dueDate
Due date (ISO format, date-only)
"2026-05-20"


plannedStart
Planned start date (ISO format, date-only)
"2026-05-10"


plannedEnd
Planned end date (ISO format, date-only)
"2026-05-18"


actual_start
Actual start time (UTC datetime)
"2026-05-10 09:00"


actual_end
Actual end time (UTC datetime)
"2026-05-15 18:30"


parentTaskId
Parent task ID; when present, this task is a subtask
"back-4"


labels
Label list
["backend", "api"]


references
External reference links or file paths
["src/api.ts"]


docs
Associated document IDs
["doc-5"]



Automatic Actual-Time Population
actualStart and actualEnd track when a task actually started and finished. The system auto-populates them under certain conditions:

When a task status changes from any status to In Progress, if actualStart is empty, it is set to the current datetime
When a task status changes to Done (or another terminal status), if actualEnd is empty, it is set to the current datetime
Creating a task with --status "In Progress" or --status "Done" also triggers auto-population
Auto-population only runs when the field is empty; you can manually override it at any time

Changing Status
Via CLI
# Mark as in progress
backlog task edit  --status "In Progress"

# Mark as done (sets the terminal status, usually Done)
backlog task edit  --status "Done"

# Archive the task
backlog task archive 

Via TUI Board
Run backlog board to launch the terminal board; select a task card and use arrow keys or shortcuts to move it between status columns.
Via Web UI
Run backlog browser to launch the browser interface; drag and drop task cards to the target status column in the board view.
Via AI Agent (MCP)
AI agents can directly call the update_task tool to change task status without human intervention.
Duplicate Task ID Detection and Repair
Under normal circumstances, task IDs are guaranteed unique at creation time. However, cross-branch merges, zero-padding equivalence (back-1 vs back-01), external imports, or manual edits can produce duplicate task IDs, causing tasks to silently collapse in views, search, and editing.
Use backlog doctor to detect and repair duplicate IDs:
# Preview conflicts (lists conflict groups, file paths, planned renames, references needing human review)
backlog doctor

# Confirm the fix and discard .bak backups (finalize)
backlog doctor --commit

# Roll back the fix (restore .bak backups)
backlog doctor --rollback

Repair principles: only rename task files and the id in frontmatter, preserving content; renames and frontmatter updates are atomic; ambiguous structures are fail-closed and references are not guessed; operations are reversible (.bak backups are created), and both --commit and --rollback require human confirmation.
Ordinal Changes Do Not Affect updated_date
When only adjusting task ordinals (e.g., board reordering, bulk sorting), the task updated_date is not refreshed, avoiding meaningless Git diff noise. updated_date is updated only when task content or metadata actually changes.

10-任务管理/01-创建与编辑任务.html.title: Creating & Editing Tasks
10-任务管理/01-创建与编辑任务.html.body:
Creating & Editing Tasks
Creating Tasks
Basic Creation
Run the following command and enter a title to quickly create a task:
backlog task create "Task Title"

If the current terminal supports interactive TTY and no title is provided, the creation wizard starts automatically to guide you through task details.

The output of backlog task create --help and backlog task edit --help ends with a Note pointing to backlog instructions overview. The project expects every session to start from that overview—which includes the project state-machine guidance and the --plain convention for AI-readable output—so new readers who check --help directly still see this guidance.

Full-Parameter Creation
You can set all fields at creation time via command-line options:
backlog task create "Implement user login" \
  -d "Support email and password login" \
  -a "@developer" \
  -s "To Do" \
  -l "feature" \
  --priority high \
  --ac "Users can log in with email" \
  --ac "Passwords must be at least 8 characters" \
  --plan "1. Design database table 2. Implement API 3. Write tests" \
  --notes "Refer to the existing auth module" \
  --dep "back-1" \
  --ref "https://docs.example.com/auth" \
  --doc "doc-5"

Common Options



Option
Description
Repeatable




-d, --description 
Task description
No


--desc 
Alias for --description
No


-a, --assignee 
Assignee; repeatable or comma-separated for multiple
Yes


--unassign
Explicitly clear assignees (does not fall back to defaultAssignee; mutually exclusive with -a)
No


-s, --status 
Initial status
No


-l, --labels 
Labels, comma-separated
No


--priority 
Priority: high, medium, low
No


--ac 
Append acceptance criterion (repeatable)
Yes


--acceptance-criteria 
Append acceptance criterion, alias for --ac
Yes


--dod 
Definition of Done item
Yes


--no-dod-defaults
Disable default DoD
No


--plan 
Implementation plan; supports \n newline escape
No


--notes 
Implementation notes; supports \n newline escape
No


--final-summary 
Final summary; supports \n newline escape
No


--ordinal 
Sort weight
No


-m, --milestone 
Assigned milestone
No


--draft
Create as draft
No


-p, --parent 
Parent task ID (creates a subtask)
No


--depends-on 
Dependent tasks, comma-separated
Yes


--dep 
Shorthand for --depends-on
Yes


--ref 
External reference link or file path
Yes


--doc 
Associated document
Yes


--due-date 
Due date (YYYY-MM-DD)
No


--planned-start 
Planned start date (YYYY-MM-DD)
No


--planned-end 
Planned end date (YYYY-MM-DD)
No


--actual-start 
Actual start time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM)
No


--actual-end 
Actual end time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM)
No


--modified-file 
Associated modified file
Yes


--plain
Output plain text after creation
No



Newlines in Descriptions
--description and --desc support cross-platform consistent newline input:
# Insert a newline in the description
backlog task create "Title" --desc "First line\nSecond line"

# Editing also supports it
backlog task edit back-10 --desc "Fixes:\n1. Fix A\n2. Fix B"


On Windows, typing \n produces a newline (the CLI internally simulates a bash double-quote escape layer and processes it uniformly)
To input a literal \n rather than a newline, enter \\\\n on Windows and \\n on non-Windows
This escape only handles \n (newline) and \\ (literal backslash); other sequences such as \t are preserved as-is
--plan, --notes, and --final-summary support the same cross-platform newline escape


Avoid bash ANSI-C quoting: do not wrap multi-line values in $'...'. Bash $'...' parses \n into a real newline before the CLI sees the argument, causing the echoed command to break across lines and the CLI to receive only the first line. Use ordinary double quotes with \n escapes instead (--plan "Step 1\nStep 2"). This rule applies to --desc, --notes, --comment, --final-summary, --append-notes, --append-final-summary, and all other multi-line fields.

Viewing Tasks
Interactive TUI View
backlog task 

Or explicitly use the view subcommand:
backlog task view 

In the TUI:

Use arrow keys or j/k to browse task details
Press E to open the task file in the system editor (the TUI suspends and resumes after you close the editor)
Press Escape or q to exit

Plain-Text Output
In non-interactive environments (scripts or AI sessions), use --plain for structured plain text:
backlog task  --plain
backlog task view  --plain

Stable JSON Output
Read commands support --json for structured, versioned JSON output, convenient for script parsing:
backlog task list --json
backlog task view back-10 --json
backlog task back-10 --json
backlog search "api" --json
backlog doc list --json

Output uses a unified envelope { schemaVersion: 1, kind: "..." }, with fields consistent with --plain, and includes date fields such as dueDate, plannedStart, plannedEnd, actualStart, actualEnd, plus acceptance-criteria progress acceptanceCriteriaCompleted / acceptanceCriteriaCount (0/0 for tasks with no acceptance criteria). Task list, task detail, and search results share the same JSON field set. --json writes only to stdout; errors go to stderr; it is mutually exclusive with --plain, and specifying both errors with a non-zero exit code.
The JSON payload also includes:

isReady: dependency readiness determination for the task; consistent with the --ready filter projection; task view --json additionally provides a readiness block (isReady / isBlocked / blockingDependencies / missingDependencies)
references / modifiedFiles: the task's references and modified-files lists (empty arrays when none), carried consistently across list, search, and detail payloads
source: defaults to null; rows from the completed corpus when expanded via --completed are marked "completed"

Continuous Watch (--json --watch)
task list --json --watch enters watch mode: it listens for task-directory changes and emits a complete JSON replacement frame on each change that is byte-for-byte consistent with a one-time --json run; it does not repeat output when nothing changes:
# Watch a single assignee's todo queue with jq
backlog task list -a "@alice" -s "To Do" --json --watch | jq --unbuffered '.tasks | length'


Options, filters, and sorting are re-evaluated on each read, so they do not drift from a one-time command
Exit via SIGINT / SIGTERM or by closing the pipe; suitable for script subscriptions and dashboard pipelines
Stops when the initiator exits: when the upstream program driving the watch (e.g., a script or IDE plugin) exits without stopping the watch, the watcher detects the initiator process disappearance and ends itself, avoiding orphan processes on quiet repositories
Low CPU at idle: when nothing happens, the per-second reconcile tick performs only a cheap file stat signature comparison (name + size + mtime + ctime, one level deep); if the signature is unchanged, it does not re-read. Idle CPU for large repositories drops from ~35% to below 1%, with unchanged output bytes and update latency

Editing Tasks
Basic Edit
backlog task edit  --title "New Title" --status "In Progress"

If no edit fields are provided and the terminal supports interactive TTY, the edit wizard starts.
Multi-ID Batch Edit
task edit accepts multiple task IDs for batch application of shared flags:
# Move multiple tasks to the same status at once
backlog task edit back-1 back-2 back-3 -s "In Progress"

# Batch append a label
backlog task edit back-1 back-2 --add-label sprint-3

Rules:

Batch-applicable flags: -s/--status, -a/--assignee, -l/--label, --add-label, --remove-label, --priority, -m/--milestone, --clear-milestone, --add-doc, --add-ref, and other shared fields
Per-task fields (--title, --desc, --plan, --notes, --comment, --ordinal, AC/DoD items, date clears, etc.) are rejected in multi-ID calls
A single task failure does not abort the batch; the command reports each failure at the end
A multi-ID call with no batch-applicable flags errors rather than opening the edit wizard

Correspondingly, the server provides a POST /api/tasks/move batch-move endpoint; multi-select drag-and-drop in the Web board submits through it in one request (see the multi-select section in Board View).
Common Edit Options



Option
Description
Repeatable




-t, --title 
Modify title
No


-d, --description 
Modify description
No


--append-description 
Append to existing description (repeatable)
Yes


--append-desc 
Alias for --append-description
Yes


-a, --assignee 
Modify assignees; repeatable or comma-separated
Yes


--unassign
Explicitly clear assignees (mutually exclusive with -a)
No


-s, --status 
Modify status
No


-l, --label 
Reset labels
No


--add-label 
Append label
No


--remove-label 
Remove label
No


--priority 
Modify priority
No


--ordinal 
Modify sort weight
No


-m, --milestone 
Modify milestone
No


--clear-milestone
Clear milestone
No


--ac 
Append acceptance criterion
Yes


--acceptance-criteria 
Set/override acceptance criteria (comma-separated or repeatable)
Yes


--clear-ac
Atomically clear all acceptance criteria (mutually exclusive with other AC changes)
No


--remove-ac 
Delete acceptance criterion at the given 1-based index
Yes


--check-ac 
Check acceptance criterion at the given index
Yes


--uncheck-ac 
Uncheck acceptance criterion at the given index
Yes


--dod 
Append DoD item
Yes


--remove-dod 
Delete DoD item at the given index
Yes


--check-dod 
Check DoD item at the given index
Yes


--uncheck-dod 
Uncheck DoD item at the given index
Yes


--plan 
Set implementation plan; supports \n newline escape
No


--append-plan 
Append to existing implementation plan (repeatable)
Yes


--notes 
Set notes (overwrite existing); supports \n newline escape
No


--append-notes 
Append notes
Yes


--final-summary 
Set final summary; supports \n newline escape
No


--append-final-summary 
Append final summary
Yes


--clear-final-summary
Clear final summary
No


--due-date 
Modify due date
No


--planned-start 
Modify planned start date
No


--planned-end 
Modify planned end date
No


--actual-start 
Modify actual start time
No


--actual-end 
Modify actual end time
No


--clear-due-date
Clear due date
No


--clear-planned-start
Clear planned start date
No


--clear-planned-end
Clear planned end date
No


--clear-actual-start
Clear actual start time
No


--clear-actual-end
Clear actual end time
No


--depends-on 
Set dependencies (overwrite existing)
Yes


--dep 
Shorthand for --depends-on
Yes


--ref 
Set references (overwrite existing)
Yes


--doc 
Set associated documents (overwrite existing)
Yes


--add-ref 
Append reference (preserves existing values)
Yes


--remove-ref 
Remove reference by value
Yes


--clear-refs
Clear all references
No


--add-doc

Yes


--remove-doc

Yes

Yes

Yes


--plain

No



Acceptance Criteria Examples
# Add a new acceptance criterion
backlog task edit back-10 --ac "New acceptance item"

# Delete the 2nd acceptance criterion
backlog task edit back-10 --remove-ac 2

# Check the 1st acceptance criterion
backlog task edit back-10 --check-ac 1

# Uncheck it
backlog task edit back-10 --uncheck-ac 1

# Atomically clear all acceptance criteria, then re-add (clear-then-add workflow)
backlog task edit back-10 --clear-ac --ac "Brand new acceptance criteria"

--clear-ac clears all acceptance criteria at once and rejects combinations with other AC change options (--ac, --remove-ac, etc.). AC and DoD editing and serialization are deterministic; repeated edits do not produce redundant or malformed checklists.
Append-Plan Example
# Append content to the existing plan
backlog task edit back-10 --append-plan "Add integration test cases"

# Replace plan first, then append multiple items
backlog task edit back-10 --plan "New plan" --append-plan "Step 1" --append-plan "Step 2"

Each append is separated from existing content by a blank line; multiple --append-plan flags are applied in command-line order. Purely whitespace values are ignored. When the implementation-plan section does not exist, the first non-empty append automatically creates it.
Notes and Summary Examples
# Append notes
backlog task edit back-10 --append-notes "New note content"

# Set final summary
backlog task edit back-10 --final-summary "Task completed, implemented..."

# Append to final summary
backlog task edit back-10 --append-final-summary "Additional note"

# Clear final summary
backlog task edit back-10 --clear-final-summary

Comment Examples
# Append a comment
backlog task edit back-10 --comment "Consider splitting the UI part into a separate PR"

# Append a comment with explicit author
backlog task edit back-10 --comment "Consider splitting the UI part into a separate PR" --comment-author @sara

# Append multiple comments at once
backlog task edit back-10 --comment "First comment" --comment "Second comment"

Comment bodies support Markdown, but a standalone --- line is reserved as a comment separator and cannot appear in the body. Comments appear in the task detail Comments section, listed in append order with index, author (if provided), and timestamp.
Differences between comments, implementation notes, and final summary:



Content Type
Purpose
Write Method




Comment
Discussion, review records, Q&A
--comment


Implementation notes
Execution progress, technical exploration
--notes / --append-notes


Final summary
PR-style completion summary
--final-summary



List Fields: Set / Add / Remove / Clear
List fields such as --ref, --doc, and --dep support four semantics, mutually exclusive within a single command:



Operation
Flags
Semantics




Set
--ref / --doc / --dep / --depends-on
Replace the entire list with the given values


Add
--add-ref / --add-doc / --add-dep / --add-depends-on
Append to existing values, preserving existing entries


Remove
--remove-ref / --remove-doc / --remove-dep
Delete the specified entry by value


Clear
--clear-refs / --clear-docs / --clear-deps
Clear the entire list



# Overwrite dependencies
backlog task edit back-10 --dep "back-3,back-4"

# Append a dependency while keeping existing ones
backlog task edit back-10 --add-dep back-5

# Remove a dependency by value
backlog task edit back-10 --remove-dep back-4

# Clear all dependencies
backlog task edit back-10 --clear-deps

Rules:

Set and add cannot be mixed (--ref and --add-ref are mutually exclusive), and clear cannot be combined with set/add/remove of the same kind; violations fail the command and leave the task file unchanged
Remove flags can be repeated or comma-separated; empty values are rejected
Empty set values are rejected: backlog task edit back-10 --dep "" errors and suggests using --clear-deps (older versions silently no-op'd with exit 0, which was a false success)
MCP task_edit semantics are consistent: empty-string elements in arrays are rejected; only an explicit empty array [] means clear

Three Forms of Reference Entries
Each entry for --ref / --add-ref is one location and supports three forms:



Form
Example




External URL
https://docs.example.com/auth


Project-relative file path
src/utils/editor.ts


Path with line range
src/utils/editor.ts:42 (single line) or src/utils/editor.ts:40-58 (range)




One entry carries one location; to reference two regions of the same file, use two entries
--remove-ref matches the stored full string, including the line-number suffix
In the Web UI, clicking a link with a line-number suffix opens the preview box at the specified line range

Comment Deletion
# Delete the 2nd comment
backlog task edit back-10 --remove-comment 2

# Delete multiple at once (list-edit flags support comma separation)
backlog task edit back-10 --remove-comment 2,3

# Clear all comments
backlog task edit back-10 --clear-comments

--remove-comment accepts 1-based indices; out-of-bounds errors with the available indices listed. --clear-comments cannot be used with --comment. After deletion, remaining comments are renumbered by position (the index itself is not persistent). CLI, MCP task_edit, the Web UI comment per-comment delete button, and the "Clear comments" button all behave consistently.
Concurrent Edit Protection
Task read-modify-write is protected by file locks to prevent two processes from silently overwriting each other's edits. On contention it fails immediately:
Edit failed: back-10 is being modified by another process; retry if appropriate.



Surface
Behavior on contention




CLI
Non-zero exit code and the message above; task file unchanged


Web API
HTTP 409


MCP
Operation error (OPERATION_FAILED)



It is fail-fast: no waiting, no merging, no automatic retry; the failing side must retry itself. The lock is based on the task file itself and works across independent backlog processes, not just within a single process. Locks also cover the draft demotion path.
Task List and Filtering
# List all tasks
backlog task list

# Filter by status
backlog task list -s "In Progress"

# Multi-status filter (repeat or comma-separated)
backlog task list -s "To Do" -s "In Progress"

# Exclude a status
backlog task list --exclude-status "Done"

# Show only unassigned tasks (mutually exclusive with --assignee)
backlog task list --unassigned

# Filter by assignee
backlog task list -a "@developer"

# Filter by milestone
backlog task list -m "M1 - CLI"

# Filter by priority
backlog task list --priority high

# View subtasks of a specific parent task
backlog task list -p back-4

# Sort by field (priority or id)
backlog task list --sort priority

# Only list tasks whose dependencies are ready to start
backlog task list --ready

# Expand corpus: also list historical tasks from completed directory
backlog task list --completed

# Plain-text output
backlog task list --plain

--completed expands the read scope from active tasks to the backlog/completed/ corpus; JSON rows are marked with source: "completed". backlog search --completed and MCP list_tasks / search_tasks with completed: true have the same semantics. Note: MCP task_search now defaults to searching only active tasks; pass completed: true explicitly to include historical tasks.
Plain-text list rows append (ac: checked/total) when a task has acceptance criteria; MCP plain-text lists do the same. Tasks without acceptance criteria do not show this suffix.
List Paging
task list, search, draft list, milestone list, doc list, doc search, decision list, and memo list all support grep-style paging window options:



Option
Description
Example




--max-count 
Output at most n items
--max-count 20


--skip 
Skip the first n items (next page)
--skip 20


--count
Output only the match count (a number)
--count



The window is applied after filtering, sorting, and --limit, in output order, so consecutive pages neither overlap nor miss items. Truncated text output ends with Showing - of  items. Next: backlog task list --skip ; copy that command to page forward. --count outputs only a number and cannot be combined with --json (returns non-zero); JSON envelopes include total / nextSkip only when the window truncates the list. Centralized paging semantics are described in the "List Paging" section of Search & Sequences.
Dependency-Ready Filter (--ready)
backlog task list --ready keeps only tasks that can start immediately:

Determination is fail-closed: if any dependency is incomplete or unresolvable, the task is considered blocked
Completed tasks count as "completion evidence" regardless of their status string (based on presence in the completed corpus)
Dependency identity is matched by normalized ID (prefix and zero-padding differences do not affect determination)
Circular dependencies and ambiguous dependency data are marked as blocked rather than guessed
The same determination appears in CLI (--ready, plain/json/interactive output), the TUI task detail panel Readiness row, the Web task detail Dependencies card status badge, and MCP task_list's ready: true parameter
This filter only marks and filters; it does not modify tasks or override ordinal-sort authority

Completing and Archiving Tasks
The first step to complete a task is to change its status to a terminal status (usually Done):
backlog task edit  --status "Done"

After reaching a terminal status, if you want to remove the task from the active board, run the complete subcommand to move the task file into backlog/completed/:
backlog task complete 

task complete is a cleanup operation: the task must be in a terminal status, otherwise the command errors and prompts you to first advance status with backlog task edit  -s "". On success, the task disappears from the active board, the file moves to the completed directory, and the output shows Completed task . with the new file path. The corresponding MCP tool is task_complete (parameter id), with the same semantics, and it does not allow completing tasks from other branches.
Archiving moves the file to backlog/archive/tasks/, which is a soft delete; the original ID can be reused by later new tasks:
backlog task archive 

To periodically remove completed tasks from the active list, run the cleanup command:
backlog cleanup

Date Fields
When creating or editing tasks, manage date fields with these options:
# Planning fields (date-only)
backlog task create "API docs" --due-date 2026-06-01 --planned-start 2026-05-25 --planned-end 2026-05-30

# Actual fields (datetime)
backlog task create "Urgent fix" --status "In Progress" --actual-start "2026-05-29 10:00"
backlog task edit back-10 --actual-end "2026-05-30 18:00" --clear-actual-start


Planning fields use YYYY-MM-DD (date-only)
Actual fields use YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (UTC datetime)
In interactive TTY environments, the create/edit wizard prompts for dates

Date Editing in Web UI
In the task detail modal sidebar:

Due Date / Planned Start / Planned End — date input
Actual Start / Actual End — datetime-local input (supports UTC ↔ local timezone conversion)

Auto-fill rules: when Due Date is set and Planned Start is empty, the system auto-fills Planned Start with the current date and Planned End with the Due Date value. You can modify these auto-filled values before saving.
Actual-time auto-fill: when task status is changed to In Progress or Done in the Web UI, the system auto-fills the corresponding actual field (if empty).
Date clearing: clicking the Clear button on any date input and saving the task removes the corresponding date field from the file. Clearing is transmitted via an empty string so the server receives the deletion correctly.
Creating Tasks in Web UI
Click the "New Task" button in the Web board or task list to open the creation modal:

References / Documentation: in creation mode, you can add reference links or associated documents via path autocomplete; typing .back discovers the .backlog directory
After saving, references and documentation are written to the task file

Demoting to Draft
If a task needs more refinement before execution, demote it to a draft:
backlog task demote 

After demotion, the task moves to backlog/drafts/ and receives an independent draft ID (e.g., draft-3). References to the original ID from other tasks are automatically cleaned up (see Archiving & Cleanup).
The Web UI demotion operation has accidental-trigger protection: all editing, status changes, and shortcuts are locked during demotion; on network errors it clearly warns "demotion may have succeeded" and refreshes the view for verification, avoiding duplicate submissions.
Label Input (Web UI)
When editing labels in the Web task detail modal, the label input supports smart autocomplete:

Dropdown hints: clicking the label input or typing displays a dropdown of all existing project labels (configured labels plus labels used in any task)
Fuzzy search: typing matches characters in order, e.g. we matches web-ui
Keyboard selection: use ↑ / ↓ to highlight options and Enter to select; press Escape to close the dropdown
Create new label: when the input matches no existing label, press Enter or type a comma , to create a new label
Duplicate detection: trying to add an item that differs only in case from an existing label (e.g. Feature when feature exists) turns the input border red and the dropdown shows feature already added

Opening Tasks in an Editor
Editing in TUI
In the TUI (backlog task  or backlog board):

Select the target task
Press E (or Shift+e) to open the task file directly in the system editor
After closing the editor, the TUI automatically resumes and reloads the latest content

Manual Editing
Task files are ordinary Markdown and can be modified with any editor:
vim backlog/tasks/back-10.md

After manual editing, Backlog.md's file watcher automatically refreshes the index without restarting the service.

10-任务管理/02-草稿管理.html.title: Draft Management
10-任务管理/02-草稿管理.html.body:
Draft Management
Drafts are a lightweight pre-task form in Backlog.md for capturing immature ideas, features pending decomposition, or requirements that need further clarification.
When to Use Drafts



Scenario
Description




Quick idea capture
Save a title and brief description without filling in all fields


Requirements pending review
Collect feedback before creating a formal task


Task-splitting preparation
Record a complex feature as a draft first, then refine it into multiple formal tasks


Avoid polluting the task list
Drafts do not consume formal task IDs and do not appear in the default board view



Creating Drafts
Via task create
Add the --draft option when creating a task to generate a draft directly:
backlog task create "Future feature idea" --draft

Via draft create
Use the draft-specific subcommand for simpler syntax:
backlog draft create "Future feature idea"

Draft with Description
backlog draft create "Refactor auth module" \
  -d "Consider migrating Session auth to JWT" \
  -l "refactor" \
  -a "@architect"

draft create supports the following options:



Option
Description




-d, --description 
Description


--desc 
Alias for --description


-a, --assignee 
Assignee


-s, --status 
Status (default Draft)


-l, --labels 
Labels, comma-separated


--due-date 
Due date (YYYY-MM-DD)


--planned-start / --planned-end 
Planned start/end dates


--actual-start / --actual-end 
Actual start/end times (stored in UTC)




Drafts share the same creation-time date options as tasks.

Editing Drafts
Use draft edit to modify draft fields directly; options are identical to task edit:
backlog draft edit draft-3 --title "Clearer title" -l "refactor,backend"
backlog draft edit draft-3 --append-notes "Added research conclusions"

Rules:

Only a single draft ID is accepted; batch editing is not supported
At least one field flag is required; otherwise it errors
--status only accepts Draft; to promote to a formal task use backlog draft promote—scripts cannot silently promote a draft in one "edit"
Add --plain to output the full edited record

Draft ID Disambiguation Protection
Draft identity resolution is fail-closed: when one ID matches multiple draft files (e.g., draft-3 and draft-03 coexist due to numbering drift), draft view / draft edit / draft archive / draft promote list all candidates and exit non-zero rather than picking one arbitrarily. backlog doctor reports such draft identity issues (duplicate numbering, frontmatter drift, unparseable files).
Listing Drafts
backlog draft list

Default sort is by priority. Optional parameters:



Option
Description




--sort 
Sort by priority or id


--max-count  / --skip  / --count
Paging window: at most n items / skip n items / output count only (semantics in Search & Sequences, "List Paging")


--plain
Plain-text output



Promoting Drafts to Tasks
When a draft is clear enough to start executing, promote it to a formal task:
backlog draft promote draft-3

After promotion:

The draft file moves from backlog/drafts/ to backlog/tasks/
The draft ID (e.g., draft-3) is replaced with a formal task ID (e.g., back-15)
The original draft file is archived or deleted

Demoting Tasks to Drafts
If a formal task is found to be immature and needs to be put on hold, demote it back to a draft:
backlog task demote back-10

After demotion:

The task file moves from backlog/tasks/ to backlog/drafts/
The original formal task ID is freed and can be reused by new tasks
A new draft ID is assigned (e.g., draft-5)

Web UI Drafts Page
Visit /drafts in the browser to view the draft list and manage filters.
Filter Bar
The top of the page provides a filter bar consistent with the task list:



Control
Description




Keyword search
Search by draft ID or title, substring match, with clear button


Status filter
Dropdown of all available statuses


Priority filter
All / High / Medium / Low


Milestone filter
All milestones / No milestone / each active milestone


Label filter
Multi-select chip input with autocomplete



The filter result count is shown in real time as Showing X / Y drafts. When active filters exist, a "Clear filters" button appears on the right to reset them in one click.
Filter State Persistence
All filter conditions (including search terms) are automatically synchronized to URL query parameters, so pages can be shared and bookmarked. Supported parameters:

?status= — status filter
?priority= — priority filter
?milestone= — milestone filter (__none means no milestone)
?label= — label filter (can appear multiple times)
?q= — keyword search

Draft Cards and Actions
Each draft card shows the title, priority badge, ID, creation/update time, assignee, and labels. Clicking a card opens the draft detail editor; the "Promote to task" button on the right promotes the draft to a formal task.
Archiving Drafts
For drafts that are no longer needed, archive them directly:
backlog draft archive draft-2

Archived drafts are moved to backlog/archive/tasks/.
Drafts Use an Independent ID Space
Drafts and formal tasks use completely independent numbering systems:

Formal task IDs: back-1, back-2, back-3...
Draft IDs: draft-1, draft-2, draft-3...

This means:

The number of drafts does not affect the formal task ID sequence
Promoting a draft assigns the next available formal task ID
Demoting a task assigns the next available draft ID
Deleting or archiving a draft does not create gaps in formal task numbering

10-任务管理/03-子任务与依赖.html.title: Subtasks & Dependencies
10-任务管理/03-子任务与依赖.html.body:
Subtasks & Dependencies
Backlog.md supports breaking complex work into subtasks and defining execution order between tasks through dependencies.
Creating Subtasks
When creating a task, use --parent (or -p) to specify the parent task ID to create a subtask:
backlog task create "Design database tables" -p back-4
backlog task create "Implement REST API" -p back-4
backlog task create "Write unit tests" -p back-4

Decimal Numbering Rules
Subtasks use a decimal numbering system in the format parentID.sequence:



Parent
Subtasks




back-4
back-4.1, back-4.2, back-4.3



Numbering rules:

Subtask sequence numbers auto-increment by creation order
A parent task can have any number of subtasks
Subtasks cannot have subtasks (single-level structure)
Subtasks are associated with the parent in lists, boards, and the Web UI by default

Viewing Subtasks
# View all subtasks of a specific parent
backlog task list -p back-4

# Subtasks are automatically listed when viewing task details
backlog task view back-4

Changing Parent-Child Relationships
Existing tasks can be reassigned to a different parent without deleting and recreating:
# Move task under a new parent
backlog task edit back-10 --parent back-4

# Remove parent-child relationship (return to top level)
backlog task edit back-10 --clear-parent

--parent / --clear-parent is shared between CLI and MCP: it only rewrites the task's parent_task_id edge, normalizes the input ID, and prevents cycles before writing (rolling back and erroring if one would form). Re-parenting does not change the task's sequence number or content, only its hierarchical position.
Setting Task Dependencies
When creating a task, use --dep (or --depends-on) to specify tasks it depends on:
backlog task create "Deploy to production" \
  --dep "back-5,back-6" \
  --notes "Wait for frontend and backend tasks to complete"

You can also add or modify dependencies after creation:
# Overwrite dependencies
backlog task edit back-10 --dep "back-3,back-4"

# When depending on multiple tasks, you can repeat the option
backlog task edit back-10 --dep "back-3" --dep "back-4"

Dependency Target Resolution Rules
Dependency targets are resolved against working-copy tasks and the completed corpus:

Depending on a completed task is valid—completed records are the "completion evidence" used by readiness determination
Archived task IDs can be reused by new tasks, so archived records do not participate in dependency resolution; IDs that exist only in archive are treated as unknown
When one ID is claimed by multiple records, or one input matches multiple identities, the command fails with an ambiguity error (fail-closed) rather than picking one
Drafts cannot be dependency targets (drafts can depend on tasks, but tasks cannot depend on drafts)

Write Gate: Self-Dependency and Cycle Rejection
Creating and editing dependencies performs hard validation:

Depending on itself (--dep back-10 on back-10) is rejected
Dependencies that would form a cycle are rejected, with the full chain in the error message (e.g., TASK-1 -> TASK-2 -> TASK-1)
Unresolvable new dependency entries are rejected (strict at creation time)

Softened rule for existing defects: when editing a task, unresolvable entries that already existed and were not modified in this edit are preserved as-is (CLI prints a warning; JSON/MCP results carry them as data), so you are not forced to clean up historical debt just to edit a title. Once an entry is rewritten, it is validated under the new rules.
Dependency Defect Diagnosis (doctor)
backlog doctor includes a dependency defect report, organized by category across the whole corpus:

Circular dependencies (including self-loops), listed by ID order
Dangling dependencies: tasks referencing non-existent IDs, listed one by one
Draft targets: tasks that depend on drafts (forbidden direction)
Released IDs: dependencies pointing to archived, reusable old IDs, with rebinding warnings
Ambiguous references: cross-referenced with duplicate-ID reports

This report is diagnostic only: it reports but does not fix (--fix still only repairs duplicate IDs). Dependency defects do not affect the exit code—long-standing historical issues should not cause every diagnosis to fail.
How Dependencies Affect Sequences
Backlog.md automatically calculates execution sequences from task dependencies:

Tasks with no dependencies, no dependents, and no ordinal are classified as Unsequenced
Tasks with dependencies are layered by topological sort, forming Sequence 1, Sequence 2...
Tasks in the same Sequence do not depend on each other and can run in parallel
Different Sequences have ordering: all tasks in Sequence N must wait until Sequence N-1 is complete

Viewing Sequences
backlog sequence list

Example output:
Unsequenced:
  back-8 - Optimize build speed

Sequence 1:
  back-1 - Design database tables
  back-2 - Set up project skeleton

Sequence 2:
  back-3 - Implement user registration API
  back-4 - Implement user login API

Sequence 3:
  back-5 - Deploy to test environment
In this example:

back-1 and back-2 can be developed in parallel
back-3 and back-4 depend on back-1 and back-2, so they start only after those finish
back-3 and back-4 can run in parallel with each other
back-5 depends on back-3 and back-4, so it must run last

Web UI Dependency Drill-Down
In the Web task detail panel, the Dependencies section lists all tasks this task depends on. Each dependency is shown as a blue badge:

Click a dependency badge: opens that dependency's detail panel directly, without returning to the board or list
Back button: after drilling into a subtask, a ← Back arrow appears in the task detail panel header; click it to return to the previous parent task
Close button: clicking × in the top-right is equivalent to the browser back button, going back one level at a time—when already drilled in, it returns to the previous parent; one more click from the outermost level closes the entire modal


This feature is unavailable in new-task or edit-task modes; it only works in preview mode.

Parent/Child Hierarchy Block in the Modal
The task detail modal provides a hierarchy block below the title for direct up/down navigation:

PARENT row: shown when the current task has a parent; includes parent ID, title, and status badge; click to open the parent
SUBTASKS section: shown when the current task has subtasks; shows completion count (e.g., 1/6) and progress bar; click the section header to expand or collapse; each subtask shows completion indicator, ID, title, status badge, and drill arrow; click to open that subtask

Both blocks render only when the corresponding relationship exists; tasks without parent-child relationships do not show them.

Completed subtasks are also included: the parent task's SUBTASKS section now lists both active and completed subtasks; previously completed subtasks could disappear from the parent view. The completion count (e.g., 1/6) is now accurate. About 100 historical files still use the old task- prefix references and are outside the scope of this change.

Drilling Down via Markdown Links
In task descriptions, documents, decision records, and Wiki pages, links to other tasks such as /task/:id (e.g., http://localhost:6420/task/506) open the target task directly in the modal, with the same experience as clicking a dependency badge:

Prefix-agnostic matching: both bare numbers (/task/123) and full IDs with prefix resolve correctly
The system automatically renders full URLs as a short alias TASK#506 for readability
After drilling down, the back button and browser forward/back navigation work the same way

Stable URLs and Sharing
Every task has an independent /task/:id/:title URL:
http://localhost:6420/task/506/Fix-CLI-actualStart-actualEnd-missing-local-to-UTC-conversion
You can copy the address-bar link and share it with team members; opening it shows the task detail over the default view and allows further dependency drill-down.
Dependency Planning Recommendations



Recommendation
Description




Control dependency count
Too many dependencies reduce flexibility; keep only true blocking relationships


Combine subtasks and dependencies
Use subtasks to split work scope and dependencies to define execution order


Review sequences regularly
Run backlog sequence list to identify the critical path and parallelizable work packages


Avoid circular dependencies
The system automatically detects and prevents cycles

10-任务管理/04-搜索与序列.html.title: Search & Sequences
10-任务管理/04-搜索与序列.html.body:
Search & Sequences
Search
Backlog.md provides a unified fuzzy-search service built on Fuse.js, covering tasks, documents, and decision records.
CLI Search
Run backlog search followed by a keyword to search across all projects:
backlog search "user login"

Filters



Option
Description
Example




--type 
Restrict result type (task, document, decision)
--type task


--status 
Filter by task status (repeatable or comma-separated for multiple)
--status "In Progress"


--exclude-status 
Exclude tasks with the given status
--exclude-status "Done"


--unassigned
Show only tasks with no assignee
--unassigned


--priority 
Filter by priority (high, medium, low)
--priority high


--modified-file 
Filter by substring of a modified file path
--modified-file src/api.ts


--completed
Extend the search scope to historical tasks in the completed corpus
--completed


--limit 
Limit the total number of returned results
--limit 10


--plain
Plain-text output
--plain



Combined Search Examples
# Search for tasks containing "api" and in "In Progress" status
backlog search "api" --status "In Progress"

# Search for high-priority bugs
backlog search "bug" --priority high --type task

# Search for changes related to a specific file
backlog search "auth" --modified-file src/auth.ts

# Search only documents and decisions
backlog search "architecture" --type document --type decision

# Exclude completed tasks
backlog search "api" --exclude-status "Done"

# Show only unassigned high-priority tasks
backlog search "api" --unassigned --priority high

# Show the first 20 results, then the next page
backlog search "api" --max-count 20
backlog search "api" --max-count 20 --skip 20

# Output only the total match count
backlog search "api" --count

List Paging
backlog search and the eight list commands task list, draft list, milestone list, doc list, doc search, decision list, and memo list share the same grep-style paging window options:



Option
Description
Example




--max-count 
Output at most n items
--max-count 20


--skip 
Skip the first n items (next page)
--skip 20


--count
Output only the total match count (a single number)
--count




The window is applied after filtering, sorting, and --limit, in output order; consecutive pages do not overlap or skip items.
When output is truncated, it ends with Showing - of  items. Next: backlog  --skip ; copy the suggested Next command to fetch the next page.
--count outputs only a number and cannot be combined with --json (returns a non-zero exit code).
The JSON envelope appends total / nextSkip fields only when the window truncates the output; if nothing is truncated, the output is byte-for-byte unchanged.
For milestone list, the window unit is a milestone; the --with-no-milestone "No Milestone" section is always placed first, does not consume the quota, and is not counted by --count.

backlog instructions overview contains a List Paging Quick Reference for these options; each command chapter (tasks, drafts, milestones, documents, decisions, memos) documents paging for that command.
TUI Search
In the interactive backlog board or backlog task list interface, typing a keyword filters the list in real time. TUI search responds instantly and updates results as you type, without requiring Enter.
Web Search
After starting the Web interface with backlog browser, press Ctrl+K (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+K (macOS), or click the search trigger in the sidebar, to open the global search dialog. It searches tasks, drafts, documents, decisions, Wiki pages, and memos in one go. Results are grouped by type, with the keyword and resource ID highlighted, and support keyboard navigation and scroll-position memory. Query and type filters are synchronized to /search?q=...&type=... links that can be refreshed or shared. See Global Search for details.

CLI backlog search plain-text output covers only tasks, documents, and decisions; memos and Wiki results are Web-only types and appear only in Web search and JSON output.

Search Score Threshold Alignment
CLI, TUI, MCP, and Web UI share the same Fuse.js score threshold of 0.45, filtering out low-relevance results. This prevents short numbers such as 63 from accidentally matching unrelated task IDs while preserving Fuse semantics for text queries.
Sequences
What Sequences Are
Sequences are groups of tasks that can run in parallel, automatically computed from task dependencies. They help you understand, without manual scheduling:

Critical path: which tasks must finish before others can start
Parallelizable work packages: tasks in the same sequence can be advanced simultaneously by different team members
Project bottlenecks: the longest dependency chain often determines overall duration

Viewing Sequences
backlog sequence list

By default this opens the sequence view in interactive TUI mode. Use --plain for plain-text output:
backlog sequence list --plain

Reading the Sequence Output
Unsequenced:
  back-12 - Optimize homepage load speed

Sequence 1:
  back-1 - Design database tables
  back-2 - Set up project skeleton

Sequence 2:
  back-3 - Implement user registration API
  back-4 - Implement user login API

Sequence 3:
  back-5 - Deploy to test environment

Unsequenced: tasks that have no dependencies, are not depended on by any other task, and have no ordinal. They block nothing and are blocked by nothing.
Sequence N: the Nth layer of parallelizable tasks. Sequence 1 has no prerequisites; Sequence 2 depends on one or more tasks in Sequence 1, and so on.
Tasks marked Done are not shown in sequences.

TUI Sequence View Operations
backlog sequence list now uses a dual-panel layout:

Left sidebar: lists Unsequenced tasks and Sequence 1, Sequence 2, etc.; click to switch the focused sequence.
Right task list: shows tasks in the currently selected sequence (or Unsequenced). Use arrow keys or j/k to browse; press Enter to view task details.
Move mode: press m in the task list to adjust task order and automatically update dependencies. The move preview is computed by the pure function buildMovePreview, so what you see is what you get.
Press Escape or q to exit.


The old recursive select item implementation could stack-overflow on deep sequences; this has been eliminated with pure functions such as buildSequenceRows.

Web UI Sequence Page
In the browser interface, the sequence page supports drag-and-drop reordering. Dropping a task card at a different sequence position automatically updates the related dependencies.
Sequence Quick Reference in CLI Instructions
backlog instructions overview includes a quick reference for sequence commands:
backlog sequence list --plain

This command prints a plain-text sequence hierarchy. Sequences are derived from task dependencies; tasks within the same sequence can run in parallel, while different sequences have a happens-before relationship. See the "Viewing Sequences" and "TUI Sequence View Operations" sections above for more details.
What Sequences Mean for Project Planning



Use Case
Action




Planning a Sprint
Assign sequence layers to different iteration cycles


Identifying Risk
Delays on the critical path directly impact overall progress


Resource Allocation
Assign tasks in the same sequence to different developers to run in parallel


Dependency Review
Run backlog sequence list regularly to check for unreasonable hard dependencies

10-任务管理/05-归档与清理.html.title: Archiving & Cleanup
10-任务管理/05-归档与清理.html.body:
Archive & Cleanup
As a project progresses, completed tasks accumulate. Backlog.md provides archiving and cleanup mechanisms to help keep the task list tidy.
Archiving Tasks
Archiving moves inactive tasks into the backlog/archive/tasks/ directory. It is a soft delete:
backlog task archive back-10

After archiving:

The task file is moved from backlog/tasks/ to backlog/archive/tasks/.
The task no longer appears in default task lists, boards, or search results.
The original task ID is released and may be reused by newly created tasks.

Archiving Drafts
Drafts can also be archived individually:
backlog draft archive draft-2

Reusing Archived Task IDs
Backlog.md's ID allocator automatically skips IDs that are already in use. After a task is archived, its original ID is reclaimed and may be assigned again by a future backlog task create.
Reference Cleanup When an ID Is Freed
Archiving (task archive) and demoting (task demote) automatically clean up references to the freed ID in other tasks:

Dependencies and references pointing to that ID are removed or corrected in active tasks and in the completed corpus, preventing old references from silently binding to new tasks after ID reuse.
The IDs of affected tasks are listed in CLI output, MCP results, and Web responses (cleanedTaskIds) and are included in the commit scope when auto-commit is enabled.
Demoted drafts keep their own dependency and parent fields, but references from other tasks to the draft are removed rather than rewritten to the new draft ID.
Completing (complete / cleanup) does not clean up references—completed records are the completion evidence needed by readiness determination.
Archive and demote operations are resolved against the local working copy (local-first) and will not accidentally modify other branches.


Files affected by cleanup are also covered by file locking and auto-commit; no manual follow-up is needed.

The Cleanup Command
The cleanup command batch-moves old completed tasks out of the active directory into the backlog/completed/ folder:
backlog cleanup

Running it starts an interactive wizard that guides you through:

Scanning all tasks in a terminal status (usually Done).
Choosing a time threshold: 1 day, 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks, 1 month, 3 months, or 1 year.
Listing all tasks that meet the threshold.
Confirming before batch-moving them to the backlog/completed/ directory.

Found 12 tasks marked as Done.

Move tasks to completed folder if they are older than:
> 1 month

Found 8 tasks older than 1 month:
  - back-3: Design database tables (2026-04-01)
  - back-4: Implement user registration (2026-04-02)
  ... and 6 more

Move 8 tasks to completed folder? (y/N)
Completing a Single Task
cleanup is for batch cleanup. To move a single terminal-status task out of the active board, use task complete:
backlog task complete back-10

Unlike cleanup, task complete only performs the completion move: it validates that the task is in a terminal status (determined by the categories/exits in config.statuses, not simply "the last status is terminal"), then moves the task file from backlog/tasks/ to backlog/completed/ without touching references in other tasks—the completed corpus is exactly the completion evidence other tasks need for readiness determination. If the task is not in a terminal status, the command fails and suggests first advancing the status with backlog task edit  -s "".
The corresponding MCP tool is task_complete (parameter id), with the same semantics: it accepts only local tasks and returns VALIDATION_ERROR when terminal-status validation fails. Note the difference from task_archive—task_archive rejects terminal-status tasks and prompts you to use task_complete instead.
Archive vs. Complete / Cleanup



Dimension
Archive
Complete / Cleanup




Trigger
Manual task archive
Manual task complete (single) or cleanup (batch)


Destination
backlog/archive/tasks/
backlog/completed/


Task Status
Any status can be archived
Only terminal statuses (e.g., Done) can be completed / cleaned up


Reference Cleanup
Automatically cleans references to the freed ID
Does not clean references (preserves completion evidence)


ID Reuse
ID becomes reusable after archiving
Whether the ID becomes reusable after moving to completed depends on configuration


Use Case
Discarded, duplicate, or mistakenly created tasks
Normally completed but outdated historical tasks that no longer need to be viewed


Recoverable
Can be moved back manually from the archive directory
Can be moved back manually from the completed directory



Maintenance Recommendations



Frequency
Recommended Action




Weekly
Run backlog cleanup to move tasks completed more than 2 weeks ago to completed


Monthly
Review the task list and archive invalid or duplicate tasks


Quarterly
Check the backlog/completed/ and backlog/archive/ directories and decide whether to delete or keep old files



Keeping the active task list lean improves board load speed, enhances the search experience, and keeps the team focused on work in progress.

20-看板与可视化/00-TUI看板.html.title: TUI Board
20-看板与可视化/00-TUI看板.html.body:
TUI Board
Run backlog board in the terminal to start a character-based interactive board. The board displays tasks grouped by status, and supports keyboard navigation, moving tasks, real-time filtering, and file watching—so you can keep track of the whole project without leaving the terminal.
Launching the Board
backlog board

On first launch, the board loads the status columns from the project configuration and places tasks into the matching columns. Legacy string-config projects default to three columns: To Do, In Progress, Done; newly initialized projects use the built-in seven-state default state machine (see Task Lifecycle). Statuses with display: false are hidden together with their tasks. If milestone mode is enabled, tasks are grouped by milestone.
Common Startup Options
# Vertical layout (status columns stacked vertically; good for narrow terminals)
backlog board --vertical

# Explicitly set the layout direction
backlog board --layout vertical
backlog board --layout horizontal

# Milestone grouping mode (tasks shown in milestone swimlanes)
backlog board --milestones

Keyboard Navigation
Once the board is running, use these keys:



Key
Action




↑ ↓ ← →
Move the selection focus on the board


Enter
Open the detail popup for the selected task


N
Open the task creator and create a task directly in the board


E
Open the current task file in the system editor (the TUI suspends and resumes after you close the editor)


Tab
Switch between board view and task list view


M
Enter / confirm board move mode


PageUp / Ctrl+U
Scroll the list / scrollable area up one page


PageDown / Ctrl+D
Scroll the list / scrollable area down one page


Home
Jump to the top of the list / scrollable area


End
Jump to the bottom of the list / scrollable area


H J K L
Vim-style navigation (available alongside arrow keys)


Q
Quit the board




Tip: When you press E to edit a task, the TUI suspends and resumes automatically; you do not need to restart the board.

When E is pressed, the system opens the file based on the actual file location of the row: rows in the drafts directory open the draft file, and rows in the tasks directory open the task file—even if the file's status field no longer matches the directory (for example after demotion). The prompt text (task / draft) matches the actual object being edited.
Vim Key Family and Boundary Behavior
The list components support both arrow keys and vim keys (h/j/k/l). The boundary semantics are the same for both:

When you reach the top or bottom of a list, the behavior depends on the panel: it may stop at the boundary, scroll a page, or jump to an adjacent panel—rather than silently doing nothing.
The same rule applies to composite lists such as filter popups, where vim keys also work.
No configuration is required: vim keys are enabled by default and coexist with arrow keys.

Creating Tasks in the Board
Press N to open the task creator directly inside the board, without leaving the TUI or switching to the Web interface:

Fields: Title, Description, Status (including Draft and workflow statuses), Priority, and five date fields—Due, Planned from/to, Actual from/to; dates must be YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm, and invalid dates are rejected with focus returned to the offending field.
Use arrow keys to move between fields; Tab / Shift+Tab also switches fields.
After creating a non-Draft task, it is inserted into the board immediately and focused.
After creating a Draft task, the UI tells you that drafts are not shown on the board.
The creator is always available, even when the board is empty.

Creator Interaction Details

Mouse support: Click Title / Description / Status / Priority fields to focus them or open selectors.
Extreme terminal sizes: Popup height and width adapt to the actual screen; input boxes remain editable on terminals as short as ~8 rows. Width is computed dynamically from the configured status / priority label lengths; very long status names automatically switch to a compact stacked layout.
Unicode-safe input: Inserting or deleting text next to astral characters (such as rare CJK characters) does not cause garbled output or cursor misalignment; wide characters are measured as two display cells (emoji are also treated as double-width).

Draft Session
The interactive interface of backlog draft list is a board session whose corpus is drafts:

Pressing N opens the creator with status fixed to Draft; the title shows "Create Draft" and the fields are identical to the task creator (including dates).
The session watches the backlog/drafts/ directory in real time: external edits and deletions are reflected immediately; drafts promoted to tasks disappear from the session automatically.
The task board session never shows draft files.

Board Move Mode
Move mode lets you change task status directly in the terminal:

Use arrow keys to select the task you want to move.
Press M to enter move mode; the current task is marked as pending move.
Use ← → to choose the target status column, and ↑ ↓ to adjust the insert position.
Press M or Enter again to confirm; the task status is updated immediately and synced to the Markdown file.
Press Esc to cancel the move and restore the original position.


Note: Cross-branch tasks from other branches cannot be moved directly in the board; the system explains why in the bottom status bar.

Multi-Select Move (Shift + Arrow Keys)
Move mode supports moving several tasks at once:
