After entering move mode with M, use Shift+↑ / Shift+↓ to move the highlight in the target column without affecting board order.
Press M (or Shift+M) to recruit the highlighted task into the move set; terminals that do not support Shift-arrow keys can use this key to recruit neighboring tasks.
After recruiting, the first normal arrow key collapses the highlight and previews the whole group landing as an adjacent block; confirming writes all tasks at once.
During the write, arrow keys and cancel keys are frozen; a move that lands in the original position is a no-op. Per-task failures are reported in the bottom status bar.

Cross-branch tasks cannot be recruited. Confirmation is debounced so pressing Enter repeatedly does not submit more than once.
Task List and Filtering
Press Tab to switch from the board to the task list view. The list view supports finer-grained filtering:

Status filter: show only tasks with a specific status.
Assignee filter: filter by @username.
Label filter: multi-select filtering by label.
Milestone filter: show only tasks belonging to a given milestone.
Priority filter: high / medium / low.
Search box: real-time fuzzy matching against task titles and descriptions.

At the bottom of the list view, open the filter panel with the corresponding shortcut; the list refreshes instantly as you check conditions. Filter conditions are shared between board view and list view and remain active when you return to the board.
Compact View
When terminal height is limited, the list view automatically switches to compact mode, hiding some metadata and keeping only task ID, title, and status so you can still browse many tasks in a small terminal window.
Milestone Board View
backlog milestones provides a dual-column layout with a sidebar plus an embedded board:

The left sidebar lists the "Unassigned" bucket and all milestones (including completed markers). Use ↑ / ↓ to move the cursor, Space to restrict the board to that milestone (an ▶ appears at the start of the row), and Enter to open the milestone detail popup (metadata only, no task list).
The right side is the full board; keyboard focus routes between the board and the sidebar. The filter bar shows /.
N creates a milestone when the sidebar is focused, and creates a task (defaulting to the currently restricted milestone) when the board is focused. In the milestone popup, E opens an edit form (title, description, Due, Planned / Actual start/end; dates must be YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm; the title is read-only after creation).
Milestone and task changes are synced live: externally edited milestones refresh the popup in place; archived or deleted milestones close the popup with a notice.

In non-TTY environments, backlog milestones list --plain outputs a Markdown grouped board consistent with backlog board -m ("No Milestone" first, then sections by milestone file order, with tasks grouped by status inside each section). Use --show-completed to include completed tasks.
Real-Time File Watching
The TUI board uses filesystem watching (Bun.watch) and refreshes automatically when:

A task status is changed in the Web UI or another terminal.
A task is updated via the backlog task edit command.
An AI agent modifies a task file through MCP tools.

This means you can have the TUI board and the Web interface open at the same time, and changes on either side are synced to the other in real time.
Real-time refresh is resilient to atomic writes: the CLI may trigger brief partial-content events when writing task files, and the TUI waits for the file to stabilize before refreshing, avoiding reads of incomplete task content. The selected task remains valid after refreshes, moves, archives, or deletions; after deletion, the adjacent task is automatically selected.
Syncing of already-open popups: Task popups and milestone popups are also "live"—when content is modified externally, they re-render in place after comparing content signatures. When a record moves out of the current view, the popup closes with a notice. Refresh events that produce no change (for example an echo from saving inside the popup) do not cause flicker or rebuild.
Acceptance Criteria Progress Indicator
Tasks in In Progress that contain acceptance criteria (AC) show an ASCII progress bar on the board row, such as [#####-----] 5/10:

Uses only ASCII characters # (done) and - (not done), so every terminal font renders it correctly.
Shows a 10-cell bar when the column is wide enough, and a 5-cell bar when narrower than 40 columns.
Color by completion: green when fully complete, red when below one-third, yellow otherwise; at least one cell is shown as soon as any item is checked.
Derived live from acceptance criteria and not persisted; tasks without AC or not in In Progress do not show it.
The task detail panel no longer shows the progress bar, only the checklist itself—the board row is the single place for progress.

Help Popup
Press ? to open the help popup: its height adapts to the terminal size (never exceeding the screen) and re-layouts live when the terminal is resized; the scroll limit is computed from the actual rendered rows so wrapped explanatory text can still be scrolled to the end on narrow terminals. The backdrop of the task detail popup also re-layouts live with terminal size, leaving no misaligned leftover areas after resizing.
Theme Adaptation and Stable Switching
The TUI board renders with terminal theme adaptation to avoid readability problems from hard-coded ANSI colors:

Most control borders use the terminal default color and follow the current color scheme.
The cyan highlight for board move mode is preserved as a recognizable marker for the task being moved.
Long lists and scrollable areas support PageUp / PageDown / Home / End for quick positioning and show a scrollbar indicator.

Tab switching between board and list view is stability-hardened: stdin input is not lost and duplicate listeners do not accumulate, so switching in either direction is reliable.
Dependency Readiness Hint
The task detail panel shows a readiness determination for tasks that have dependencies:

✓ Ready to start — all dependencies are ready, work can begin immediately.
● Blocked by  — at least one dependency is not yet complete or cannot be resolved.

The determination is fail-closed: incomplete dependency data, cycles, or ambiguous references are all treated as blocked, never guessed. The same determination appears in the Web task detail Dependencies card, the Web task detail status badge, backlog task list --ready, and the MCP task_list ready: true parameter. It is for display and filtering only; it does not modify tasks or change ordering.
Hide Empty Status Columns
The board can hide status columns that currently contain no tasks, reducing visual clutter:

Uses the shared configuration key hide_empty_columns (the same switch as the Web interface).
When toggled inside the board, the UI reflects the change immediately (optimistic update) and writes the configuration asynchronously.
When exiting the TUI, it waits for pending writes to finish so the configuration is not lost.
All status columns remain visible during drag / move operations so they can serve as valid drop targets.

Window Title
When entering the TUI, the terminal window title is updated to include the project name; the original title is restored on exit. Title push/pop is strictly paired and works correctly in nested terminals such as tmux by passing through the escape sequences.
Key Hint Convention
Key hints in the bottom footer and help panel consistently use uppercase letters for pressable keys (for example N to create, E to edit, M to move), avoiding confusion from mixed-case labels. Footer text is centralized as constants to prevent wording drift between views.
Plain-Text Fallback in Non-Terminal Environments
When backlog board runs in a non-TTY environment (such as a CI pipeline, script pipe, or IDE integrated terminal), it automatically falls back to plain-text output, printing a structured Markdown board table instead of launching the interactive interface:
# Check board status in CI
backlog board > board-status.md

The plain-text output includes the project name, timestamp, task lists for each status column, and metadata such as assignees and labels, making it easy to archive or share by email.
Running Multiple Views at the Same Time
backlog board and backlog browser can run in parallel. The terminal board is good for quickly checking status while focused on coding; the Web interface is better for detailed editing and drag-and-drop operations. Both share the same data.

20-看板与可视化/01-Web看板.html.title: Web Board
20-看板与可视化/01-Web看板.html.body:
Web Board
Run backlog browser to start the browser-based visual task-management interface. The Web board is built with React + Tailwind CSS v4 and supports drag-and-drop, milestone swimlanes, label filtering, and real-time sync. It is the preferred tool for team collaborators and users who prefer a graphical interface.
Starting the Web Interface
# Default startup: port 6420, opens the system default browser automatically
backlog browser

# Use a custom port
backlog browser --port 8080

# Start without automatically opening the browser (good for remote servers or background use)
backlog browser --no-open

After startup, the terminal prints the service address, for example http://localhost:6420. Press Ctrl+C (or Cmd+C) to stop the service.

Tip: You can change the default behavior through the autoOpenBrowser and defaultPort configuration values; see the Configuration Management chapter.

Board View
After opening the Web interface, you enter the board view by default. The interface is divided into columns by status, each showing task cards for that status:
Drag-and-Drop

Move across columns: Hold a task card and drag it to the target status column to change the task status.
Reorder: Drag a card up or down within the same column to adjust its displayed order on the board.
Undo support: All drag-and-drop operations are written to the Markdown files in real time and can be traced back through Git.

Milestone Swimlanes
When the milestone view is enabled, the board groups task cards by milestone inside each column. Tasks belonging to the same milestone cluster together, forming clear horizontal swimlanes that make it easy to track progress by iteration or version.
Label Filtering
A label filter dropdown at the top of the board lets you check the labels you want; the board instantly filters to show only tasks with matching labels. Multi-label combination filtering is supported.
All Tasks View
Click "All Tasks" in the navigation bar to switch to a table layout:

Supports multi-dimensional filtering by status, priority, label, and milestone.
Click table headers to sort.
The search box at the top is a trigger button: click it or press Ctrl+K / Cmd+K to open the global search dialog (Fuse.js fuzzy matching, results grouped by type, keyword and ID highlighted).

Gantt Chart View
Click "Gantt" in the navigation bar to enter the timeline visualization page:

Two-column layout: task list on the left, timeline on the right.
Five time granularities (day / week / month / quarter / year).
Automatically parses task start/end times (plannedStart / plannedEnd / createdDate).
Task dependencies are visualized with SVG arrows.
Supports dragging to pan the timeline.

See the Gantt Chart View chapter for details.
Milestone Management Page
The "Milestones" page in the navigation bar provides full milestone lifecycle management:

Create milestone: Click the "Add Milestone" button and enter a name.
Milestone details: Each milestone card shows the number of assigned tasks and completion progress.
Drag-and-drop assignment: Drag tasks from the unassigned pool to a target milestone, or remove them in the opposite direction.
Completion detection: When all tasks under a milestone enter the Done status, the system automatically marks the milestone as completed.
Completed milestones: By default, completed milestones are collapsed at the bottom of the page to reduce visual clutter.

Documents & Decisions
The Web interface also provides read-only browsing of the project knowledge base:

Document list: Groups and displays all documents under backlog/docs/ by subfolder; click a title to view the rendered Markdown content.
Decision records: Displays ADR decisions from backlog/decisions/, including status labels and creation time.

Real-Time Updates
The Web server broadcasts file changes to all connected clients through WebSocket:

After modifying a task with backlog task edit in the terminal, the browser board refreshes automatically within about one second.
When editing a task in the Web interface, if another user or process modifies the same file at the same time, the interface merges changes intelligently to avoid overwriting.
Draft preservation: content that is being edited but not yet saved is kept after a file refresh and is not lost.

Dark Mode and Responsiveness
The Web interface follows the system theme for dark mode and also supports manual switching. The layout is responsive for desktop and mobile:

Desktop: multi-column board side by side, suitable for large screens.
Mobile: single-column stacked layout, supporting touch swiping and long-press dragging.

Mermaid Diagrams and Attachments
If task Markdown contains Mermaid syntax, the Web interface renders it as flowcharts, sequence diagrams, or Gantt charts. Images and attachments in the backlog/assets/ directory can be previewed directly in task details through relative paths.

20-看板与可视化/02-看板导出.html.title: Board Export
20-看板与可视化/02-看板导出.html.body:
Board Export
The board export feature generates a static Markdown snapshot of the current project state, making it easy to embed in README files, email reports, or archive in version control.
Export as Markdown Table
# Export to the default file Backlog.md
backlog board export

# Export to a specific file
backlog board export project-status.md

# Force overwrite an existing file
backlog board export --force

The exported file contains:

Project title and export timestamp
Version label (if --export-version is provided)
Markdown tables grouped by status, each row showing task ID, title, assignee, and labels
Metadata summary: task counts per status and completion percentage


Subtasks are listed under their parent with a └─ prefix; deeper descendant tasks (such as subtasks of subtasks) are also listed recursively in ID order and are not omitted.
Note: The default export destination is Backlog.md in the project root. If the file already exists and --force is not used, the command prompts for confirmation before overwriting.

Embed in README.md
To display the board status directly on the repository home page, use the --readme flag:
backlog board export --readme

This command looks for the board marker placeholders in README.md:



When found, it inserts the current board table between the two markers. If the markers do not exist in README.md, the command prompts you to add them manually.
This feature is commonly used in open-source projects so visitors can see the current iteration progress at a glance.
Export Version Label
At release points or when a milestone is completed, you can attach version information to the export:
# Simple version number
backlog board export --export-version "v1.2.3"

# Combined: embed in README and label the version
backlog board export --readme --export-version "Release 2024.12.1-beta"

The version string appears below the export table title, making it easy to distinguish from historical export records.
Automated Export Example
Integrate board export in CI/CD or release scripts:
# Automatically update the README board before a release
backlog board export --readme --force --export-version "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"
git add README.md Backlog.md
git commit -m "chore: update board snapshot"


Tip: Because backlog board export is a read-only operation, it can run safely in CI environments that do not have write access. If you need to commit the result, make sure the pipeline has the appropriate Git credentials configured.

30-文档与决策/00-文档管理.html.title: Document Management
30-文档与决策/00-文档管理.html.body:
Document Management
Backlog.md treats project documents as first-class citizens. All documents are stored as Markdown files under backlog/docs/, support nested subfolders, a global ID index, and full CLI lifecycle operations.
Creating Documents
# Minimal creation
backlog doc create "API Design Guide"

# Specify document type
backlog doc create "Architecture Decision Description" -t guide

# Create in a subdirectory
backlog doc create "Deployment Manual" -p guides/deployment

After creation, the CLI prints the generated file path, for example backlog/docs/guides/deployment/doc-5 - Deployment Manual.md. The document ID (such as doc-5) is globally unique across the entire backlog/docs/ tree; you can view and update it by ID regardless of which subfolder it lives in.

doc create also accepts the --plain flag. Creation output is already plain text; the flag is accepted (rather than switching output formats) so that agent invocations that habitually append --plain to every command do not fail with "unknown option".

Subpath Rules

Paths are always relative to the backlog/docs/ directory; do not write absolute paths.
Multi-level nesting is supported, for example -p guides/deployment/aws.
.. and absolute paths are not allowed; the system rejects attempts to escape the directory.

Updating Documents
# Update document content
backlog doc update doc-5 --content "## Deployment Steps\n\n1. Build image\n2. Push to registry"

# Update title, type, and labels at the same time
backlog doc update doc-5 --title "Production Deployment Manual" -t runbook --tags deploy,aws

# Move to a new subdirectory
backlog doc update doc-5 -p guides/production

backlog doc update uses incremental updates: provide only the fields you want to change; fields you omit keep their original values. For example, if you only pass --title, the document content and path are not affected.
Multi-Line Content and Appending
--content supports \n newline escapes, consistent with task --desc, --plan, and --notes:
backlog doc update doc-5 --content "## Overview\n\nFirst paragraph\nSecond paragraph"

To append a block while preserving existing content, use the repeatable --append-content option. The appended block is separated from the base content by a blank line, and can be combined with --content (the append is placed after the replaced content):
# Append a section to the end of an existing document
backlog doc update doc-5 --append-content "## Appendix\n\nSupplementary notes"

# Replace then append
backlog doc update doc-5 --content "New content" --append-content "Appendix section"

The MCP document_update tool provides a matching appendContent parameter.
Listing Documents
backlog doc list

In TTY terminals, this command opens a dual-pane interactive browser: the left pane lists Documents (N) and the right pane renders the Markdown content of the selected document in real time. ← / → switch focus between panes, ↑ / ↓ (or j / k) navigate or scroll within the current pane, Enter opens the full viewer, ? opens the help popup, and q exits. The active pane border is highlighted in yellow and returns to normal when focus is lost. --plain, --json, and non-TTY environments still output a list text, unchanged.
The command scans backlog/docs/ and all subdirectories, printing the ID, title, type, and path of every document. When there are many documents, combine paging windows and fuzzy search:
# Paging window: first 20 / next page / total count only
backlog doc list --max-count 20
backlog doc list --max-count 20 --skip 20
backlog doc list --count

backlog search "deployment"

The paging options (--max-count / --skip / --count) have the same semantics as the eight list commands such as search and task list; see the "List Paging" section in Search & Sequences. Search covers tasks, documents, and decision records (memo and Wiki results are in the Web global search).
Viewing Documents
# Interactive view (TUI popup renders Markdown)
backlog doc view doc-5

# Plain-text output (good for AI agents or scripts)
backlog doc view doc-5 --plain

The --plain flag outputs raw Markdown content plus frontmatter metadata, making it easy to read in pipelines or chat windows.
Reference Forms and Ambiguity Handling
doc view accepts three reference forms and tries them in order:



Form
Example
Description




Bare ID
doc-5
Default form; directly resolves when the ID is unique across the backlog/docs/ tree


Document-relative path
migration/doc-14
Omit the .md extension; also supports folder/ID-filename form


Filename title slug
Deployment Manual
The title part after ID - in the filename, case-insensitive



Identity resolution is fail-closed: when the same ID appears in different subdirectories (for example guide/doc-1 - A.md and migration/doc-1 - B.md), the bare ID immediately fails and lists all candidate paths (exit code 1) rather than picking one. The error message includes runnable disambiguation suggestions—folder/ID when the candidate is unique, otherwise the full path (auto-quoted when it contains spaces). Path forms reject .. escapes and drive-letter prefixes; matching multiple files also errors.
Related behaviors:

Documents or decisions that lack an id frontmatter still appear in lists but cannot be addressed by ID.
The Web interface shows a dedicated hint for ambiguous IDs (server returns HTTP 409 plus the candidate list) and does not fall back to stale cached entries.
MCP returns an AMBIGUOUS_ID error and includes candidate paths in the structured content.

Backlinks
The document page (right pane of the CLI doc view interactive browser, and the Web document detail page) displays a backlinks list showing which tasks, documents, decisions, or Wiki pages reference the current document:

The index is built on the client (buildBacklinkIndex) and refreshes live as content changes; it never writes back to files.
Each backlink shows the source type icon, title, and ID; click to open the source in the current view.
Sources that match multiple IDs are collapsed into a dropdown selector to avoid drowning the page in long lists.

Backlinks are a read-only navigation aid and do not affect document content or dependency resolution.
Live SQL Query Blocks
Documents (shared with tasks, decisions, memos, and Wiki pages) can embed sqlite-query and duckdb-query fenced code blocks. The Web reading view renders these blocks as live read-only query results against the real database file (the editing view still shows the original source):
```sqlite-query
source: backlog/databases/shop.sqlite
view: table
sql: |
  SELECT product, price, stock
  FROM inventory
  ORDER BY price DESC
```

Block fields (minimal YAML subset):



Field
Required
Default
Description




source
Yes
—
Project-relative path to the database (no leading /, absolute paths, or .. escapes). SQLite supports .sqlite / .sqlite3 / .db; DuckDB supports .duckdb (later expanded to .csv / .xlsx).


sql
Yes
—
Query statement; must be read-only (must start with SELECT or WITH … SELECT; write keywords are rejected, and a read-only handle is used as a physical safeguard).


view
No
table
Display mode: table (grid), list (vertical key-value list), value (first row and first cell only), echarts (render a chart directly; see Chart Blocks).


refresh
No
manual
Manual refresh only; automatic / scheduled refresh is not supported.



By default results are limited to 500 rows; the cap is configured by query_max_rows in config.yml. If the limit is exceeded, the block shows a truncation notice. Pagination can be enabled in the block header; paging is pushed down to the engine via LIMIT / OFFSET and is not constrained by the preview cap. The block header provides four actions: Refresh (rerun against the current disk state), Show / Hide Query (expand/collapse the read-only source + SQL, collapsed by default), Copy Markdown (serialize the current results as a GFM table to the clipboard), and Export CSV (rerun on the server and generate a CSV saved to the user's chosen location). If the safe-path check fails or the query errors, the error is rendered inside the block and does not affect the rest of the page.
Query blocks can also render charts directly (view: echarts), or be referenced by standalone charts via fromQuery; see Chart Blocks for the full flowchart and data-chart usage.
Document Organization Recommendations
As the project evolves, files under backlog/docs/ will grow. The following directory structure is recommended to keep things clear:
backlog/docs/
├── readme.md              # docs directory overview
├── api/
│   ├── doc-1 - REST-Standards.md
│   └── doc-2 - GraphQL-Schema.md
├── guides/
│   ├── doc-3 - Local-Development.md
│   └── doc-4 - Deployment-Process.md
└── runbooks/
    └── doc-5 - Troubleshooting.md

Tip: backlog doc list and backlog doc view automatically traverse all subdirectories. When document IDs are globally unique, you only need to remember the ID; if the same ID exists in different subdirectories, disambiguate with folder/ID (for example migration/doc-14) or the title slug. When ambiguous, the command lists all candidate paths.

30-文档与决策/01-决策记录.html.title: Decision Records
30-文档与决策/01-决策记录.html.body:
Decision Records
Decision records (Architecture Decision Records, ADRs) track key technology and design choices in a project. Backlog.md supports the ADR format natively. Each decision is stored as a Markdown file in backlog/decisions/, including status metadata and full context.
Creating Decision Records
# Default status is proposed
backlog decision create "Use PostgreSQL as the primary database"

# Specify the status at creation time
backlog decision create "Migrate to TypeScript" -s accepted

After creation, the system generates a file such as decision-3 - Migrate-to-TypeScript.md under backlog/decisions/. The file frontmatter includes a status field that identifies the decision's current lifecycle stage.
Status Flow
Decision records support five standard statuses that reflect the full lifecycle from proposal to retirement:



Status
Meaning




proposed
Proposed, pending discussion or review


accepted
Accepted, becomes the current project standard


rejected
Rejected, the option is not adopted


deprecated
Previously accepted but now obsolete


superseded
Replaced by a newer decision



There are two ways to change status:
# Change only the status; the body is preserved byte-for-byte
backlog decision update decision-3 --status accepted

# Change status and append content in the same commit
backlog decision update decision-3 --status superseded --append-content "## Supplement\n\nSuperseded by decision-7"

--status accepts free text; the convention values are proposed / accepted / rejected / superseded. An explicitly passed status takes precedence over the frontmatter value. You can also edit the decision file frontmatter directly, or edit it in the Web interface decision detail page (see Documents & Decisions). On the MCP side, the decision_update tool provides content / appendContent / status parameters. It is recommended to record the reason and time of status changes in the body to keep the audit trail complete.
Listing Decisions
backlog decision list

The output includes the ID, title, and current status of all decisions. Completed decisions (accepted, rejected, deprecated, superseded) are usually shown alongside active ones for quick reference to historical choices.
In TTY terminals, this command opens a dual-pane interactive browser: the left pane lists Decisions (N) and the right pane renders the raw Markdown of the selected decision in real time. ← / → switch focus between panes, ↑ / ↓ (or j / k) navigate or scroll within the current pane, Enter opens the full viewer, ? opens the help popup, and q exits. The active pane border is highlighted in yellow.
# Plain-text output (good for scripts)
backlog decision list --plain

# Paging window: at most n / skip n / total count only
backlog decision list --max-count 20
backlog decision list --max-count 20 --skip 20
backlog decision list --count

# Structured JSON output (versioned envelope kind: "decision-list")
backlog decision list --json

Non-TTY environments fall back to plain-text output by default; when the decision log is empty it prints No decisions found..
Decision listing is also exposed through MCP: the decision_list tool supports limit / offset / status / search filtering and returns a unified { items, total, offset, limit, hasMore } paging envelope. See MCP Workflow for details.
Viewing Decisions
backlog decision view decision-3

In TTY environments this opens a scrollable interactive viewer by default (PageUp / PageDown / Home / End are available; mouse tracking is disabled on Windows to avoid hanging PowerShell / VS Code). In non-TTY environments it falls back to --plain output of frontmatter and Markdown body.
When a single ID matches multiple files, the command prints all candidate paths and fails with exit code 1 rather than picking one (the same fail-closed identity rule as documents).
Updating Decisions
# Replace the decision body
backlog decision update decision-3 --content "## Context\n\nUpdated context description"

# Append a section (repeatable; preserves existing body)
backlog decision update decision-3 --append-content "## Supplement\n\nNew considerations"

decision update reuses structured section parsing (Context / Decision / Consequences / Alternatives). Both --content and --append-content support the same \n newline escapes as other commands; status is changed via --status (see previous section). The three options can be used individually or in combination.
ADR Format Overview
Generated decision files follow the standard ADR structure:
---
status: proposed
date: 2026-05-07
---

# Migrate to TypeScript

## Context

The project currently uses JavaScript. As the codebase grows, type-safety issues become more prominent ...

## Decision

Migrate fully to TypeScript with strict mode enabled.

## Consequences

- Positive: compile-time type checking, better IDE support, fewer runtime errors
- Negative: initial migration cost, team learning curve

Field Descriptions

status: Current status of the decision, required.
date: Creation date, auto-generated.
Context: Describes the problem background and constraints.
Decision: States the decision clearly.
Consequences: Lists positive and negative effects of the decision.

Linking to Tasks and Documents
When creating or editing a task, you can link a related decision with the --doc option:
backlog task create "Upgrade build tool to Vite" --doc decision-3

This lets you jump directly to the decision context from the board or task detail, avoiding repeated discussion of decisions that are already settled.
Backlinks
The decision page (right pane of the CLI decision view interactive browser, and the Web decision detail page) displays a backlinks list showing which tasks, documents, decisions, or Wiki pages reference the current decision:

The index is built on the client (buildBacklinkIndex) and refreshes live as content changes; it never writes back to files.
Each backlink shows the source type icon, title, and ID; click to open the source in the current view.
Sources that match multiple IDs are collapsed into a dropdown selector.

Backlinks are a read-only navigation aid and do not affect decision content or status flow.
Best Practices

Record promptly: Create a decision record within 24 hours after a technical discussion ends so details are not forgotten.
Keep it focused: Each decision addresses one issue; avoid mixing unrelated choices in the same file.
Be transparent about status: Once a decision is superseded or deprecated, update its status to superseded or deprecated and reference the replacement in the body.
Review regularly: Run backlog decision list each quarter to check for decisions that have remained in proposed for too long, and drive them to closure.

30-文档与决策/02-里程碑管理.html.title: Milestone Management
30-文档与决策/02-里程碑管理.html.body:
Milestone Management
Milestones group tasks by iteration, version, or release cycle and are the core tool for tracking phase progress and planning roadmaps. Backlog.md stores milestone data as Markdown files in backlog/milestones/, under version control alongside task files.
Creating Milestones
Milestones can be created through the CLI, Web interface, or MCP.
CLI Creation
backlog milestone add "M3 - Web UI"

# Set description, dates, and linked documents in one command
backlog milestone add "M3 - Web UI" \
  --description "UI and interaction goals for this phase" \
  --due-date 2026-07-31 --planned-start 2026-07-01 --planned-end 2026-07-25 \
  --doc doc-5 --doc doc-8

--doc can be repeated to link multiple documents; empty values are rejected. created_date is written automatically on creation.
Web Interface Creation

Start the Web interface with backlog browser.
Click "Milestones" in the navigation bar to enter the milestone management page.
Click the "Add Milestone" button and enter the milestone name (for example M3 - Web UI).
The description field supports Markdown editing, Mermaid preview, and paste-upload images (images are automatically promoted to paste/ before saving).
Click save; the system generates the corresponding milestone file under backlog/milestones/.


Tip: AI agents can create milestones directly through the MCP milestone_add tool without opening the browser.

Editing Milestones
Edit a milestone's title, description, and date fields through the CLI:
backlog milestone edit M1 --title "M1 - Core CLI" --description "Phase 1 goals" \
  --due-date 2026-06-30 --planned-start 2026-05-01 --planned-end 2026-06-15 \
  --actual-start "2026-05-01 09:00" --actual-end "2026-06-10 18:00"

# Clear date fields
backlog milestone edit M1 --clear-due-date --clear-planned-end --clear-actual-start


Milestones can be located by title or ID (fuzzy matching).
Planned fields (dueDate / plannedStart / plannedEnd) use the format YYYY-MM-DD.
Actual fields (actualStart / actualEnd) use the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (UTC).
Passing an empty string clears the corresponding field.

Milestones also support document links consistent with tasks:
# Overwrite linked documents
backlog milestone edit M1 --doc doc-5

# Append / remove by value / clear
backlog milestone edit M1 --add-doc doc-8
backlog milestone edit M1 --remove-doc doc-5
backlog milestone edit M1 --clear-docs

--doc (set) and --add-doc (append) are mutually exclusive in the same command, and --clear-docs cannot be combined with other document flags; the rules are identical to task list-type fields. Adding or removing document links is a substantive change and refreshes updated_date.
Milestone Date Editing in the Web UI
Click a milestone card on the milestone management page to open the edit popup:

Due Date / Planned Start / Planned End — date inputs.
Actual Start / Actual End — datetime-local inputs.
Documentation — linked document entries can be previewed directly inside the popup: local (non-URL) entries open an in-app file preview (shared with the task popup) when you click the preview control; http(s) entries remain external links that open in a new tab. The preview resets automatically when switching milestones and does not persist after the popup closes.

A milestone's actualStart / actualEnd are automatically driven by status changes of its child tasks:

When any task under the milestone changes to In Progress, if actualStart is empty it is automatically set to the current date and time.
When the last non-terminal task under the milestone changes to Done, if actualEnd is empty it is automatically set to the current date and time.
You can override these auto-filled values manually at any time.

Milestone List and Details
View all milestones and their completion status in the terminal:
backlog milestone list

Example output:
Active milestones (2):
  m-1: M1 - CLI (8/12 done)
  m-2: M2 - MCP Support (3/5 done)

Completed milestones (1):
  (collapsed, use --show-completed to list)
Each milestone shows the ratio of completed tasks to total tasks, making progress clear at a glance.

Milestone ID display style: Milestone IDs are uniformly displayed in uppercase M-N form across all interfaces, aligned with the TASK-9 style for task IDs—the Web list and detail popup use an em dash (M-9 — Title), while the TUI milestone row and CLI milestone list --plain section headings use a hyphen (M-9 - Title, ## M-9 - Title (n tasks)). This is a display-layer change only; storage format and alias resolution (m-2, 2, M2, etc.) are unaffected.

Viewing Completed Milestones
By default, completed milestones are collapsed to reduce noise. To expand them:
backlog milestone list --show-completed

Plain-text output (good for scripts):
backlog milestone list --plain

# Paging window: unit is milestone
backlog milestone list --max-count 10
backlog milestone list --max-count 10 --skip 10
backlog milestone list --count

--plain output is a Markdown grouped board fully consistent with backlog board -m: first the "No Milestone" section, then sections by milestone file order, with tasks grouped under ###  (count) subheadings. Tasks in the completed directory are excluded by default; --show-completed includes them. Empty status columns are automatically narrowed.
TUI Milestone Board
Run backlog milestones in a TTY to enter the interactive milestone board: the left pane lists milestones (Space to restrict scope, Enter to view metadata, N to create), and the right pane is an embedded task board. The milestone detail popup supports pressing E to edit dates and description. See TUI Board for details.
Assigning Tasks to Milestones
There are three ways to assign a task to a milestone:
1. Specify at Task Creation
backlog task create "Implement board drag-and-drop" -m "M2 - MCP Support"

The -m option supports fuzzy matching; the system automatically finds the closest milestone. You can also use the milestone ID (such as m-2) or a plain number (such as 2).
2. Edit an Existing Task
backlog task edit 7 --milestone "M2 - MCP Support"

3. Filter the Task List by Milestone ID
In the milestone filter of backlog task list, you can locate milestones in several forms:
# Numeric alias
backlog task list -m 2

# Canonical ID
backlog task list -m m-2

# Case variants
backlog task list -m "M2"

# Exact or partial title match
backlog task list -m "MCP Support"

Filter parsing supports numeric aliases, canonical IDs (m-N), case variants, and titles with punctuation. Behavior is consistent across the CLI, interactive task list, and MCP task_list active/draft paths. If the query matches no milestone, an empty list is returned.
4. Clear Milestone Assignment
backlog task edit 7 --clear-milestone

5. Web Interface Drag-and-Drop Assignment
On the Web milestone management page, the "Unassigned task pool" shows all tasks without a milestone. Drag a task card onto a target milestone card to assign it; drag in the opposite direction to remove it.
Milestone Completion Detection and Archiving
Automatic Completion Detection
When all tasks under a milestone enter the Done status, the system automatically marks the milestone as completed. In backlog milestone list, it moves from the "Active milestones" area to the "Completed milestones" area.
Archiving Milestones
Completed milestones that remain in the active list for a long time accumulate noise. You can archive them:
backlog milestone archive "M1 - CLI"

After archiving:

The milestone is removed from the active milestone list.
Its tasks automatically become "unassigned" (the tasks themselves are not deleted; only the milestone binding is removed).
The file is moved into the archive area and its ID no longer participates in fuzzy matching.

Archiving supports locating the milestone by title or ID:
backlog milestone archive m-1
backlog milestone archive 1

Archiving does not modify any task files—tasks keep their reference to the milestone. If you want to clear or reassign the milestone field on tasks at the same time, use remove (see next section).
created_date and updated_date
Milestones automatically maintain two timestamps, just like tasks:

created_date: written at creation time (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM).
updated_date: refreshed only on substantive changes—pure ordering adjustments do not refresh it, but adding or removing document links does.

backlog milestone list appends (updated ...) after each entry (falling back to (created ...) when there is no update record); MCP milestone_list shows Created: / Updated: labels. Historical files missing these fields do not cause errors; display falls back to created_date. The Web interface shows "Last updated" on milestone cards and "Created / Updated" in the detail popup header.
Removing a Milestone (remove)
In addition to archive, there is remove. Both move the milestone file into the archive directory; the difference is whether task files' milestone fields are processed:
# Default: clear the milestone field on matching tasks
backlog milestone remove "Release 1.0"

# Keep task milestone references
backlog milestone remove "Release 1.0" --task-handling keep

# Reassign to another active milestone
backlog milestone remove "Release 1.0" --task-handling reassign --reassign-to "Release 2.0"




Operation
Milestone file
Task files




archive
Moved to archive
Not modified; tasks keep their reference to the milestone


remove --task-handling keep
Moved to archive
Not modified


remove --task-handling clear (default)
Moved to archive
Clear the milestone field on matching tasks


remove --task-handling reassign
Moved to archive
Reassign to the active milestone specified by --reassign-to



Unassigned Task Pool
Tasks that do not belong to any active milestone form the "unassigned task pool". On the Web milestone page these tasks are shown together at the top of the page, making it easy to:

Quickly review work items that have not yet been included in iteration planning.
Batch drag-and-drop them to the right milestone.
Identify omissions or tasks that need to be rescheduled.

In the terminal, unassigned tasks are not shown in backlog milestone list, but you can view them through filtering:
backlog task list --milestone ""

Grouping the Board by Milestone
Both the TUI board and Web board support milestone grouping mode:
# TUI board displays milestone swimlanes
backlog board --milestones

In this mode the board no longer only groups by status; instead, tasks in each column are arranged in horizontal swimlanes by milestone, helping you visually compare remaining work across iterations.

40-Web界面/00-启动与访问.html.title: Launch & Access
40-Web界面/00-启动与访问.html.body:
Startup & Access
Backlog.md includes a modern Web interface for intuitively managing tasks, boards, milestones, and documents in the browser. Start it with the backlog browser command.
Starting the Web Server
Open a terminal, enter the Backlog.md project directory, and run:
backlog browser

The server binds to 127.0.0.1 (loopback) by default and automatically opens the interface in the default browser after starting. The console prints something like:
🚀 Backlog Web UI running at http://localhost:6420
By default it only listens to local requests; other devices on the same network cannot access it directly.
Command-Line Options
Specifying a Port
If the default port 6420 is already in use, specify another port with --port:
backlog browser --port 8080

After startup, open http://localhost:8080 in the browser.
Automatic Port Fallback
By default (config item autoPort: true), if the default port is occupied, the server automatically scans for the next available port and prints the real address in the console. You do not need to specify one manually, and it will not exit with an error:
🚀 Backlog Web UI running at http://localhost:6421
Automatic scanning only accepts ports in the user port range (1024–65535) and refuses random high ports assigned by the OS for ephemeral use. If autoPort is set to false, a port conflict will produce an EADDRINUSE error (use --port to specify one explicitly). This switch can also be toggled in the Web interface "Settings" panel.
Disable Auto-Open
If you do not want the browser window to pop up automatically (for example on a remote server or in a CI environment), add --no-open:
backlog browser --no-open

In this case, copy the address printed in the console and open it manually.
Specifying the Bind Host
By default the Web server binds only to 127.0.0.1, which is suitable for local development. To allow access from other devices on the LAN, use --host:
# Listen on all interfaces (open LAN access)
backlog browser --host 0.0.0.0

When binding to a wildcard, the console prints the specific LAN IPv4 address and notes that the API is currently unauthenticated. The browser automatically opens the first available LAN address. You can also bind to a specific network interface:
backlog browser --host 192.168.1.100

Using a Custom Browser
In devcontainers or containers without a default browser, you can specify the launch command via the BROWSER environment variable:
BROWSER=/usr/bin/chromium backlog browser

BROWSER is treated as a single executable path (surrounding quotes are stripped; it is not split or shell-evaluated), and the URL is passed as a separate argument. When unset, the platform default is used: open (macOS), cmd /c start (Windows), xdg-open (Linux).
Combining Options
backlog browser --port 3000 --no-open
BROWSER=/usr/bin/chromium backlog browser --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

Technical Features
The Web interface is built with the following technologies for a smooth experience:

React: component-based interactive UI with no full-page reloads.
Tailwind CSS v4: modern styling system with a clean, consistent look.
Responsive layout: automatically adapts to desktop and mobile screen sizes.
Dark mode: follows the system theme automatically, or can be switched manually between light and dark.

Real-Time Sync
The Web interface stays in sync with local Markdown files:

Changes to task status or content in the browser are written back to the corresponding Markdown files.
Changes made in external editors (such as VS Code or Vim) are reflected in the Web interface instantly.
No manual refresh is needed; all views update in real time via WebSocket.

Interface Layout
The Web interface uses a classic left-right layout:

Left sidebar: fixed width, showing the navigation menu and file tree.
Right content area: takes the remaining space, showing tasks, boards, documents, or Wiki content.

Adjusting Sidebar Width
The right edge of the sidebar is a full-height draggable handle. Hover over it until the cursor becomes a left-right arrow, then drag to adjust the sidebar width. While dragging, a blue ghost bar previews the final position; releasing the mouse applies the width immediately and saves it to browser local storage (localStorage) so it is restored next time.

Minimum width is 200px, preventing the sidebar from becoming invisible.
Maximum width is 500px, avoiding excessive use of content area space.

Collapsing the Sidebar
A collapse/expand button (arrow icon) is located on the right side of the sidebar. Click it to collapse the sidebar to a narrow icon-only mode; click again to expand. Collapse state and width settings are both saved to localStorage.
Stopping the Server
Press Ctrl + C in the terminal running backlog browser to stop the Web server. All saved changes have already been written to the filesystem, so no data is lost.
Loading Indicators
Loading feedback in the Web interface has two layers:

Initial load: the board area shows a skeleton screen that matches the real column layout (breathing-animation ghost columns), with a loading spinner in the center. The uninitialized-project waiting screen also shows a loading spinner.
Background indexing: while background work such as cross-branch indexing runs, a status chip appears in the header on the right (showing the current stage text; hover for full details), and a sweeping progress bar runs below the header. The already-loaded board and tree remain interactive and are not covered by the skeleton screen.

Loading animations still play when the system has "reduce motion" enabled—loading progress is essential feedback rather than decoration; a static spinner is easily mistaken for a freeze on remote desktops and virtual machines.
Running as a Persistent Service
backlog browser --no-open starts only the service without opening the browser, making it suitable for registering as a startup persistent service (doc-003). Key point: one independent service and port per project, and the working directory must point to the project root.

Linux (systemd user service): create ~/.config/systemd/user/backlog-browser-.service with ExecStart set to backlog browser --no-open --port  and Restart=on-failure; run loginctl enable-linger so it starts on boot without a login session. For many projects, use a template unit backlog-browser@.service.
macOS (launchd): place a uniquely labeled plist in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ with RunAtLoad and KeepAlive. Note that Apple Silicon and Intel binaries are at /opt/homebrew/bin/backlog and /usr/local/bin/backlog respectively.
Windows: use Task Scheduler (New-ScheduledTaskAction, triggered by -AtLogOn) for login startup. For always-on service without a logged-in user, wrap it with NSSM as a real Windows service to get automatic restart.

40-Web界面/01-看板视图.html.title: Board View
40-Web界面/01-看板视图.html.body:
Board View
The board view displays tasks in a column layout, giving an intuitive picture of each task's current status. You can change task status by dragging and dropping cards, without opening the task detail page.
Entering the Board Page
After starting the Web interface, click the "Board" tab in the top navigation bar to enter the board view. The page shows columns grouped by task status by default.
Asynchronous Loading Indicator
The board page uses a bind-first startup: the browser UI immediately shows a skeleton screen and loading-stage text (such as scanning tasks, building index), then renders real content after Core corpus initialization finishes in the background. If an error occurs during initialization, the page shows a retryable error panel; clicking it reloads. The sidebar stays mounted during loading; only the task count is in a loading state.
Hide Empty Status Columns
When a project uses 5+ statuses but most tasks are concentrated in a few, the board can become cluttered with empty columns. You can enable Hide empty status columns in the settings panel (or via hide_empty_columns in config.yml): after enabling, status columns that currently have no tasks are automatically hidden, so the board only shows columns with at least one task.

All status columns remain visible while dragging a task so it can be dropped into any target column. Empty columns are hidden again after the drag ends.

Drag-and-Drop to Change Task Status
The board page groups tasks by status. Common columns include:

Todo — tasks to do
In Progress — tasks in progress
Done — completed tasks

Hover over a task card, hold the left mouse button, drag it to the target status column, and release. The task status is updated automatically, and the change is synced to the corresponding Markdown file in real time.

During dragging, the target column highlights to show the drop area.

Drag-and-Drop Behavior Details

Preserves column order: if the current column has been manually sorted (for example by ID descending), the visual order stays stable during the drag and does not reorder under the cursor.
Precise cross-column placement: when dropping a task into the target column, you can place it between any two existing cards. The system inserts the task at the visual position where you release the mouse, rather than simply appending it to the end.
Cross-column sort recovery: after a task is placed across columns, the target column's manual sort is automatically cleared and restored to default ordinal ordering, ensuring the new task appears in the right place.

Milestone Swimlanes
If the project has milestones, the board page supports swimlanes grouped by milestone. Find the milestone filter or view-toggle control at the top of the page and click "Group by milestone".
Each milestone expands into a horizontal swimlane, with tasks inside the swimlane grouped by status columns. This view makes it easy to track the progress of a specific milestone.
Label Filtering
A label filter dropdown is provided at the top of the page. Click the dropdown, check the labels you want to filter by, and the board will show only tasks that have any of the selected labels.

Supports multi-select labels; a task only needs to match one selected label to be shown.
Uncheck labels or click "Clear filters" to restore the full task list.

Custom Label Colors
Each label has a small colored square (color swatch) on the right; click it to open a color picker and set a custom color for the label.

Preset palette: 17 preset colors that adapt automatically to light/dark mode.
Persistence: non-default color configurations are saved to the label_colors field in backlog/config.yml and remain effective after restarting the service.
Restore default: choose "Default" and save to revert to the system default gray.
Card rendering: labels on board task cards show the configured background color; unconfigured labels keep the default gray.


Label color configuration is stored per project; different projects can have different label color schemes.

Task Card Labels
Each task card bottom shows that task's label list.

Width adaptation: the card dynamically calculates how many labels fit in the available width, showing as many as possible; extras are collapsed as +N.
Real-time response: when the window or sidebar width is adjusted, the number of displayed labels is recalculated automatically.
Label colors: labels with custom colors are shown with the corresponding background color.

Task Card Acceptance Criteria Progress
For tasks in In Progress that contain acceptance criteria (AC), the card title row shows a rounded progress bar and a checked/total count (such as 2/4). The progress bar and task ID are laid out in the same flex row:

Progress is calculated live from acceptance criteria and is not persisted as a separate field.
Tasks without acceptance criteria show no progress indicator.
After all acceptance criteria are checked, the task remains in In Progress and must be dragged to the Done column to complete.
The progress bar uses emerald fill with a gray track; contrast against the card background is guaranteed in both light and dark themes.

The task list view shows the same progress indicator in the title column (a fixed 80px-wide progress bar for consistent row height).
Show Completed Tasks
The filter bar in both board and task list provides a "Show completed" checkbox:

When checked, completed records in backlog/completed/ are shown alongside active tasks through the same filtering, sorting, and grouping pipeline; cards and list rows are marked with a "Completed" badge.
The checked state is synced to the address bar (completed=1), so it can be shared via links and survives refresh. It counts as an active filter, so "Clear filters" also unchecks it.
Completed cards cannot be dragged (status cannot be written back to the completed directory). Clicking them opens a read-only popup: it shows all content but provides no edit, status-change, or other action buttons, and a read-only notice is shown below the title bar.
When unchecked, no additional query overhead is incurred.

Multi-Select and Bulk Drag
The board supports moving multiple cards at once:

Multi-select: Ctrl/Cmd + click toggles the selected state of a single card; Shift + click selects a range. After selecting, a selection toolbar appears at the top showing the count and a clear button.
Bulk drag: dragging any selected card moves the whole group; the drag ghost badge shows the actual number of cards being moved. Holding Ctrl/Cmd while starting a drag on an unselected card adds it to the current selection.
Precise insertion: bulk placement supports inserting at any position between two cards in the target column; the drop order is submitted in board reading order. If the target column is in manual sort mode, it automatically reverts to default ordering on drop to ensure correct placement.
Cross-branch cards do not participate in bulk writes; releasing on the original spot is a no-op and does not send a request.

Column Sorting
Each column has a "⋮" column action button in the upper-right corner; clicking it opens a sort menu:
Local Sort (6 Options)
The top half of the menu provides six display-only sort options:

ID ↑ / ID ↓: sort by task ID ascending/descending
Title ↑ / Title ↓: sort by task title alphabetically ascending/descending
Priority ↑ / Priority ↓: sort by priority ascending/descending

Local sorting only affects the display order of the current board column and is not saved to the backend. When the menu is reopened, the active sort item is highlighted with a dark background and an × button appears on the right; click it to clear the sort and restore the original ordinal order.

Dragging a task card or executing "Apply Priority Order" below automatically clears local sorting.

Sort by Creation Date
In addition to local sorting, the column menu provides a Sort by creation date action (ascending/descending). The system compares each task's createdDate field using parseStoredUtcDate; tasks with missing or invalid dates are placed at the end, with task ID as tie-breaker. This sort applies to the current column, just like priority sorting.
Column Menu for Cross-Branch Tasks
When a column contains tasks from other branches (cross-branch tasks), the column action menu is still visible but some actions are restricted:

Local sort options (ID / title / priority) still work, because they only affect view order and do not modify any persisted data.
The Apply Priority Order button is hidden, because that operation modifies the ordinal field of all tasks in the current column, and cross-branch tasks should not be affected by the current branch's sort operation.


Cross-branch tasks show a branch-source indicator on the card. When all tasks in the column belong to the current branch, Apply Priority Order is shown normally.

Reorder by Priority (Save)
The bottom of the menu (separated by a divider) provides the "Reorder by priority (save)" option:

One-click reorder all tasks in the current column by priority (high → medium → low).
The new order is saved to the backend and persists after refreshing the page.
The icon is a list with an up arrow, indicating a persistent operation.

Task Card Date Indicators
Each task card on the board shows date information when set:

Header: calendar icon + plannedStart ~ plannedEnd planned date range. The year is omitted when it matches the current year to reduce visual noise.
Footer: clock icon + dueDate due date, shown next to the relative creation time.
Completion time: cards in a terminal status (such as Done) with an actualEnd show the actual completion time in local time (M/D HH:mm, full year if across years; hover shows the stored UTC value) to the right of the assignee in the footer.
Overdue highlight: when a task is not in a terminal status (Done / Cancelled) and the due date has passed, dueDate is highlighted in red (text-red-600 dark:text-red-400 font-semibold).

Opening Task Details
Click any task card on the board to open the task detail modal:

The underlying board page stays visible, and the address bar updates to /task/:id/:title.
Supports dependency drill-down navigation: clicking a dependency tag in the task detail opens the subtask details.
The task detail includes a Comments area for viewing and adding comments (in edit mode).
Acceptance criteria (AC) list items show sequence numbers (#1, #2 ...) for easy reference and communication.
Closing the modal returns you to the original board view, preserving the current label filters and column sort state.
When accessing /task/:id directly, the system opens the corresponding task with the board as the background.


Task cards on the board do not support both drag and click at the same time; once you start dragging, releasing the mouse completes the status change and will not accidentally open task details.

Task Detail Keyboard Shortcuts
After opening task details, these shortcuts enable quick actions:



Key
Action




e / E
Enter edit mode


c
Change status


d
Delete task


p
Print


Escape
Close modal / cancel editing


Cmd/Ctrl + S
Save changes



When focus is inside an editable element such as input, textarea, select, or contenteditable, preview-state shortcuts (e/E/c/d/p) are suppressed so they do not intercept normal text input. Edit-state Escape and Cmd/Ctrl + S still work inside editable targets.
Real-Time Updates
The board view supports real-time sync in multi-user collaboration scenarios:

When other users drag tasks in the Web interface, your page updates card positions automatically.
After task files are modified in an external editor, card content and status in the board columns refresh automatically.
After tasks are created or deleted, the board reflects the change immediately without manual refresh.
Changes to milestones, documents, decisions, and Wiki are also broadcast by type via WebSocket, and the corresponding lists refresh incrementally in place.

Refresh uses an in-place reconcile strategy: unchanged data keeps its original object reference; open pages, scroll positions, and filter states are not affected by broadcasts. Full-page reload is only used for first load, configuration changes, or when incremental refresh fails.

40-Web界面/02-任务列表.html.title: Task List
40-Web界面/02-任务列表.html.body:
Task List
The "All Tasks" page displays all project tasks in a table, supporting multi-dimensional filtering and search. It is ideal for quickly locating and managing large numbers of tasks.
The page uses a full-width layout and avoids document-level horizontal scrollbars: the table scrolls inside its own container, only the "Title" column is flexible, and the other columns have fixed widths. Filter controls stay on one line when there is enough room; "Clear filters" is rendered only when filters are active, so it does not take up invisible space. Scrollbars use a thin style that matches the theme and stays unobtrusive in both light and dark modes.
Entering the Task List Page
After starting the Web interface, click the "All Tasks" tab in the top navigation bar to enter the task list page. The page shows task ID, title, status, priority, assignee, labels, associated milestone, and other key information in a table layout.
Using Filters
A set of filter controls above the table can be stacked to find tasks precisely.
Filter by Status
Click the "Status" dropdown and check the statuses you want to view. Multiple statuses can be selected at once; for example, checking Todo and In Progress shows all pending and in-progress tasks.
Click "Clear" or uncheck all statuses to restore all tasks.
Exclude by Status
Next to the "Status" filter is an Exclude status dropdown (StatusExcludedDropdown) for inverse filtering: tasks whose status is checked are hidden. For example, after checking Done, the table shows only unfinished tasks. Include and exclude dropdowns can be used together, and filter states are synced to URL query parameters for easy sharing.
Filter by Priority
Click the "Priority" dropdown and select High, Medium, or Low. Priority filtering is single-select; after switching, only tasks of the selected priority are shown.
Filter by Label
Click the "Label" dropdown and check target labels. Multi-select is supported; a task only needs to contain one of the selected labels to match.
Labels are sorted in alphabetical order (case-insensitive), making them easy to scan. Mixed case, accented characters, and fullwidth/halfwidth Unicode equivalents are all sorted stably.
Filter by Milestone
Click the "Milestone" dropdown and select a specific milestone to show only tasks belonging to that milestone. Select "No milestone" to filter out tasks without a milestone.
Show Completed Tasks
The filter bar also provides a "Show completed" checkbox: when checked, historical tasks in backlog/completed/ are shown alongside active tasks (with a Completed badge), the state is synced to the URL, and clicking opens a read-only popup. See the section of the same name in Board View.
Acceptance Criteria Progress Bar
For tasks in In Progress that have acceptance criteria, the title column shows a fixed-width rounded progress bar with a checked/total count; each row has the same height. Tasks without acceptance criteria show nothing.
Global Search
The search box at the top of the task list is a trigger button (showing "Search (⌘K)..."). Clicking it, or pressing Ctrl+K / Cmd+K, opens the global search dialog for searching tasks, documents, decisions, and Wiki pages.
The full dialog description (type filtering, grouped results, keyboard operations, shareable links, position memory) is in Global Search.

Search supports both Chinese and English; keywords are highlighted in result titles and resource IDs.
The dialog is always global in scope and does not stack with the list page filters. To narrow tasks by status, priority, label, or milestone, use the filter dropdowns on the page.
The sidebar and list page no longer provide inline search result dropdowns.

Opening Task Details
Find the target task in the table and click anywhere on the row (usually the task title or ID) to open the task detail modal.
Modal and Background Page
Task details are shown in a modal centered on the screen; the underlying page (task list) remains visible:

The modal overlays the current page; the background page is slightly dimmed but still recognizable.
Closing the modal returns you to the original task list page without losing the current filters and sort state.
When accessing /task/:id directly (such as /task/506), the system opens the corresponding task modal with the task list as the background.

Stable URLs and Sharing
When task details are opened, the address bar updates to the /task/:id/:title format:
http://localhost:6420/task/506/Fix-CLI-actualStart-actualEnd-missing-local-to-UTC-conversion

URLs support prefix-agnostic matching: both /task/123 and /task/back-123 open the same task.
A bare /task/:id link automatically redirects to the full URL with the title slug.
You can copy the address-bar link and share it with team members; when they open it, the task detail is shown over the default view (board).

Dependency Drill-Down
In the Dependencies area of task details, each dependency is shown as a blue tag. Clicking a tag drills into that dependency without returning to the list:

After drilling in, a ← Back button appears on the left side of the modal title bar; click it to return to the parent task.
Supports continuous multi-level drill-down (for example A → B → C).
The browser forward/back buttons also correctly traverse the drill-down history.
The × close button in the upper right is equivalent to the browser back button: it consumes one history level per click. A task opened directly from the list closes with one click; when drilled into a subtask, the first click returns to the parent, and a second click from the outermost level closes the modal.
The ← back arrow behaves the same as ×, consuming only one history level.


Drill-down navigation is only available in preview mode; clicking dependency tags in new-task or edit-task mode does nothing.

Parent/Child Task Hierarchy
If the current task has a parent or subtasks, a hierarchy block appears below the modal title:

PARENT row: shows the parent task's ID, title, and status tag; click to open the parent task directly inside the modal.
SUBTASKS section: shows subtask completion count (such as 1/6), a progress bar, and a collapse arrow; click the section header to expand or collapse.
Each subtask shows a completion dot, ID, title, status tag, and drill arrow; click to open that subtask inside the modal.



Tasks that have neither a parent nor subtasks do not show this block, and the modal looks the same as before.
Acceptance Criteria Numbering
Acceptance criteria (AC) list items in task details show sequence numbers (#1, #2 ...), making it easy to reference specific items in discussions or on the command line.
Outline Drawer (Modal Table of Contents)
Task details, Wiki previews, file previews, and similar modals show a bookmark-style "Contents" tab at the middle of the left edge: clicking the tab hides the tab and opens a floating outline panel on the left side of the modal that is the same height as the modal—the modal width itself does not change, so there is no layout jitter. Clicking an entry smoothly scrolls to the corresponding section (scrollspy highlights the current position); closing the panel restores the bookmark tab.
When the window is narrow and docking on the outside would go off-screen, the drawer automatically switches to floating mode over the modal content: it does not render a close button, and clicking any entry or the semi-transparent background closes it. On narrow screens the bookmark tab also moves inside the panel, ensuring the entry is always reachable.
The file preview modal width has been increased accordingly, making long document previews more comfortable.
Dependency Graph Toggle
The Dependencies area header in the task detail modal has a graph button on the right. Clicking it switches the modal body to an interactive dependency subgraph centered on the current task (zoom, pan, legend filtering, node drill-down); each task's view state is remembered independently. See Graph View for details.
The modal also lists the dependency closure of "waiting for / waited on by" by hop count, marking root blockers and unresolvable references; rejected dependency edits (such as those that would create a cycle) are rolled back with a reason.
References and Modified Files Tabs
The References and Modified Files sections in the modal are combined into a tabbed panel, with the tab titles showing counts (such as References(5)):

The default tab depends on task status: completed tasks default to Modified Files; other tasks default to References. Switching tabs only affects the current task.
Modified files are shown as monospace path chips; click to open in file preview. Only project-relative paths are allowed; URL-style inputs are rejected.
When opening a document that contains YAML frontmatter in file preview, the top --- … --- block is shown as an independent metadata panel and no longer mixed into the rendered body (partial previews, line-range previews, and files without frontmatter keep the original behavior).
Both lists support add/remove in edit mode; changes are saved to the task file.

UTC Hover Tooltips for Dates
Date-times in the interface are displayed in the local time zone; hovering over a date that includes time shows a tooltip with the original string stored in the Markdown file, labeled (UTC). Pure date values (YYYY-MM-DD) have no hover tooltip. This rule covers task details, task list, board cards, milestones, drafts, and the stats page.
Read-Only Popup for Completed Tasks
Completed tasks opened from "Show completed" or search results are read-only: edit and status-change buttons are not shown, and a read-only notice banner appears below the title bar. Cross-branch tasks have the same read-only behavior.
Auto-Linking Entity IDs
Task / document / decision IDs written in Markdown bodies such as task descriptions, notes, and comments (for example back-123, doc-5, decision-3) are automatically converted to clickable links when rendered. Clicking opens the corresponding entity:

Resolution is fail-closed: IDs that cannot be uniquely resolved are displayed as plain text, never guessed.
Prefix-agnostic matching: 123 and back-123 point to the same task.
Ranges and lists: ranges like back-101~105 and slash lists like back-101/102/103 are rendered as a single trigger; clicking opens a portal dropdown listing each ID in the range, making it easy to reference a continuous or related set of tasks in one place.
When typing bare numbers in the Web editor input, prefixes are auto-completed based on context, with an insert-link hint.
All three entity types share the same normalized identity keys, so rendering and input behavior are consistent.

Preserving Unsaved Edits
When editing a task, if the task file is modified in the background by another process (for example by another user or an external editor save), the modal does not reset your unsaved input—the system only merges fields that were not touched after the refresh. Your unsaved changes to title, description, plan, notes, dates, AC, DoD, references, and documents are all preserved.
Comments
In the Comments area of task details, you can view all comments for the task:

Comment list: shown read-only, including sequence number, author (if any), timestamp, and Markdown-rendered body.
Input form: as long as the task is editable (including in preview mode), a comment input form appears at the bottom of the area; you do not need to enter edit mode first.
Author input (placeholder "Commenter"): optional, enter the comment author's name.
Add a comment... text box: a rich Markdown editor with a toolbar, paste-to-Markdown, image / Word document drag-and-drop upload, and [[ entity-link autocompletion. Pasted images are automatically promoted from the temporary directory to assets/paste/ on save (a standalone --- line is still preserved as a separator and cannot be used as comment content).
Add comment button: after submitting, the comment list refreshes immediately and keeps the current mode—adding a comment in preview mode does not switch the modal to edit mode.


Delete comment: a delete button appears when hovering over a comment; the Comments area header also has a Clear comments button to remove all comments at once. The command-line equivalents are --remove-comment  and --clear-comments.
Read-only cross-branch tasks show the comment list but do not provide the input form or delete actions.
Comment bodies support Markdown, but standalone --- lines cannot appear in comments (they are preserved as separators).

Table Sorting
All table header columns (ID, Title, Status, Priority, Milestone, Created) support click sorting.
Default Ordinal Sort
The list is sorted by task ordinal by default, consistent with the board, without any explicit action. When no column is in an active sort state, the table returns to ordinal sort mode.
Triple-Click Cycle
Clicking any header column cycles sorting in a triple-click pattern:

First click: sort ascending by that column.
Second click: switch to descending.
Third click: clear the column sort and restore default ordinal sort.

Double-Arrow Sort Icons
Each header column shows a pair of arrows on the right:

Inactive: both ↑ and ↓ are light gray.
Ascending active: the left ↑ is highlighted; the right ↓ remains gray.
Descending active: the right ↓ is highlighted; the left ↑ remains gray.


The outer frame width is identical across the three states, so header text does not jitter when switching sort direction.

40-Web界面/03-里程碑管理.html.title: Milestone Management
40-Web界面/03-里程碑管理.html.body:
Milestone Management
Milestones group tasks into phase goals, making it easier to track overall project progress. The Web interface provides a complete milestone list, detail view, and task-assignment functionality.
Entering the Milestone Page
After starting the Web interface, click the "Milestones" tab in the top navigation bar to enter the milestone management page. The page is divided into two columns: the left side lists milestones, and the right side shows the detail view of the selected milestone.
Viewing the Milestone List
The left list shows all active milestones in the project. Each entry displays the milestone name, description summary, and completion progress. Click any milestone in the list, and the right detail area loads its full information.
Viewing Milestone Details
Clicking a milestone card title (the button on the card is "Details") opens the milestone detail modal, and the address bar updates to /milestone/:id, so the link can be shared directly or reopened after refresh (the same modal-over-route mode as task details; the underlying page remains visible).
The detail view contains:

Name and description (Markdown rendered, including Mermaid charts; placeholder text shown when there is no description).
"Created / Updated" in the top info box (shown only when the corresponding timestamp exists).
Five date fields: dueDate, plannedStart, plannedEnd, actualStart, actualEnd.
Documentation card: linked documents shown as a list, removable one by one.
Full task list belonging to the milestone (supports header sorting).
Completion progress and task counts per status.

Click any task title in the task list to jump to the corresponding task details.
Editing Milestones
Click the "Edit" button in the detail view title bar to enter edit mode. Add/Edit shares the same form components as the task modal:

Description: PasteAwareMDEditor rich Markdown editor, supporting paste conversion from Word/Google Docs/webpages, doc upload, and clipboard image paste (the promote API is called before saving to write into paste/).
Documentation card: linked documents can be added or removed in both preview and edit modes; the add input supports path autocompletion.
Date fields: all five dates can be modified inline in both preview and edit modes (date and datetime-local inputs, with automatic UTC ↔ local time-zone conversion).
Dirty-data protection: when the description has unsaved changes, pressing Esc / Cancel / × shows a confirmation; link clicks inside the description are also intercepted to prevent accidental navigation and data loss.
Shortcut: Ctrl/Cmd+S to save.
After saving, the Markdown file is updated, and the milestone field in the corresponding task files is also synced.


Milestone cards directly show date information and "Last updated" (if available), making it easy to identify time nodes quickly in the list.

Archive and Remove Confirmation Dialogs
Both "Archive" and "Remove" use styled confirmation dialogs (no longer the browser-native window.confirm), with copy that clearly explains the impact on files:

Archive: the milestone file is moved to the archive directory; task files are not modified, and tasks keep their reference to the milestone.
Remove: the milestone file is also moved to the archive directory, and task files are handled according to the following options:
Clear the milestone field on tasks (default option, i.e., set the milestone field on tasks to empty; the tasks themselves remain unchanged).
Keep the reference on tasks, or reassign to another active milestone.



The dialog title is the operation name itself (no longer repeating the milestone name), and the option label in the remove dialog has been changed from "Keep tasks unassigned" to "Clear the milestone field on tasks"—because the operation actually clears the milestone field in the task files, while "unassigned" is just the name of the UI grouping.
Unassigned Task Pool
Find the "Unassigned tasks" area above the milestone list or near the detail area. It shows the list of tasks that currently do not belong to any milestone, acting as a staging pool before assignment.
Browse the unassigned tasks to find the entries you want to categorize.
Drag-and-Drop Assignment to Milestones
In the unassigned task pool, hold the target task card and drag it to the name area of the target milestone on the left, then release. The task is assigned to that milestone.
After successful assignment:

The target task disappears from the unassigned pool.
The target milestone's task count updates automatically.
