The milestone field in the corresponding Markdown file is modified accordingly.


You can also adjust task order within the same milestone detail page by dragging task cards to the target position.

Group Sorting
Each milestone group (including "Unassigned tasks" and each milestone) has its own independent sort header:

ID: sort by task ID number ascending/descending.
Title: sort by task title alphabetically.
Status: sort by status name.
Priority: sort by priority (high → medium → low).
Created: sort by task creation date ascending/descending.

Default sort: the task table inside each milestone card defaults to ordinal sort, aligned with the "All Tasks" page.
Triple-click cycle: clicking any header column cycles—first ascending, second descending, third clears the column sort and restores default ordinal sort.
Click a header column to sort by it; click again to switch direction. Each group's sort state is completely independent; choosing "Sort by priority" in one milestone does not affect the display order of other milestones.
The sort icons use the same double-arrow design as the task list: left ↑ for ascending, right ↓ for descending, with the active direction highlighted. The order of the milestone cards themselves (between groups) remains unchanged.
Completed Milestones
The bottom of the page has a "Completed milestones" collapsible section. Click the section title to expand and view historically completed or archived milestones. Completed milestones usually no longer accept new task assignments, but you can click to view their history.
Searching Milestones
A search box above the milestone list lets you enter keywords; the system filters milestone names and descriptions with fuzzy matching. Results are reflected in the list in real time, making it easy to locate targets when there are many milestones.
Clearing the search box restores the full milestone list.

40-Web界面/04-文档与决策.html.title: Documents & Decisions
40-Web界面/04-文档与决策.html.body:
Documents & Decisions
The Web interface provides browsing for document lists and decision records, grouped by subfolder, making it convenient to read project knowledge-base content in the browser.
Entering the Documents Page
After starting the Web interface, click the "Documents" tab in the top navigation bar to enter the document list page. The page displays all Markdown documents under backlog/docs/ in groups.
Browsing the Document List
The document list is automatically grouped by subfolder. For example:

guides — guide documents
api — API documents
(root) — documents placed directly under docs/

Click a group title to expand or collapse the document entries under that folder. Each entry shows the title, a last-updated summary, and labels if any.
Sidebar Sort Toggles
The document area header in the sidebar provides Name / ID sort toggles. Click to switch the sort column and direction (↑ / ↓ shown next to the column name):

Name: sort by document title (falls back to filename when there is no title), numeric-aware (doc-4 sorts before doc-10).
ID: sort by document ID, with name as tie-breaker.
Each folder level is sorted independently; folders are always listed before files.

The decisions area also provides Title / ID sort toggles; decisions are a flat list without folders. The three sidebar sections (Documents, Wiki, Decisions) share the same control style.
Viewing Document Content
Click a document title in the list to navigate to the document detail page. The document content is shown as rendered Markdown, including:

Title and body
Code blocks and syntax highlighting
Tables and lists
Images and links

Click the "Back" button at the top of the page or the browser back button to return to the document list.
In-Document Anchor Jumping
Title links inside the document body ([link](#section-name) form) smooth-scroll to the target within the current document context and update the address bar anchor, without jumping to the app root. Heading IDs are generated by a unified slug algorithm; human-readable TOC anchors (such as #A1, #A1: Section Title) are still parsed and located correctly. For documents linked by local short links, :line or :start-end line-range suffixes are also supported; clicking shows the specified line range in the preview box.
Links with anchors (such as /documentation/5#A2) also automatically scroll to the target heading on first load: after content is rendered asynchronously, an observer locates the heading, and the anchor in the address bar is preserved during URL normalization (bare IDs are completed with the title slug).
Documents also support direct positioning by ID: whether in the root directory or a subfolder, entering a bare ID (such as doc-20) or a plain number (20) opens the corresponding document accurately. When the ID is ambiguous, a fail-closed conflict hint is shown with a candidate list.
Table of Contents (TOC)
Document, decision, and Wiki detail pages provide a TOC button in the header: clicking expands the heading outline of the current page. The hierarchy comes from actually rendered headings (including duplicate headings and CJK headings):

Click an entry to smooth-scroll to the corresponding section; as you scroll, the current section is highlighted in the TOC (scrollspy).
Entries with subtrees can be collapsed; when there are many entries, deep levels are collapsed by default and the current branch is expanded automatically.
The panel header provides "Collapse all / Expand all" master switches.
The TOC button does not appear when the page has no headings or is in edit mode.


Task details, Wiki previews, and file preview modals have the same outline as a bookmark-style drawer protruding from the left edge of the modal (without changing modal width). See the "Outline Drawer" section in Task List.

Silent Reload on Content Changes
When a document is modified externally on disk, an already-open document page reloads silently based on a content fingerprint comparison: the body is updated only when the content actually changes, and scroll position and anchor are preserved. In edit mode the page does not reload, so unsaved input is not affected.
Mermaid Diagrams
```mermaid code blocks in document, decision, and Wiki bodies are rendered as diagrams: the fence language identifier is case-insensitive; diagram themes switch automatically with the interface light/dark mode; the Markdown editor preview pane also renders Mermaid.
Entering the Decision Records Page
Click the "Decisions" tab in the top navigation bar to enter the decision record (ADR) list page. The page shows all decision files under backlog/decisions/.
Each decision record displays:

Decision title
Current status (Proposed, Accepted, Rejected, Deprecated, Superseded)
Creation date

Viewing Decision Details
Click any entry in the decision list to enter the decision detail page. The page renders the full ADR content, including sections such as background, considerations, final decision, and impact.
Decision status tags are distinguished by color, and status names are localized with the interface language (for example "已接受" in Chinese); non-standard statuses are shown as-is. Each status also has its own icon, so color is not the only distinguishing signal.
Creating a New Decision
The "+" button in the sidebar decisions area opens the new decision page: enter the title and body (images can be pasted and are automatically promoted to assets/paste/ on save); after saving, it navigates to the new decision page. If the body is left empty, the default "Context / Decision / Consequences" template is used.
Editing a Decision
The decision detail page has an Edit button in the upper-right corner: click to enter edit mode, where Cancel / Save button pairs appear; list refreshes during editing do not interrupt or overwrite your input; the ?edit=true deep link opens directly in edit mode.
In edit mode, you can directly modify the status in the header: the dropdown lists standard statuses such as proposed / accepted / rejected / superseded (displayed localized, stored values remain in the original English), or keeps the free-text status already in the data. Changing only the status does not rewrite the body.

40-Web界面/05-设置与主题.html.title: Settings & Themes
40-Web界面/05-设置与主题.html.body:
Settings & Theme
The settings page centrally manages Backlog.md configuration items, Definition of Done defaults, and Web interface theme preferences. The task editor also provides rich editing capabilities in the settings-related area.
Entering the Settings Page
After starting the Web interface, click the "Settings" tab in the top navigation bar to enter the settings page. The page is divided into multiple configuration blocks arranged from top to bottom.
Viewing and Modifying Configuration Items
In the "Configuration" block, you can view and edit currently effective parameters, including:

Default assignee (defaultAssignee): a list-type setting automatically applied when a task/draft is created without an explicit assignee.
Labels (labels): editor for the project's predefined label list.
Default editor (defaultEditor): clearing this field disables the default editor (the service default code --wait can hang unattended agent processes).
Web server port: defaultPort and the automatic-port toggle (automatically use the next available port when the default is occupied).
Hide empty status columns (hideEmptyColumns): when enabled, the board hides status columns with no tasks, reducing visual clutter; all status columns remain visible while dragging a task so it can be dropped.
Auto-open browser (autoOpenBrowser).
Task resolution strategy (taskResolutionStrategy): conflict-resolution strategy when tasks with the same name exist in multiple branches—most_recent (take the most recently modified version) or most_progressed (take the version whose status has advanced the furthest, falling back to modification time when progress is equal); new projects default to most_recent.
Advanced Settings cross-branch toggles: below Task Resolution Strategy are Cross-Branch Tasks (includeCrossBranch, default off—whether scanned tasks from other branches appear in board/task list/search), Check Active Branches (checkActiveBranches, default on—whether to scan other local branches, also determines the candidate branch set for task ID allocation), and Active Branch Days (activeBranchDays, default 30 days, shown only when the scan toggle is on).
Diagram engine (diagramEngine): which engine renders Mermaid diagrams—pele (default, open-sourced by the Obsidian team, zero-dependency, renders Mermaid 12.1.0 syntax to SVG) or mermaid (11.16.1 fallback); the choice is persisted to the diagram_engine key in config.yml and remains effective after restarting the browser. It affects only Mermaid diagrams, not ECharts data charts.
Git-related options (see Configuration Management).

Click the item you want to modify, enter the new value, and click the "Save" button. Configuration changes are written back to the project configuration file immediately; some settings (such as port) take effect after restarting backlog browser.
List-type settings (default assignee, labels) are presented as a list editor: you can add or remove items one by one, and they are written back to the YAML list in the configuration file on save. These settings are the same configuration modified by backlog config set; both entry points see each other's changes.
Default assignee takes effect when creating a task: if no assignee is specified, the default is applied; an explicit assignee completely replaces the default (no merge). Clearing the assignee chips in the creation form saves an empty value and does not fall back to the default.
State Machine Editor
The settings page provides a state machine editor for visually maintaining the object-form statuses configuration in backlog/config.yml—previously only editable by hand. The editor uses a left-right layout:

Left state card list: add, delete, and edit states (name, category, exit action, display flag), and maintain each state's next transitions (target to, condition when, AI autonomy level ai, prerequisite if, required evidence requires / evidence); supports multi-select terminal statuses.
Right Mermaid live preview: a migration tree recursively expanded from the initial state along next, with back edges and cycles degraded to dashed back-references so they do not expand infinitely.
Layout toggle: switch between card layout and tab layout.

The two restore buttons have strictly distinct semantics:

Reset: appears only when there are unsaved changes; discards edits and reloads the current content from config.yml (never overwrites the file).
Default: replaces the current configuration with the built-in seven-state default state machine (equivalent to a factory reset).

The state machine is declarative, not enforced: the editor can show lint warnings but will not block saving; after saving, the server broadcasts config-updated, and board columns and terminal-status determination refresh immediately. The three AI-facing overviews (CLI backlog instructions overview, MCP resources, and instruction tools) automatically render the same state machine, and agents work according to the declared machine. See Task Lifecycle for state machine semantics.
The terminal-status set is derived from the state machine and is the only place to change it: the settings page previously had a "terminal status" multi-select, but it did not store a list; instead it silently rewrote each state's category—conflicting with the state machine editor writing the same field. Now the settings page only shows the derived terminal-status set (such as Done, Dropped) as read-only with a source note; backlog config list also prints terminalStatuses: [Done, Dropped] (derived from statuses). To add or remove terminal statuses, modify the corresponding state's category in the state machine editor above.
Editing Definition of Done Defaults
In the "Definition of Done" block, you can view and edit the default completion criteria checklist automatically attached to new tasks.
Click the text editing area and enter or modify DoD items, one per line. After saving, new tasks created through the Web interface or CLI will carry the updated default DoD list.
Customizing the Web UI Theme
In the "Theme" block, you can switch the interface appearance:

Follow system — automatically match the operating system's light or dark mode setting.
Light mode — force a light background theme.
Dark mode — force a dark background theme.

After switching, the entire Web interface color scheme takes effect immediately without refreshing the page. The preference is saved locally in the browser and restored automatically on the next visit.
Language Switching
In the "Language" dropdown in the "Project Settings" block, you can choose the Web interface display language:

English
日本語 (Japanese)
简体中文 (Simplified Chinese)
繁體中文 (Traditional Chinese)

After selecting a language, interface text switches immediately without refreshing the page. The language preference is saved together with the project configuration to the locale field in backlog/config.yml (or the project root configuration) and restored automatically the next time the Web interface starts.

The language setting is persisted only after clicking the "Save changes" button to write it to the configuration file. Switching language before saving previews the new language immediately, but refreshing the page reverts to the last saved setting.

Using the Task Editor
Click any task in the Web interface to enter the task editor page. The editor provides rich forms and Markdown editing capabilities.
Rich-Text Markdown Editor
The task description area uses the MDEditor rich-text editor. You can type Markdown syntax directly; the editor provides real-time preview and common formatting shortcut buttons:

Heading levels
Bold, italic, strikethrough
Unordered and ordered lists
Code blocks and blockquotes
Links and tables

Interactive Acceptance Criteria Checklist
Find the "Acceptance criteria" area in the task editor. Each acceptance criterion has a checkbox on the left; click to mark it complete or incomplete. The checked state is automatically synced and saved to the corresponding section of the Markdown file.
When checking multiple acceptance criteria or DoD items in the Web popup preview mode, the system batches saves: it waits about one second of inactivity before sending a single request (carrying the complete checked array), rather than sending a request on every click. Any unsaved checks are flushed immediately before the popup closes; if it fails, they roll back to the server's known state. This prevents a request storm when working through a long checklist and makes board and task-list refreshes smoother.
If you manually modify the acceptance criteria format in the Markdown source file, the editor automatically repairs and syncs the list structure when loading, ensuring checkboxes display correctly.
Task Content Outline
For tasks with longer content, the editor shows a "Contents" (TOC) panel on the right. The outline automatically extracts headings at all levels from the task body; click any heading to quickly scroll to the corresponding position. As you scroll, the outline highlights the current section.
Rich Form Fields
A set of structured form fields is provided at the top of the editor; click to modify:

Status — dropdown selection of Todo, In Progress, Done, etc.
Priority — choose High, Medium, Low.
Labels — enter label names, supports multiple labels.
Milestone — dropdown to select an existing milestone or leave blank.
Assignee — enter assignee name.
Dependencies — add IDs of other tasks this task depends on.
References — add referenced tasks or external links.

After modifying any field, click the "Save" button at the bottom of the page; the changes are written back to the Markdown file.
Automatic Mermaid Diagram Rendering
If the task body contains Mermaid syntax code blocks, the Web interface automatically renders them as visual diagrams, including flowcharts, sequence diagrams, Gantt charts, etc. No extra action is needed; the diagram appears immediately after saving the task. The Pele engine is used by default; you can switch to the Mermaid 11.16.1 fallback in the Diagram Engine dropdown on the settings page (see the "Diagram engine" configuration item above).
Images and Attachment Viewing
Images referenced in tasks (such as ![description](assets/xxx.png)) are displayed directly as previews in the editor. Click a preview to view the original image in a new tab.
Files under the project's backlog/assets/ directory are automatically served by the Web server, ensuring all attachments and screenshots load normally in the Web interface.

40-Web界面/06-富文本粘贴与文档上传.html.url: 40-Web界面/06-富文本粘贴与文档上传.html
40-Web界面/06-富文本粘贴与文档上传.html.title: Rich-text Paste & Document Upload
40-Web界面/06-富文本粘贴与文档上传.html.body:
Rich-Text Paste & Document Upload
The Backlog.md Web interface editor supports one-click conversion of external rich-text content to Markdown, including paste from Word, Google Docs, and webpages, as well as uploading .docx files. It also supports screenshot paste, automatically uploading images and embedding them into the task body.
Paste as Markdown
In the Markdown editing area of the task editor, copy and paste content directly from an external source. The editor automatically recognizes rich-text HTML and converts it to clean Markdown.
Supported Sources



Source
Converted Content




Microsoft Word
Paragraphs, headings, lists, tables, bold/italic/underline


Google Docs
Paragraphs, headings, lists, tables, formatting


Excel
Tables (including header detection)


Webpages
HTML structure, links, lists, tables


Screenshots
image/png images, uploaded automatically



Paste Flow

Select content in the external app and copy.
Press Ctrl+V (or Cmd+V) in the Backlog.md editor.
The editor reads text/html from the clipboard.
Word/Excel-specific markup is cleaned (noisy tags, inline styles, mso-list, etc.).
If images are present, they are extracted and uploaded to a temporary directory.
Turndown converts the cleaned HTML to Markdown.
The conversion result is inserted at the editor cursor position.

If the clipboard does not contain HTML (plain text only), the editor falls back to native paste behavior without extra processing.
Upload Word Documents
In addition to clipboard paste, the editor supports direct upload of .docx files. This is especially useful for documents with many images or complex formatting.
How to Use
In the task editor:

Click the "Upload Word" button in the editor toolbar and select a local .docx file.
Or drag and drop a .docx file directly into the editor area.

Conversion Flow

The front end sends the .docx file to the back end via POST /api/docx/convert.
The back end uses the mammoth library to parse the document and extract text content as HTML.
Embedded images in the document are extracted and uploaded to backlog/assets/.temp/.
The back end returns the raw HTML, image list, and conversion warnings.
The front end uses the exact same cleanHtml + Turndown pipeline as "Paste as Markdown" to convert the HTML to Markdown.
Image references are embedded in the body as /assets/.temp/{uuid}.png.

Unified Pipeline Ensures Consistency
Word document upload and rich-text paste share the same front-end conversion logic, ensuring consistent output formats. For complex tables, nested lists, and similar scenarios, the unified pipeline avoids format differences that could arise from back-end direct conversion.
Image Handling
Screenshot Paste
When pasting a screenshot directly (such as from QQ/WeChat or system screenshot tools):

The image is uploaded as an image/png blob.
It is saved to backlog/assets/.temp/{uuid}.png.
A preview thumbnail is shown in the editor.

Webpage Images
When pasted content contains  tags from a webpage:

Data URI images: base64 data is extracted and uploaded to the temporary directory.
HTTP(S) URL images: downloaded securely by the back end and then uploaded.
file:// local paths: rejected (browser security restriction).

Promote on Save
All temporary images (including pasted screenshots and images extracted from Word documents) are automatically promoted when the task is saved:

The front end scans Markdown for /assets/.temp/ references.
It calls POST /api/assets/promote to move files in batches.
Images are moved from .temp/ to the permanent paste/ directory.
The front end updates URL mappings in the Markdown and then performs the save.

Expired files in the temporary directory (older than 30 minutes) are automatically cleaned up when the server starts.
Limitations and Notes

File size: single files over 20MB return an error.
Format support: only .docx file upload is supported; older .doc files must be converted first.
Corrupted documents: unreadable documents show a readable error message instead of crashing.
Image size: if a single image exceeds the size limit, it may be skipped or cause the overall operation to fail (depending on policy configuration).

40-Web界面/07-Wiki浏览与编辑.html.title: Wiki Browsing & Editing
40-Web界面/07-Wiki浏览与编辑.html.body:
Wiki Browsing & Editing
The Backlog.md Web interface provides a complete Wiki module for browsing and editing knowledge-base content under backlog/wiki/. The Wiki is an LLM-maintained incremental knowledge base—AI agents read source files such as tasks/docs/decisions and automatically compile them into structured wiki content; it is human-readable and editable, and pages can be created and modified directly.
Entering the Wiki
After starting the Web interface, click the "Wiki" tab in the top navigation bar to enter the Wiki page. The page is divided into left and right parts:

Left sidebar: collapsible file tree reflecting the directory structure of backlog/wiki/.
Right content area: rendered Markdown content.

Browsing the File Tree
The sidebar shows all content under backlog/wiki/ in a tree structure:

Click the chevron icon to the left of a folder to expand or collapse it.
The number of Markdown files in a folder is shown next to the folder name (such as concepts (3)).
Click a .md file to view its content on the right.
Empty folders are also shown in the tree and can be expanded to view their children.

Sort Toggles
The Wiki area header provides Title / Filename sort toggles. Click to switch the sort column and direction:

Title: sort by the page frontmatter title (falls back to filename when there is no title); the tree display labels also change to titles.
Filename: sort by filename (without .md); labels display filenames accordingly—the tree always shows the field currently used for sorting.
Folders are always listed before pages; each level is sorted independently and numeric-aware (page-4 comes before page-10).

Paths and URLs
Wiki page URLs preserve directory-level readability; the / separator is not encoded as %2F. For example, a page at concepts/web-ui-features.md shows in the address bar as:
http://localhost:6420/wiki/concepts/web-ui-features
Spaces, CJK characters, and other special characters in the path are safely encoded, but the directory hierarchy remains intuitive. You can copy or edit the path in the address bar to quickly jump to a target page.
Viewing Page Content
Wiki pages are shown as rendered Markdown:

The page title is extracted from frontmatter and displayed.
Supports code-block syntax highlighting, Mermaid diagrams, tables, and lists.
Labels: the page's labels are shown below the title (such as concept, source).
Click wikilink references in the body to jump to the corresponding page.

Online Editing
Click the "Edit" button in the upper-right corner of the page to enter edit mode:

Title: modify the page title in the large input box at the top; after saving, it is automatically written to frontmatter.
Labels: the ChipInput below the title supports adding/removing labels; press Enter or comma to add, Backspace to remove the last one.
Body: use the full Markdown editor (supports paste-as-Markdown, image upload, and Word document conversion).
Save: the Save button turns blue and enabled only when content, title, or labels have changed.
Cancel: click Cancel to discard all changes and restore the original content.

After saving, the page frontmatter automatically updates the updated_date field.
Switching Pages Auto-Exits Edit Mode
In edit mode, if you click another Wiki page in the sidebar, the system automatically exits edit mode and shows the new page in read-only view:

Unsaved edits are silently discarded.
The edit/view toggle button state updates to "View" mode.
This prevents the new page content from being accidentally shown in the editor and reduces confusion.


If you want to save the current changes, click Save before switching pages.

Creating Files and Folders
Create new content anywhere in the sidebar:

Hover over a folder name or the Wiki root title.
A + button appears on the right; click it to expand a dropdown menu:
Create file — create a new page; enter the filename (.md is auto-completed).
Create folder — create an empty folder.


After creation succeeds, you are automatically navigated to the new page.

The + button on the root "Wiki" title creates content under the backlog/wiki/ root directory.
Renaming
Select Rename from the dropdown menu of a file or folder:

Enter a new name; cross-directory moves are supported (such as concepts/new-name).
If you are currently viewing the page, you are automatically navigated to the new path after renaming.

Popup Preview and Outline Drawer
Wiki previews and file previews opened from the file tree or search are presented as popups without leaving the current page. A bookmark-style "Contents" tab protrudes from the middle of the left edge of the popup: clicking it opens a floating outline panel on the left side of the popup that is the same height as the popup; clicking an entry smoothly scrolls to the corresponding section. The popup width remains unchanged; on narrow screens the drawer automatically switches to floating mode over the content. The file preview popup width has been increased, making long documents more comfortable.
Real-Time Sync
Wiki content is synced in real time across all open tabs:

Wiki files modified through the CLI or an external editor → WebSocket broadcast → all browser tabs refresh automatically.
Edits saved in the browser → other tabs show the update instantly.
The file tree also responds automatically to create, modify, delete, and rename operations.

Differences from Documents




Documents (docs/)
Wiki (wiki/)




Maintainer
Human-written
Mainly maintained by AI Skill; human-readable and editable


Purpose
Project guides, API docs, reference manuals
Knowledge base: concept extraction, source summaries, cross-references


Editing
Modified through the editor after creation
Edited directly in the browser; frontmatter auto-managed


Structure
Human-organized
AI maintains standard directories (sources/, concepts/, entities/)

40-Web界面/08-统计页面.html.title: Statistics Page
40-Web界面/08-统计页面.html.body:
Statistics Page
The statistics page provides a project-level overview of task data, helping you quickly grasp overall progress and tasks that need attention.
Entering the Statistics Page
After starting the Web interface, click the "Statistics" tab in the top navigation bar to enter the statistics page.
Page Structure
The statistics page is divided into four main areas:
Contribution Heatmap
The top of the page shows a GitHub-style contribution heatmap, visually presenting the number of tasks completed each day over the past year.
The heatmap card provides a completed corpus toggle in the upper-right corner: by default statistics include only active tasks (backlog/tasks/); when enabled, the sample expands to historical completed records in backlog/completed/, and the state is synced to the page URL (completed=1). Top metrics such as average completion time switch corpora together with this toggle.

Grid layout: 7 rows (Sunday to Saturday) × 53 columns (weeks), consistent with the GitHub contribution graph layout.
Color intensity: 5 levels, from light to dark, representing the number of tasks completed that day.
Level 0 (no tasks): light gray close to the background color
Level 1 (1–2 tasks): light green
Level 2 (3–5 tasks): medium green
Level 3 (6–9 tasks): dark green
Level 4 (10+ tasks): deepest green


Dark mode: automatically switches to a dark-theme green gradient palette.
Month labels: abbreviated month names at the top, localized by the current language.
Weekday labels: abbreviated Sunday, Tuesday, Thursday labels on the left (shown every other row to save space).

Interactions

Hover: hovering over any cell shows a floating tooltip with the specific date (YYYY-MM-DD format) and the number of tasks completed that day.
Click: clicking a cell keeps the tooltip fixed until you click elsewhere on the page or click the same cell again.
Title: shows the total number of tasks completed in the past year, such as "143 tasks completed in the past year", with automatic pluralization by language.

Status Overview
Basic project statistics are shown at the top of the page:

Total tasks: total number of tasks in the project.
Completion percentage: proportion of tasks in Done status.
Drafts: current number of drafts.
Average task duration: the fifth card in the top metrics row, showing the average completion time in minutes and sample size for tasks in canonical terminal statuses. The span definition is fully consistent with Gantt chart Actual Start / Actual End (actualStart → createdDate → now fallback chain). Completion only counts canonical terminal statuses—Done is included in the sample; abandoned terminal statuses such as Dropped do not count as completed.
Status distribution: task counts for each status such as To Do / In Progress / Done.


Average duration is strongly right-skewed (most tasks finish in minutes, a few drag on for weeks), so the card also displays the sample size next to the mean to avoid a single average being misleading.

Priority Distribution
Task distribution across priorities is shown visually:

High — number of high-priority tasks
Medium — number of medium-priority tasks
Low — number of low-priority tasks
None — number of tasks without a priority set

Project Health
The project health section is the core of the statistics page, showing four types of tasks that need special attention:



Category
Color
Condition




At Risk
🟡 amber
Non-Done tasks with a due date of today or tomorrow


Overdue
🔴 red
Non-Done tasks whose due date has passed


Stale
🔵 blue
Non-Done tasks without a due date, not updated for more than 30 days


Blocked
🔴 red
Tasks with uncompleted dependencies



The page header horizontally displays the four health indicators as colored dots + counts. Click or hover to view the specific task list for each category.
Health Task Cards
Each health category lists matching task cards below:

At Risk / Overdue cards: show task title and Due by date.
Stale cards: show task title and Updated date.
Blocked cards: show task title and Dependency status.

All cards are clickable and jump to the task edit page.
Hover Tooltips
Hovering over a health indicator dot shows the description for that category:

At Risk: "Due soon, needs immediate attention"
Overdue: "Past the due date"
Stale: "No due date and not updated for more than 30 days"

Automatic Data Refresh
The statistics page supports real-time data sync:

Server cache: the backend maintains statistics cache and refreshes with a 500ms delay. When tasks are created or modified via the CLI, backlog commands, or other means, the statistics page automatically detects the change and updates within about one second.
Client cache: the page uses localStorage to cache the last loaded statistics result. When reopening the page, cached data is shown first while the latest data is fetched silently in the background, enabling instant loading.
WebSocket push: the server actively pushes updates via the "statistics-updated" event, so no manual refresh is needed.

Recent Activity
The bottom of the statistics page shows recent project activity:

Recently created: list of tasks created in the last 7 days.
Recently updated: list of tasks modified in the last 7 days.


If a task has never been edited, its creation date is used as the fallback for "Recently updated", ensuring newly created tasks are not missed.

40-Web界面/09-甘特图视图.html.title: Gantt View
40-Web界面/09-甘特图视图.html.body:
Gantt Chart View
The Gantt chart view displays task start/end times and dependencies on a timeline, helping you intuitively grasp project progress, identify the critical path, and spot schedule conflicts.
Entering the Gantt Chart View
After starting the Web interface, click the "Gantt" tab in the top navigation bar to enter the Gantt chart view. On first entry, the system automatically parses date data for all tasks and renders the timeline.
Page Layout
The Gantt chart view uses a left-right dual-column layout:

Left task list: a fixed-width table showing task ID, title, time columns, and action buttons.
Right timeline area: dynamically rendered task bars and dependency arrows, with a time-axis scale at the top.

Scroll events in the two columns are bidirectionally synchronized, so they stay aligned when scrolling vertically.
Time Granularity Switching
The top of the timeline provides five granularity buttons:



Granularity
Scenario
Characteristics




Day
View dense short-term development schedules
Multiple tasks on the same day are offset horizontally to avoid overlap


Week
Iteration progress review
Suitable for Sprint or weekly meeting scenarios


Month
Monthly project review
Balances detail and overview


Quarter
Medium- to long-term project overview
Large time-span window


Year
Annual project big picture
Most macroscopic perspective



When switching granularity, task bar positions and widths are recalculated automatically to remain clear at the current scale.
Task Time Parsing
The Gantt chart does not require tasks to have planned dates. The system parses each task's effective start/end time according to the following rules:
Start time

If the task has plannedStart → use the planned start time first.
If there is no planned start time → use the task creation date (date part of createdDate).

End time

If the task has plannedEnd → use the planned end time first.
If there is no planned end time but there is updatedDate → use the date part of the update date.
If only the creation date exists → enable the minimum-width fallback.


Tip: To make a task show an exact time range on the Gantt chart, fill in plannedStart and plannedEnd in the "Planned dates" area of the task edit page.

Minimum Width Fallback
For tasks that only have a creation time and no planned dates, the system gives them a minimum visual width so they do not compress into invisible thin lines on the timeline:

Day view: minimum visual width of about 4 hours; multiple tasks on the same day are automatically offset horizontally to avoid complete overlap.
Week/Month view: minimum width of 1 day.
Quarter/Year view: fixed 8-pixel color block width, ensuring visibility even at macroscopic scales.

These tasks are marked with * in the left list; hovering shows a "fallback rendering" hint.
Task Bar Interactions
Hover to View Details
Hovering over any task bar pops up a tooltip showing:

Task ID and title.
Parsed start and end times.
Whether it is fallback rendering (tasks with only creation time).

Click to Highlight the Dependency Chain
Clicking a task bar highlights the entire dependency chain for that task:

Predecessor tasks (what this task depends on) and successor tasks (what depends on this task) remain at normal brightness.
Other unrelated tasks and arrows fade to 30% opacity.
Click the task bar again or click an empty area to cancel the highlight.

This is very useful for quickly locating upstream and downstream impact scope in complex projects.
Open Task Details

Click the "Details" button in the left list: opens the familiar task edit modal, where you can modify task fields, dates, and dependencies.
Click the task bar on the right: highlights the dependency chain (as described above).

Dependency Arrows
Dependencies between tasks are visualized with SVG Bézier curve arrows:

Arrows point from the predecessor task's end position to the successor task's start position.
Multiple dependencies are automatically staggered to reduce line tangling.
Arrows scale adaptively when switching time granularity.
Dependency arrows also participate in the "click to highlight" interaction.


Note: The Gantt chart view currently only visualizes dependencies and does not support dragging to adjust task times. To modify task dates, use the "Details" button on the left to enter the task edit page.

List Sorting
The first four columns of the left task list (ID, Title, Start Time, End Time) support click sorting:

Each header shows double-arrow icons (↑/↓) on the right.
Inactive arrows are gray; ascending highlights the left arrow; descending highlights the right arrow.
Click to toggle ascending/descending; clicking another column sorts by the new column.
The outer frame width is the same across the three states, so header text does not jitter when switching.

After sorting, the Gantt bars on the right are re-laid out in the new task order, but their time positions remain unchanged.
Timeline Panning
Hold the mouse button and drag left or right in the timeline area to pan the time axis and view more dates:

Drag left to view earlier times.
Drag right to view later times.
Panning is smooth and does not refresh the page.

Dark Mode Support
The Gantt chart view is fully adapted for dark mode:

Task bars, timeline scales, and dependency arrows all use Tailwind CSS dark: variants.
Hover tooltips and highlight states remain clear against dark backgrounds.
No page refresh is needed after switching system theme or manual switching.

Tracking Gantt Chart
The tracking Gantt chart displays both the planned time range and actual task progress on the same row, helping you intuitively track deviations.
Dual-Layer Rendering
Each task row draws two independently positioned elements stacked on the z-axis:

Bottom actual bar: solid status-color fill.
In Progress → blue
Done / Completed → green
To Do → gray
Blocked → red
Cancelled → light gray


Top planned border: 60° diagonal-line fill frame (two border layers: 2px shadow layer + 1px final line).

Deviation Scenarios



Deviation Scenario
Condition
Visual Appearance




Early start
actualStart 
Actual bar begins to the left of the planned frame; left overflow is solid color.


Normal
actualStart = plannedStart, actualEnd ≤ plannedEnd
Actual bar extends inside the frame; overlap area shows color + diagonal lines, unreached tail shows pure diagonal lines.


Delay
actualEnd > plannedEnd
Actual bar exceeds the planned frame on the right; right overflow is solid color.



Left Time Columns
The toolbar provides showPlanTime and showActualTime toggles:

Actual Start / Actual End: always displayed, parsed in priority order actualStart → actualEnd → createdDate/updatedDate.
Planned Start / Planned End: planned time columns, displayed only when showPlanTime is enabled.

Smart Dependency Arrows
In tracking mode, dependency arrow connection points consider both actual and planned times:

If actual start is earlier than planned start, the arrow connects to the earlier actual position.
If actual end is earlier than planned start (rare), it falls back to planned end to keep the dependency chain coherent.
Arrow colors are uniformly gray to avoid clashing with status-colored actual bars.

Interaction Enhancements

Hover tooltip: shows planned time range, actual time range, and fallback indicators together.
Legend: the toolbar shows a legend—status-color bar = actual, diagonal-line frame = planned, arrow = dependency, amber * = estimated time.
Click highlight: the planned border layer also participates in highlight/dimming.
Default sort is ID descending; default view is day view.
The first task is automatically selected on load; switching views auto-scrolls to the selected task.

Date Field Recommendations
To get the most value from the Gantt chart, it is recommended to fill in planned dates for key tasks:



Field
Purpose
Recommendation




plannedStart
Task planned start time
Expected start date of the task


plannedEnd
Task planned end time
Expected completion date of the task


dueDate
Task due date
Distinguish from plannedEnd: due date is a hard constraint; planned end is the expected completion time


actualStart
Actual start time
Auto-filled by the system; can be manually corrected


actualEnd
Actual end time
Auto-filled by the system; can be manually corrected



These fields can be filled directly in the "Planned dates" area of the task edit page. After filling them, the Gantt chart automatically uses the more precise time range and no longer relies on creation-date fallback rendering.

40-Web界面/10-全局搜索.html.title: Global Search
40-Web界面/10-全局搜索.html.body:
Global Search
The Web interface provides a macOS Spotlight-style centered search dialog that searches tasks, drafts, documents, decisions, Wiki pages, and memos in one go. It replaces the earlier sidebar inline search that could only show 5 results.
Opening and Closing



Action
Method




Open
Press Ctrl+K (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+K (macOS); or click the search trigger button at the top of the sidebar


Close
Press Esc, click the × in the upper-right corner of the dialog, click the mask area outside the dialog, or use the browser back button



When the dialog opens, the underlying page stays as-is and scrolling is locked; after closing, you return to the original page without losing filter or sort state.

The search box in the sidebar is now a read-only trigger button showing "Search (⌘K)..."; clicking it opens the dialog. Input and results have moved into the dialog.

Dialog Layout

Desktop: horizontally centered, about 12vh from the top, fixed 800px width, max height 75vh, with a dark semi-transparent mask.
Narrow screens (width 

Search Types
A row of type tabs at the top of the dialog re-searches immediately when a new scope is selected:



Tab
Scope




All
Tasks, documents, decisions, Wiki, memos


Tasks
Only tasks (including drafts)


Documents
Only documents


Wiki
Only Wiki pages


Decisions
Only decision records


Memos
Only memos



No results are shown when the input is empty; search runs automatically about 300 milliseconds after typing.
Include Completed Tasks
The dialog provides a "Completed corpus" toggle: when enabled, the search scope expands to historical tasks in the backlog/completed/ directory. Matched completed records carry a Completed badge and open in a read-only popup (no edit actions) when clicked. It is off by default, and default results are identical to before.
Results List
Results are grouped by type (Tasks → Documents → Wiki → Decisions → Memos). Each group has a header showing the count and a collapse arrow:

Click the header (or press Enter / Space when focused) to collapse or expand the group; collapsed groups do not participate in scroll positioning.
Each row shows: type icon, resource ID, title, and status/priority labels.
The entered keyword is highlighted in both titles and resource IDs.
There is no result count limit; the list uses virtual scrolling and stays smooth even with thousands of results.

Keyboard Operations



Key
Behavior




↑ / ↓
Move selection up/down


Enter
Open the selected item


Esc
Close the dialog


Ctrl+K / Cmd+K
Open (keeps focus if already in the dialog)



Navigation Behavior When Opening Results

Tasks: opened as a modal over the current page; after closing, you return to the search dialog with the query, type filter, and scroll position preserved.
Documents / Decisions / Wiki: navigate to the corresponding full-page view; use the browser back button to return to the search dialog.
Memos: navigate to /memos?date=—memos do not have an independent detail route, so they are opened in the memo page's day view.

Position Memory
After scrolling in the result list and pressing Enter to open an item, returning via Back returns the list to its original position (it records the "first visible row" rather than pixel offset, so it can still restore stably when the result set changes). If the position is no longer valid (for example results have decreased), the list returns to the top.
Closing the dialog with Esc, clicking the mask, or clicking × does not record position—there is no need to remember scroll position when actively abandoning the search.
Sharing and Refreshing
The dialog state is saved in the address bar:
http://localhost:6420/search?q=timezone&type=task

q is the keyword; omitted if not entered.
type is the type filter (doc is short for document); omitted means "All".
Refreshing the page or sending the link to a colleague reopens the dialog with the same query, filter, and results.

Related Chapters

Task List — list page filtering and task detail modal
Wiki Browsing & Editing — Wiki page reading and editing

40-Web界面/11-图谱视图.html.title: Graph View
40-Web界面/11-图谱视图.html.body:
Graph View
The Graph View displays a Neo4j-style force-directed graph of dependencies and ownership between tasks, drafts, and milestones, as well as the knowledge network formed by Wiki pages, documents, and decisions. It is powered by the built-in dependency graph service: this service scans Markdown files under backlog/ to build a graph database, incrementally updates as files change, and requires no manual maintenance.
Entering the Graph Page
After starting the Web interface, two graph entries are provided below "Statistics" in the sidebar:

Graph (/graph): task dependency graph, with nodes for tasks, completed tasks, drafts, and milestones.
Knowledge Graph (/knowledge): knowledge network, with nodes for Wiki pages, documents, decisions, and tags.

You can also open the corresponding page by directly accessing /graph or /knowledge.
Node and Edge Visual Conventions

Node shape and color: distinguished by category (task / completed / draft / milestone / Wiki / document / decision / tag); node radius reflects degree (more connections = larger node); titles are shown as caption plates that disclose progressively with zoom level.
Theme-aware strokes: in light theme, each node type switches to a darker border of the same hue and edge colors deepen synchronously, avoiding the washed-out problem where "edges look like gaps and nodes look like outline-less dots" on light backgrounds; dark theme colors remain unchanged.
Edge styles:
DependsOn (dependency): solid line.
ParentOf (parent-child): dashed line, arrow pointing to the parent task.
BelongsToMilestone (milestone membership): dotted line.
The knowledge graph additionally has TaggedWith (tag), SourcedFrom (source), and LinksTo (wikilink reference) edges.


Legend: the page provides a clickable legend; clicking a node category temporarily hides it (click again to restore), making it easier to focus on specific node types. Sample lines in the legend use the same theme-aware colors as the canvas edges, so they never differ.

Interactions



Operation
Method




Zoom / pan
Mouse wheel to zoom, drag empty space to pan


Focus neighborhood
Hover or click a node to keep its direct neighbors highlighted while other nodes fade


Open details
Click a task node to open the task detail modal (over the graph; closing returns to the graph with the viewport unchanged); click a knowledge node to open the corresponding Wiki / document / decision page in a new tab


Keyboard
Arrow keys to pan, Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[ to zoom, Ctrl+0 to return to overview, Esc to clear selection



A zoom control group (zoom in, zoom out, overview) is provided in the upper-right corner. The graph receives graph-updated broadcasts via WebSocket; any file change refreshes the graph in place at the current viewport without interrupting the current browsing position.
Relationship Graph in Task Details
The Dependencies area header in the task detail modal has a graph toggle button on the right. Clicking it switches the modal body to a relationship subgraph centered on the current task:

The subgraph expands bidirectionally along dependency, parent-child, and milestone edges (with depth and node-count limits); clicking a node continues drilling into neighboring tasks.
Each task's graph view state (zoom position, legend filtering) is remembered independently and restored when returning after drilling.
Click the ← Back arrow in the title bar again or press Esc to return to the task detail body.

In addition, the modal shows dependency closure query results: "Waits for / Waited on by" listed by hop count, with root blockers highlighted; unresolvable or cyclic references are also labeled truthfully. If an inline dependency edit is rejected (for example because it would create a cycle), the UI rolls back the change and shows a localized reason.
High-DPI Rendering Performance
On high-pixel-density screens such as Retina / 4K, the graph canvas is now specifically optimized and redraw overhead is significantly reduced:

Viewport culling: only nodes and edges within the current visible area are drawn; elements outside the viewport are skipped.
Batch drawing: edges are grouped by (dash, alpha) and nodes by (style, alpha); each group is drawn in one batch, reducing draw calls.
DPR cap: devicePixelRatio is capped at MAX_DPR=2, avoiding meaningless rendering of pixels beyond human perception on ultra-high-DPI screens.
Text LOD: labels are displayed progressively across three zoom stages (textStage); the farther you zoom out, the more text is omitted, and at the farthest level only nodes are drawn.
Gesture snapshot: pan/zoom operations reuse the previous frame's snapshot and only redraw after the new frame stabilizes, eliminating drag stutter.

All optimizations are pure rendering-layer changes and do not alter graph data, layout, or interaction semantics.
Graph Service and Cache
The graph service starts automatically with the Web server. During first build, /api/graph returns a building status; the graph page becomes available automatically once complete:

Scan scope: only tasks, drafts, milestones, completed (task graph) and wiki, docs, decisions (knowledge graph) under backlog/; archive directories are not included.
Cold-start acceleration: file-fingerprint cache validation means unchanged files are not reparsed; parser or graph-structure version upgrades automatically trigger a full rebuild.
Hot update: any write from CLI / TUI / Web / MCP notifies the graph service to incrementally sync, with directory watching and periodic reconciliation as a fallback.
Cache location: graph data is stored in the OS cache directory (not inside the project tree), partitioned by project path hash. Two browser sessions each hold independent databases and do not contend. The cache directory can be overridden with the environment variable BACKLOG_GRAPH_CACHE_DIR. Only lock files and fingerprint sidecars (*.kuzu.lock, *.kuzu.meta.json) are written to the cache directory; the database itself lives in the WASM in-memory filesystem—this is by design, not a deficiency. The graph can be rebuilt from Markdown at any time.
Backend: the default backend is RyuGraph WASM (Kuzu's MIT fork built for WebAssembly, executing inside Bun's WebAssembly runtime, working out of the box on all platforms without environment variables). The native Kuzu dependency has been removed; BACKLOG_GRAPH_BACKEND=kuzu is no longer a valid value. BACKLOG_GRAPH_BACKEND=memory forces a pure-JS memory fallback mode (Cypher search is not supported). If ryu initialization fails, it automatically falls back to the memory backend without crashing. During fallback, a one-line English warning is printed in the terminal ([graph] RyuGraph (WASM) backend init failed for  ...), and the Web interface displays the English error message returned by the server as-is.
Lock conflicts: only one process may hold a graph slot for a project at a time. Locks are automatically reclaimed when the holder process has exited; if the holder is still alive, the interactive terminal asks whether to take over (troubleshooting for stuck building and takeover is in Troubleshooting).


The graph is only for visualization and querying; it never writes back to Markdown files—all data still uses files under backlog/ as the single source of truth.

40-Web界面/12-文档预览.html.title: Document Preview
40-Web界面/12-文档预览.html.body:
Document Preview
The Backlog.md Web interface supports in-app preview of common Office documents: clicking a document link opens a dedicated preview modal instead of downloading locally. Word and Excel also support editing and writing back to the source file.
Which paths are supported for preview depends on where the link is located:

Reference fields (project-relative backlog/... paths written in task / milestone / document metadata, such as backlog/docs/report.pdf): use the raw-byte endpoint GET /api/raw-file to fetch content (with content-type, restricted to the project data directory), covering any path inside the project.
Body (links in descriptions / comments / notes / document Markdown): only documents under the assets/... convention (i.e., the backlog/assets/ directory) are supported. If the body directly uses a backlog/... prefix, the link is not intercepted and will result in a browser 404.

Cross-origin documents, modifier-key clicks, or links with target=_blank / download still follow the browser's default behavior.
Word Documents
Rendered with docx-editor, showing real paginated A4 pages.

Read-only preview by default; click Edit to enter edit mode, showing the toolbar, margin guides, and ruler.
After editing, Save writes back to the source file through a confirmation guard; Exit edit returns to preview.
The modal header explicitly shows a status badge: gray read-only preview in read mode, blue edit mode in edit mode—status is not inferred from appearance.
Supports CSS full-screen filling the viewport, with content clipped to rounded corners.

PDF Documents
Based on self-hosted pdf.js (loaded at runtime, not in the initial bundle); pages are drawn to canvas page by page.

Fit-to-width adapts to the window width, with no horizontal scrolling even when the left outline is expanded.
PDFs with an outline (table of contents) show a clickable left outline panel; click to scroll to the target page.
Supports CSS full-screen, with the page area clipped to rounded corners.

PPTX Presentations
Based on @aiden0z/pptx-renderer (Apache-2.0), faithfully restoring OOXML to HTML/SVG, with large documents window-mounted.

A thumbnail panel lists each slide; click to jump to the main view.
Presentation mode is edge-to-edge full-screen playback, supporting WPS-style keyboard navigation (→ ↓ Space PageDown Enter for next; ← ↑ PageUp Backspace for previous; Home/End for first/last; Esc to exit).
Read-only preview only.

Excel Spreadsheets
Based on Univer open-source sheets preset, preserving a readable layout: cell text and values, fonts, fills, borders, alignment, merged regions, column widths, row heights, and number formats.

Read-only viewing mode by default, with an explicit read-only badge, displaying cached file values (no recalculation).
Edit mode shows the ribbon, formula bar, and status bar; formula cells show the formula itself rather than the calculated result.
Save applies an in-place OOXML patch: only edited worksheets' cells and merged regions are rewritten; other content (charts, images, conditional formatting, etc.) is preserved as-is. Saves with no actual changes honestly report "no changes" rather than "success".
Only .xlsx / .xlsm; newly added worksheets in the editor are not written back, and cell formatting changes are not written back.

Unsupported Formats
For Office formats the app cannot render (legacy .doc, PowerPoint and Excel family variants, macros, and template variants), clicking does not directly download or open; instead, a prompt suggests converting to .docx or .pdf first. Modifier-key clicks or target=_blank / download still open in a new tab.
Localization
All user-visible text in the four preview modals follows the app language (en / zh-CN / zh-TW / ja), including status badges, buttons, dialogs, and player hints.

50-AI集成/00-MCP工作流.html.title: MCP Workflow
50-AI集成/00-MCP工作流.html.body:
MCP Workflow
Backlog.md integrates deeply with AI coding assistants through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). MCP is a standardized protocol that allows AI agents to directly invoke Backlog.md's functional tools without users manually typing CLI commands. With MCP, AI can read, create, and manage tasks like a human developer, enabling true collaborative project management.
What Is MCP Integration
In the traditional approach, AI assistants could only learn Backlog.md's CLI commands from instruction files and then execute shell commands on their own. This had two problems:

AI had to parse shell output, which was error-prone.
When command execution failed, AI had difficulty accurately determining the cause.

MCP integration fundamentally changes this model. AI agents call Backlog.md's tool functions directly through a standardized protocol, with structured parameters and return values, greatly improving reliability. The Backlog.md MCP server runs locally and communicates with AI clients via stdio, exposing no network ports.
Spec-Driven Workflow
A Spec-Driven workflow is recommended for collaborating with AI: break large requirements into small tasks and implement them step by step. The process is divided into four steps.
Step 1: Describe the Idea
Describe the feature you want to build or the problem you want to solve to the AI agent. The AI will help you break the idea into multiple small tasks, each with a clear description and acceptance criteria. Tasks should be small enough to be completed in a single conversation.
Example conversation:

I want to add user authentication to the project. Please break it into executable tasks, each with acceptance criteria.

Step 2: One Task at a Time, One Task per PR
Each agent session handles only one task. This constraint offers three benefits:

More focused context and better AI understanding.
Each task corresponds to an independent Pull Request, making code review easier.
If something fails, only a single task needs to be redone, without affecting a large amount of code.

Before starting a new task, have the AI read the current task details:
backlog task  --plain

Step 3: Write the Implementation Plan Before Coding
Before implementing code, have the AI study the current codebase, then write an Implementation Plan and write it into the task via CLI:
backlog task edit  --plan "1. Study existing code structure
2. Design interfaces
3. Implement core logic
4. Add tests"

The implementation plan ensures the proposal reflects the current state of the codebase and prevents AI from developing based on outdated assumptions. After writing the plan, it is recommended to confirm with team members before starting coding.
Step 4: Implement and Verify
The AI agent writes code according to the implementation plan. After completion, perform the following verification steps:

Review AI-generated code to confirm it follows project standards.
Run the test suite to ensure no existing functionality is broken.
Run lint checks to keep code style consistent.
Check acceptance criteria item by item to confirm they are all satisfied.
Update the task status to Done.

backlog task edit  --check-ac 1 --check-ac 2 --check-ac 3
backlog task edit  -s Done

Restart Loop When Unsatisfied
If the AI's implementation does not meet expectations, do not keep spinning in the same session. The correct approach is:

Clear the old plan, notes, and final summary in the task.
Refine the task description and acceptance criteria based on lessons learned.
Start a new AI session and rerun the entire process.

The restart loop avoids context pollution and lets the AI re-examine the requirement with a clearer perspective.
MCP Tool Capability List
After connecting via MCP, the AI agent can call 33 tools, categorized by domain as follows (required parameters are marked (required)).
Tasks (7)



Tool
Capability
Key Parameters




task_create
Create a new task
title (required), description, status, priority, assignee, labels, milestone, dependencies, acceptanceCriteria, parentTaskId, dueDate / plannedStart / plannedEnd


task_list
List tasks with multi-dimensional filtering
status / statusExcluded (single value or array), assignee / unassigned, milestone, labels, search, ready (only ready-to-start), completed (include completed corpus), offset / limit


task_search
Search by title/description
query, status, priority, modifiedFiles, completed, offset / limit


task_view
View task details
id (required)


task_edit
Edit metadata, plan/notes/comments, dependencies, acceptance criteria, task-level DoD
id (required), status, planSet / planAppend / planClear, notesSet / notesAppend / notesClear, commentsAppend, finalSummary, acceptanceCriteriaCheck / acceptanceCriteriaUncheck, definitionOfDoneAdd


task_archive
Archive a task (soft delete; frees ID and automatically cleans references)
id (required)


task_complete
Complete cleanup: move terminal-status task to completed/
id (required)



Documents (5)



Tool
Capability
Key Parameters




document_list
List documents, supports substring filtering
search, offset / limit


document_view
View document metadata and body
id (required)


document_create
Create a document (optional docs subdirectory path)
title, content (required), type, path, tags


document_update
Update content/title/metadata
id, content (required), title, appendContent, type, path, tags


document_search
Fuzzy search documents
query (required), offset / limit



Milestones (5)



Tool
Capability
Key Parameters




milestone_list
List milestone files and milestone values on tasks
offset / limit


milestone_add
Create a new milestone
name (required), description, actualStart / actualEnd, documentation


milestone_edit
Rename / change dates / change description
from, to (required), updateTasks, dueDate / plannedStart / plannedEnd


milestone_remove
Remove a milestone, optionally clean task references
name (required), taskHandling (clear / keep / reassign), reassignTo


milestone_archive
Archive a milestone
name (required)



Memos (5)



Tool
Capability
Key Parameters

List memos (newest first)
date, tags, offset / limit


memo_view
View full memo text

Create a memo

id (required), content / append, tags

Memo tools share the same ID scheme (YYYYMMDD-N) and file format with the CLI and Web. See Memos for details.
Decisions (2)



Tool
Capability
Key Parameters




decision_list
List decisions, supports status/keyword filtering
status (proposed / accepted / rejected / superseded), search, offset / limit

id (required), content / appendContent, status



Definition of Done (2)



Tool
Capability
Key Parameters




definition_of_done_defaults_get
Read project default DoD checklist
none

Replace project default DoD checklist (inherited by new tasks)
items (required, no commas)



Workflow (1)



Tool
Capability
Key Parameters




get_backlog_instructions
Get workflow guide (markdown); overview automatically renders the current project's full state machine at the end: state table, categories, transition edges, terminal-status table
instruction (overview / task-creation / task-execution / task-finalization / milestones / documents / decisions / drafts / memos / graph)



Graph (6)
Tools for querying the task relationship graph and managing user databases. Graph tools use a one-shot switch model: each call goes through the full open → query → close cycle (default derived graph reuses snapshots already written by the Web UI GraphService), without keeping a GraphService resident in the MCP process, so it does not rebuild the corpus at startup or slow down MCP server startup.



Tool
Capability
Key Parameters




graph_query
Execute read-only Cypher query against the specified graph database (write keywords such as CREATE/MERGE/SET/DELETE are rejected directly), readOnlyHint: true
db (required, default or user database name), statement


graph_schema
Output database schema: node tables and properties (name/type/primary key), relationship tables and endpoints
db (required)


graph_list_databases
List all available databases (default derived graph + user databases) with name, kind, node/edge counts
none


graph_describe_database
Return description, timestamp, and per-table row/edge counts for a single database
db (required)


graph_create_database
Create a user graph database (write operation, destructiveHint: true; no content is written without confirmation)
name, description, acknowledged: true (all required)


graph_import_csv
Import CSV into a user database: by default imports as nodes (missing tables created with inferred types, primary-key idempotent updates); add rel/from/to to switch to relationship import (endpoints matched but not created); files are validated as a whole before opening the database, destructiveHint: true
db, csv (required), node / map / header / rel / from / to



The accompanying graph guide volume (backlog instructions graph / backlog://workflow/graph) covers parameters for the six tools and Cypher / CSV usage.
List Paging
All MCP list tools uniformly support offset + limit paging, returning structured results through a unified envelope:
{ "items": [], "total": 128, "offset": 0, "limit": 50, "hasMore": true }


task_list, task_search, document_search, document_list, milestone_list, memo_list, and decision_list all follow this envelope; text output additionally appends a CLI-style Showing X-Y of N items hint.
hasMore / total let the agent determine whether the list is complete and loop through pages accordingly—no more silent truncation.
task_list pages by the ordered sequence of status buckets and then re-renders by bucket; bucket order is unchanged. The unconfigured / archived diagnostic sections of milestone_list are excluded from paging, ensuring warnings are not lost.

MCP Resources and Prompts
The Backlog.md MCP server registers the following workflow resources with the client; AI agents can actively read them during a session:



Resource URI
Content Description




backlog://workflow/overview
Workflow overview: when to create tasks and basic flow; get_backlog_instructions returns this volume by default.


backlog://workflow/task-creation
Task creation guide: how to search, scope, and create tasks.


backlog://workflow/task-execution
Task execution guide: how to plan, update, and advance tasks.


backlog://workflow/task-finalization
Task finalization guide: how to verify, summarize, and complete work.


backlog://workflow/milestones
Milestone guide: create, edit, remove, and archive milestones.


backlog://workflow/documents
Document management guide: create, update, list, and view project documents.


backlog://workflow/decisions
Decision guide: create and list decisions, including output modes and status handling.


backlog://workflow/drafts
Draft guide: create, promote, demote, and archive drafts.


backlog://workflow/memos
Memo guide: create, list, view, update, and delete quick memos.


backlog://workflow/graph
Graph guide: parameters for the six graph MCP tools, Cypher queries, and CSV import usage.


backlog://init-required
Fallback resource for uninitialized projects: how to initialize Backlog.md in this directory.



AI agents read backlog://workflow/overview first when connecting or encountering uncertain scenarios to get contextual guidance. The CLI-side backlog instructions  corresponds one-to-one with the above volumes; see Agent Instruction Files.
Security Features
Backlog.md's MCP implementation is secure by design:

stdio-only transport: AI clients and the MCP server communicate only through standard input/output, do not listen on any network port, and cannot be accessed externally.
localhost-only runtime validation: Web UI and other services bind to local addresses by default.
Pure protocol wrapper: the MCP layer contains no business logic; all operations are ultimately handled by the Core layer, sharing the same data validation rules as the CLI and Web UI.
Roots discovery mechanism: the MCP client sends a list of workspace root directories, and Backlog.md automatically looks for valid projects in those directories. The normal startup path also follows changes in client workspace roots; when none is found, it falls back to a minimal-functionality mode exposing only init-related tools.
Fixed project root: to lock to a fixed directory (for example global ~/.backlog), start with --cwd or the BACKLOG_CWD environment variable; the server will then not follow client workspace roots.

Frequently Asked Questions
Codex cannot connect to the Backlog.md MCP server

Symptom: Codex reports MCP server startup failure or timeout.
Common cause: the local backlog command resolves to a stale/corrupted dist/backlog binary.
Solution:
Rebuild the project (bun run build).
Use the current Codex command format: codex mcp add backlog -- backlog mcp start.
Test backlog mcp start separately to confirm it starts normally.



Shared MCP server writes to the wrong project

Symptom: in user-level or shared-server scenarios, tasks created by AI appear in the wrong directory.
Cause: older server versions parsed the project root only once at startup.
Solution: upgrade to the latest version; to fix the directory, use backlog mcp start --cwd .

50-AI集成/01-支持的AI工具.html.title: Supported AI Tools
50-AI集成/01-支持的AI工具.html.body:
Supported AI Tools
Backlog.md supports integration with a variety of mainstream AI coding assistants. Connection methods vary slightly by tool, but the core principle is the same: register Backlog.md's MCP server with the AI client so it can directly invoke Backlog.md tools.
Supported Tools Overview



Tool
Integration Method
Configuration Command




Claude Code
MCP
claude mcp add backlog --scope user -- backlog mcp start


OpenAI Codex
MCP
codex mcp add backlog -- backlog mcp start


Google Gemini CLI
MCP
gemini mcp add backlog -s user backlog mcp start


Kiro
MCP
kiro-cli mcp add --scope global --name backlog --command backlog --args mcp,start


Cursor
MCP
Manual mcpServers configuration


GitHub Copilot
CLI instructions
Generate copilot-instructions.md



Claude Code
Claude Code is Anthropic's command-line AI assistant with native MCP support.
Run the following command to register:
claude mcp add backlog --scope user -- backlog mcp start

Parameter description:

--scope user: writes the configuration at user level, available to all projects.
backlog mcp start after --: the command to start the Backlog.md MCP server.

After successful registration, type @backlog in a Claude Code session to invoke Backlog.md tools.
OpenAI Codex
OpenAI Codex CLI also supports the MCP protocol.
Run the following command:
codex mcp add backlog -- backlog mcp start


Note that Codex uses -- as the stdio command separator. This format has been updated to match current Codex CLI behavior.

Codex automatically includes the Backlog.md toolset in its available tools list. During conversations, Codex autonomously decides when to call Backlog.md tools based on context.
Google Gemini CLI
Gemini CLI provides MCP support through the gemini command.
Run the following command:
gemini mcp add backlog -s user backlog mcp start

Parameter description:

-s user: equivalent to --scope user, applies at user scope.
backlog mcp start: startup command.

Kiro
Kiro CLI's configuration is slightly different and requires explicitly specifying how to split arguments.
Run the following command:
kiro-cli mcp add --scope global --name backlog --command backlog --args mcp,start

Note that arguments after --args are comma-separated, not space-separated.
Cursor
Cursor supports two ways to integrate with Backlog.md.
Method 1: MCP Configuration
Open Cursor settings, find the MCP configuration entry, and manually add the mcpServers configuration:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "backlog": {
      "command": "backlog",
      "args": ["mcp", "start"]
    }
  }
}

After saving, Cursor's AI assistant can use the full set of Backlog.md tools.
Method 2: CLI Instruction File (AGENTS.md)
Cursor also reads the project root AGENTS.md as a general agent instruction. When running backlog init or backlog agents --update-instructions, the Cursor-specific instruction is written into AGENTS.md; a separate .cursorrules file is no longer generated. On repeated runs, the existing AGENTS.md content is preserved, and Backlog.md only updates its marked block.
GitHub Copilot
GitHub Copilot currently does not support the MCP protocol, so it is integrated via CLI instructions.
Run the following command to generate the agent instruction file:
backlog agents --update-instructions

This command generates .github/copilot-instructions.md in the project root, containing:

Complete Backlog.md CLI command reference
Task creation conventions
Acceptance criteria format
Workflow guide

Copilot reads this file when generating code to understand the project's task-management conventions and assist development better.
Verifying Integration
After configuration, verify integration as follows:

Start the corresponding AI client.
Enter a prompt such as "List my pending tasks".
Observe whether the AI correctly calls Backlog.md's list_tasks tool.
If the AI returns the current project's task list, integration is successful.

If integration fails, check:

Whether the backlog command is in the system PATH.
Whether backlog mcp start can start normally (test separately in a terminal).
Whether the AI client's MCP configuration correctly points to backlog mcp start.
If using Codex, confirm the command includes the -- separator.
If the AI starts a compiled binary rather than source code, ensure dist/backlog has been rebuilt.

50-AI集成/02-代理指令文件.html.title: Agent Instruction Files
50-AI集成/02-代理指令文件.html.body:
Agent Instruction Files
Agent instruction files are standardized guide documents Backlog.md prepares for AI coding assistants. They tell AI how to work with Backlog.md, including workflow conventions, command usage, and task-management standards. Through unified instruction files, different AI tools maintain a consistent understanding of the project and avoid workflow drift caused by tool switching.
What Are Instruction Files
AI coding assistants read specific Markdown files in the project as context when starting. Backlog.md leverages this mechanism to generate instruction files containing project-management conventions. These files cover:

An introduction to Backlog.md's core capabilities
Task file structure explanation
Complete CLI command reference
Acceptance criteria and Definition of Done (DoD) conventions
Typical workflow examples
Common mistakes vs. correct practices

After reading these files, AI can accurately use Backlog.md features in conversations without users repeatedly explaining project conventions.
Generating Instruction Files
Backlog.md provides two ways to generate or update agent instruction files.
Auto-Generated During Project Initialization
When running backlog init to initialize a new project, the wizard asks whether to install AI agent instructions:
backlog init my-project
# The interactive wizard shows the option:
# "Install AI agent instructions?"

After choosing to install, Backlog.md generates the corresponding instruction files based on your choices.
Manually Updating Instructions for Existing Projects
For existing projects, you can update or regenerate instruction files at any time with:
backlog agents --update-instructions

This command scans the current project and regenerates all instruction files based on the current configuration, ensuring the content stays in sync with the project's current state. After modifying task status flows, label systems, or other project conventions, it is recommended to run this command to update AI instructions.
Generated File List
Depending on the AI tools you use, Backlog.md generates one or more of the following files:



File Path
Applicable Tools
Scope




CLAUDE.md
Claude Code / Claude Desktop
Project root


AGENTS.md
Generic agent instructions, Cursor
Project root


GEMINI.md
Gemini CLI
Project root


.github/copilot-instructions.md
GitHub Copilot
Project repository




Note: Cursor no longer generates a separate .cursorrules file owned by Backlog; it uses AGENTS.md uniformly. Repeated generation commands preserve existing user content in AGENTS.md and only update Backlog-managed marked blocks.
Instruction files do not contain a copy of the project state machine (as of v1.53.9): the state machine uses config.yml as the single source of truth, and backlog instructions overview renders it on the fly based on the current configuration. Old state-machine blocks written into AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md by earlier versions are removed during the next backlog init or backlog agents --update-instructions.

CLAUDE.md
Designed specifically for Claude Code and Claude Desktop. Claude tools automatically read CLAUDE.md in the project root as part of the system prompt. This file contains the complete Backlog.md operation guide and is the most comprehensive instruction file.
AGENTS.md
A generic agent instruction file for Cursor and AI tools that do not recognize brand-specific files. The content is basically the same as CLAUDE.md but uses more generic phrasing. Cursor reads AGENTS.md in the project root as a generic agent instruction; some IDE plugins or custom AI clients also prefer AGENTS.md.
GEMINI.md
An instruction file optimized for Google Gemini CLI. Gemini CLI recognizes GEMINI.md in the project root and includes it in context.
.github/copilot-instructions.md
