The onStatusChange command is executed via sh -c in the project root, with task information injected through environment variables: $TASK_ID (task ID), $OLD_STATUS (old status), $NEW_STATUS (new status), $TASK_TITLE (title), referenced in the command string as $TASK_ID, etc. Callback failure only prints an error log and does not block the status change. A task's individual onStatusChange frontmatter field takes precedence over the global config. This key is not in the config get/set available-keys list; edit config.yml directly to set it.
When autoCommit is enabled, Backlog.md automatically runs git commit each time a task is created or modified via CLI, saving the step of manual commit. Combined with bypassGitHooks, this improves efficiency when pre-commit hooks are slow.
autoCommit only commits files actually touched by each write (new files, replaced old paths, source and destination paths of moves/archives), and does not git add the entire backlog/ directory or clear your existing staged/unstaged changes. This ensures auto-commits do not interfere with other changes in your current workspace.
filesystemOnly is suitable for pure-filesystem projects or environments without Git; enabling it disables all Git-related features.
ID and Prefixes



Item
Type
Default
Description




prefixes.task
string
task
Task ID prefix


prefixes.draft
string
draft
Draft ID prefix


zeroPaddedIds
integer
—
ID zero-padding width, e.g., 3 generates task-001



Prefix configuration allows customizing task and draft ID formats. For example, after setting prefixes.task to back, new task IDs become back-1, back-2, etc.
Reserved prefixes: task prefixes may only contain letters and cannot use the reserved names doc and decision (used by documents and decisions respectively). This rule is enforced consistently across all entry points—the init --task-prefix flag, interactive wizard, and browser initialization page all reject them. backlog doctor reports prefix conflicts in existing projects, and refuses to run --fix while conflicts remain (to avoid assigning new numbers into conflicting storage during duplicate-ID repair). Existing projects already using reserved prefixes continue to work normally; re-initialization does not actively rewrite them.
zeroPaddedIds controls the formatted width of IDs. When set to 3, IDs display as task-001; when set to 4, they display as task-0001. This helps maintain lexicographic consistency in filenames.
Web UI



Item
Type
Default
Description




defaultPort
integer
6420
Web UI default listening port


autoPort
boolean
true
Automatically scan the next 100 user ports when the default port is occupied


autoOpenBrowser
boolean
true
Whether to automatically open the browser when starting the Web UI


hideEmptyColumns
boolean
false
Whether the board hides status columns with no tasks



Modify defaultPort to avoid conflicts with other local services. When autoPort is enabled (default), if the default port is occupied the server automatically uses the next available port and prints the actual address in the terminal; it only accepts ports within the user port range (1024–65535) that it scans itself, and refuses random high ports assigned by the OS. When autoPort is disabled, a port conflict produces an EADDRINUSE error directly. This toggle is also available in the Web interface "Settings" panel. Disabling autoOpenBrowser means running backlog browser only starts the server and does not pop up a browser window, suitable for remote development or server environments.
hideEmptyColumns (corresponding to hide_empty_columns in config.yml) hides status columns that currently have no tasks, reducing visual clutter; all status columns remain visible while dragging a task so it can be dropped. It can also be toggled next to the Auto Open Browser switch in the Web interface "Settings" panel.
MCP HTTP Transport
The mcp.http.* keys (mcp.http.host / mcp.http.port / mcp.http.auth.*) are currently reserved configuration only: the current MCP implementation only supports stdio transport (backlog mcp start), does not listen on any network port, and has no consumer logic for HTTP transport. Configuring these keys has no effect; continue using the stdio approach. See MCP Workflow for details.
Configuration Storage Location
Backlog.md looks for configuration files in the following priority order:

backlog/config.yml
backlog.config.yml (project root)

backlog/config.yml is recommended so configuration is stored centrally with tasks, documents, and other project data, making backup and migration easier. When using backlog.config.yml, you can specify the relative path to the backlog folder via the backlogDirectory item (such as .backlog).

Custom backlog directory fully effective: memo storage and graph scanning/watching previously hard-coded the directory name as backlog, causing read/write/watch errors and empty graphs in projects with custom directories such as .backlog. This is now resolved by uniformly parsing the configured directory. If you previously used memos in a custom-directory project, old data is still under your backlog-dir/memos and is now correctly recognized; if an empty backlog/memos was mistakenly created at the root, you can delete it manually. Re-running backlog init will also create missing directories such as memos/, docs/, etc.

Example YAML configuration file:
projectName: "My Project"
statuses:
  - Backlog
  - To Do
  - In Progress
  - Done
labels:
  - bug
  - feature
  - docs
dateFormat: "YYYY-MM-DD"
checkActiveBranches: true
include_cross_branch: false
remoteOperations: true
activeBranchDays: 30
autoCommit: false
bypassGitHooks: false
prefixes:
  task: "back"
  draft: "draft"
defaultAssignee:
  - "@alice"
defaultEditor: "vim"
defaultPort: 6420
autoPort: true
autoOpenBrowser: true
hide_empty_columns: false


Block YAML lists: list-type configurations (statuses, labels) support both the block sequence syntax shown above and inline syntax (statuses: ["To Do", "In Progress", "Done"]). The system parses block lists according to standard YAML semantics first, while remaining compatible with the legacy inline bracket format.

After modifying the configuration file, Backlog.md automatically loads the latest settings without restarting the service.

60-配置与运维/01-Shell补全.html.title: Shell Completions
60-配置与运维/01-Shell补全.html.body:
Shell Completions
Backlog.md includes intelligent shell completion for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell. After enabling, press Tab while typing a backlog command in the terminal to auto-complete subcommands, options, and dynamic values, greatly improving efficiency.
One-Click Completion Script Installation
Backlog.md provides automatic detection and installation based on the current shell type:
backlog completion install

After running, the tool detects your shell environment and installs the completion script to the corresponding location:



Shell
Installation Location




bash
~/.bashrc or ~/.bash_profile


zsh
~/.zshrc


fish
~/.config/fish/completions/


PowerShell
$PROFILE file



After installation, reload the shell configuration file or open a new terminal window for completions to take effect.
Supported Shells
Bash
The Bash completion script supports command, subcommand, and option completion. Dynamic value completion depends on the bash-completion package. It is preinstalled on most Linux distributions; if not, install it via the package manager:
# Debian/Ubuntu
sudo apt-get install bash-completion

# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install bash-completion

Zsh
Zsh users can use completions directly with no extra dependencies. Zsh's completion system is feature-rich, supporting menu selection and description display, providing the most complete experience.
Fish
Fish completion scripts are placed at ~/.config/fish/completions/backlog.fish; Fish automatically loads all completion definitions in that directory. Fish completions support description text and argument highlighting.
PowerShell
PowerShell completion is implemented by registering Register-ArgumentCompleter. The installation script automatically modifies the PowerShell configuration file (view the path via $PROFILE). To register manually, refer to the registration logic in the completion script.
Dynamic Completion Capabilities
Backlog.md's completion system supports not only static commands and options, but also dynamically extracts real data from the current project:
Actual Task IDs
After typing backlog task edit, press Tab to list all valid task IDs in the current project:
backlog task edit 
# shows: task-1  task-2  task-3  doc-1  ...

Status Values
After typing -s or --status, press Tab; the completion system reads the status list from the project config:
backlog task list -s 
# shows: To Do  In Progress  Done

Labels
After typing -l or --labels, press Tab; the completion system aggregates all labels already in use:
backlog task create "New feature" -l 
# shows: bug  feature  docs  backend

Assignees
After typing -a or --assignee, press Tab; the completion system lists all assignees that appear in existing tasks:
backlog task edit 1 -a 
# shows: @alice  @bob  @team-lead

Dynamic completion data comes from the Backlog.md project in the current working directory. If you run a command in a directory without a Backlog.md project, dynamic value completion falls back to an empty list or default values, but static command completion remains available.
Manual Completion Script Installation
If automatic installation encounters issues, or you need to deploy completion scripts to a non-standard location, you can install manually. Backlog.md ships with completion script sources for each shell in the package.
Finding Completion Scripts
Completion scripts are installed with the npm package, in the completions/ folder of the package directory:
# Find the globally installed backlog.md package path
npm root -g
# Completion scripts are at:
# /backlog.md/completions/backlog.bash
# /backlog.md/completions/backlog.zsh
# /backlog.md/completions/backlog.fish
# /backlog.md/completions/backlog.ps1

Manual Bash Installation
Add the following to ~/.bashrc:
source /path/to/backlog.bash

Manual Zsh Installation
Copy the completion script to a Zsh function search path, such as ~/.zsh/functions/:
cp /path/to/backlog.zsh ~/.zsh/functions/_backlog

Ensure ~/.zshrc includes that directory in fpath:
fpath=(~/.zsh/functions $fpath)

Manual Fish Installation
Copy the completion script to Fish's completions directory:
cp /path/to/backlog.fish ~/.config/fish/completions/backlog.fish

Manual PowerShell Installation
Add the completion registration code to the PowerShell profile. First determine the profile path:
$PROFILE

If the file does not exist, create it:
New-Item -Path $PROFILE -ItemType File -Force

Then append the contents of backlog.ps1 to the profile.
After manual installation, reload the shell configuration file or open a new terminal window for completions to take effect.

60-配置与运维/02-项目概览.html.title: Project Overview
60-配置与运维/02-项目概览.html.body:
Project Overview
The backlog overview command provides project-level task statistics as plain text, suitable for quickly checking project status in the terminal or for use in scripts and CI pipelines.
Launching Overview
Interactive TUI
Run directly in a TTY-capable terminal:
backlog overview

The system outputs an ANSI-colored terminal interface containing status distribution, priority distribution, recent activity, and project health. Use the terminal's native scrollbar or mouse wheel to browse all content.
Plain-Text Output
Use --plain mode in non-interactive environments or when piping:
backlog overview --plain

Plain-text mode does not output ANSI color codes, making it suitable for redirecting to files or piping to other commands:
backlog overview --plain > project-status.txt
backlog overview --plain | grep "Overdue"

Output Content
The overview command output includes the following dimensions:
Status Overview
Status Overview
===============
  To Do: 12 tasks (40%)
  In Progress: 8 tasks (27%)
  Done: 10 tasks (33%)

  Total Tasks: 30
  Completion: 33%
Shows task counts and percentages per status, plus total task count and overall completion rate.
Priority Breakdown
Priority Breakdown
==================
  high     5  17%
  medium   15 50%
  low      7  23%
  none     3  10%
Statistics by high / medium / low / no priority.
Recent Activity
Recent Activity
===============
Recently Created
----------------
  TASK-32 - Add user authentication module

Recently Updated
----------------
  TASK-28 - Optimize database queries
Lists tasks created and updated in the last 7 days.
Project Health
Project Health
==============
  Average Task Age: 12 days
  At Risk: 2   Overdue: 1   Stale: 3   Blocked: 1

At Risk Tasks: (due soon, require immediate attention)
------------------------------------------------------
  TASK-15 - Complete API docs

Overdue Tasks: (passed the due date)
------------------------------------
  TASK-7 - Fix login timeout

Stale Tasks: (No updates for 30+ days, no due date set)
--------------------------------------------------------
  TASK-3 - Research third-party libraries

Blocked Tasks: (waiting on dependencies)
----------------------------------------
  TASK-11 - Integrate payment gateway
The health section aligns with the Web statistics page and shows:

Average task age: average number of days all tasks have existed
Average task duration: average completion time in minutes and sample size for tasks in canonical terminal statuses. The span definition is fully consistent with Gantt chart Actual Start / Actual End; completion only counts canonical terminal statuses—Done is included in the sample, abandoned terminal statuses such as Dropped do not count as completed. Duration distribution is strongly right-skewed, so sample size is also shown
At Risk: tasks due today or tomorrow
Overdue: tasks past the due date
Stale: tasks without a due date and not updated for more than 30 days
Blocked: tasks with uncompleted dependencies

Specific task IDs and titles are listed under each category.
Statistics Corpus Scope
overview counts only active tasks by default (non-empty status under backlog/tasks/). Consistent with the "Completed corpus" toggle on the Web statistics page, add --completed to include historical completed records (backlog/completed/) in the sample—metrics such as average task duration switch corpus accordingly:
backlog overview --plain --completed


Pure-date due dates are parsed and displayed as the local-time-zone day: in any time zone, dueDate: 2026-09-20 is shown as September 20 and will not shift to the previous or next day due to UTC conversion. Created/updated timestamps with time are still stored as UTC and displayed in local time.

Relationship to the Web Statistics Page



Feature
CLI overview
Web Statistics Page




Interactivity
Terminal TUI / plain text
Browser interactive interface


Color
ANSI color / no color
Web color theme


Health cards
Plain-text lists
Clickable cards with date labels


Use case
Quick terminal check, CI, scripts
Detailed analysis, daily monitoring



Both use the same underlying statistics logic (src/core/statistics.ts), so the data is fully consistent.

60-配置与运维/03-故障排查.html.title: Troubleshooting
60-配置与运维/03-故障排查.html.body:
Troubleshooting
This page aggregates common failures when using Backlog.md. Each section is organized as "Symptom → Cause → Remedy". Detailed explanations for each feature remain on their original pages; this page only serves as a troubleshooting index and remedy guide.
Web Port Occupied
Symptom: port unavailable when starting backlog browser, or the address does not open.
Cause: default port 6420 is already used by another process.
Remedy:

By default autoPort: true; when the port is occupied, the server automatically scans for the next available port and prints the real address in the terminal (such as http://localhost:6421). Copy the console output; this is not a failure.
If autoPort is disabled, an occupied port raises an EADDRINUSE error—explicitly specify a port with backlog browser --port 8080.
Automatic scanning only accepts ports within the user port range (1024–65535) and refuses random high ports assigned by the OS.

See Startup & Access and the Web UI section of Configuration Management.
Graph Stuck Building / Lock Conflict
Symptom: graph page shows loading for a long time, /api/graph keeps returning building; or a lock conflict is reported on startup.
Cause: a graph slot lock can only be held by one process at a time. When the holder process has exited, the lock is automatically reclaimed and will not get stuck building; stuck building usually means the holder process is still alive (for example another browser session or a residual backlog browser process).
Remedy:

If the holder process has exited, no action is needed; the lock is reclaimed and rebuilt automatically.
If the holder is still alive, the interactive terminal asks whether to take over the lock—confirm only after ensuring the old process no longer needs the graph.
Two browser sessions each hold independent databases (partitioned by project path hash) and do not contend; when troubleshooting, confirm whether multiple service processes were started for the same project.
The cache directory can be overridden with the environment variable BACKLOG_GRAPH_CACHE_DIR; BACKLOG_GRAPH_BACKEND=kuzu is no longer a valid value (native dependency removed); the only valid override is memory.
When Cypher search is unavailable (graph page finds nothing, backlog graph query errors), first check the terminal for the warning [graph] RyuGraph (WASM) backend init failed for , falling back to memory: if present, the backend has degraded to memory (no Cypher). Distinguish "path not visible to WASM" (fixed in v1.53.9) from "engine error" (needs reporting) based on the reason at the end of the warning.

Watch / File Changes Not Refreshing
Symptom: TUI board, Web interface, or task list --json --watch does not reflect recent changes.
Cause and Remedy:

TUI board: uses Bun.watch to listen to the tasks directory. It is resilient to atomic writes (waits for the file to stabilize before refreshing), but confirm you modified the backlog/ directory of the current project—instances started with --cwd / BACKLOG_CWD only watch their own resolved project.
--json --watch: notifications are advisory; a 1-second reconcile tick uses file stat signatures as a fallback to repair missed events; if the signature has not changed, output is not repeated. Confirm the listening process's upstream program is still alive (it stops when the launcher exits).
Web interface: refreshes via WebSocket broadcasts. If the whole page does not refresh, first confirm the WebSocket connection is normal in the browser console; writes from CLI / TUI / MCP all trigger notifications.

macOS Illegal Hardware Instruction / Architecture Mismatch
Symptom (M-series Mac): running backlog reports illegal hardware instruction or Binary package not installed for darwin-....
Cause: Node, Bun, or Homebrew is running under Rosetta (x64 emulation), but an Intel binary incompatible with the native CPU architecture is installed.
Remedy: first check the architecture reported by each tool:
uname -m                            # arm64 = Apple Silicon hardware; x86_64 = Intel or Rosetta shell
node -p process.arch                # Node/Bun runtime architecture
sysctl -in sysctl.proc_translated   # 1 = current shell is running under Rosetta
which brew                          # /opt/homebrew = arm64 brew, /usr/local = Intel brew

If architectures are inconsistent, reinstall with the native architecture:
brew reinstall backlog-md                    # upstream formula; first confirm `which brew` outputs /opt/homebrew
arch -arm64 npm i -g @kuwork/backlog.md
arch -arm64 bun add -g @kuwork/backlog.md

Deliberately running x64 Node under Rosetta also works: the launcher falls back to whichever backlog.md-darwin-* package is actually installed. See Installation & Initialization for details.
Watch Process Spinning at High CPU (Older Versions)
Symptom: backlog task list --json --watch continuously consumes high CPU even when nothing is happening (about 35–42% in large repositories).
Cause: older versions' 1-second reconcile tick unconditionally repeated full task-list reads; cost grows with repository size.
Remedy: upgrade to the latest version—when idle, it only performs a cheap stat-signature comparison per second, reducing CPU to below 1%, with unchanged output and latency. Browser and TUI watchers do not use this polling and are unaffected.
MCP Connection Issues
Symptom: AI client reports MCP server startup failure, timeout, or tasks being written to the wrong project.
Remedy: see the "Frequently Asked Questions" section of MCP Workflow:

Startup failure / timeout: usually the local backlog command resolves to a stale binary—rebuild, register with the codex mcp add backlog -- backlog mcp start format, and test backlog mcp start separately.
Writing to the wrong project: upgrade to the latest version (server follows client workspace roots), or use backlog mcp start --cwd  to lock the directory.

Pressing E to Open Editor Freezes
Symptom: in TUI / Web, pressing E to open the editor hangs or the editor does not start.
Cause and Remedy: common with the default editor code --wait, which can hang unattended agent processes, or editor paths containing arguments failing to parse.

Clear the default editor: backlog config set defaultEditor ""
Or override per command with the EDITOR environment variable: EDITOR=nvim backlog board
If the editor path contains arguments, write the full executable path or use a wrapper script; set TERM=xterm-256color for color issues.

See the "Editor resolution priority" section of Configuration Management.
